- `envelopeCurve` (function): `n` gains, one per sample at `rate`, for `env` at volume `vol`.
- `FALL_FLOOR` (const): Where the source's exponential fall ends, as a gain: Web Audio cannot ramp exponentially to 0.
- `FallEnvelope` (interface): The source's percussive envelope: a linear attack to full volume, then an exponential fall to `FALL_FLOOR`.
- `holdEnvelope` (function): The source's `hold`: an ADSR sustaining full volume, with a 30 ms release (shorter when the attack leaves less).

### [`engine/audio/dsp/measure.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/measure.ts)

- `dcOffset` (function): The mean of `[from, to)`: the DC offset.
- `peak` (function): The largest absolute sample in `[from, to)`.
- `rms` (function): The root mean square of `[from, to)`.
- `toneAmplitude` (function): The amplitude of the sinusoid at `freq` Hz in `[from, to)` at `rate` samples per second (Goertzel, Hann window).

### [`engine/audio/dsp/osc.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/osc.ts)

- `blamp` (function): The PolyBLAMP residual of a unit rise in slope (per sample) at phase 0, the integral of `blep`.
- `blep` (function): The PolyBLEP residual of a rising unit step at phase 0: what a band-limited step adds to a naive one, for a sample at phase `x` in [0, 1) (just after the step when `x < dt`, just before it when `x > 1 - dt`).
- `DUTY` (const): The duty cycle of each pulse-like wave: the share of a period spent high.
- `oscillate` (function): One sample of `wave` at `phase` (in [0, 1)), band-limited for a phase step of `dt` per sample (|frequency| / rate; clamped to 0.5).
- `TONAL_WAVES` (const): The tonal waves: square, pulse (25% duty), pulse12 (12.5% duty), triangle, sine and saw.
- `TonalWave` (type): One of the tonal waves.
- `wrap` (function): `x` wrapped into [0, 1).

### [`engine/audio/dsp/pluck.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/pluck.ts)

- `Pluck` (class): A plucked string: `next()` gives one sample at a time.

### [`engine/audio/dsp/render.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/render.ts)

- `DEFAULT_RATE` (const): The sample rate `render` uses when none is given.
- `render` (function): The sound `def` as mono samples at `rate` per second, its random draws seeded by `seed`: the same bits in Node and Chromium (see the file comment for the contract).
- `RENDER_CODES` (const): The codes `render` raises beyond a definition's own (engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts), with their fixes.
- `soundHash` (function): The 64-bit FNV-1a hex digest of `samples` (engine/core/hash.ts's `hashNumbers`): one golden per sound.

### [`engine/audio/dsp/synth.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/synth.ts)

- `renderVoice` (function): Renders `voice` and adds it into `out` at its start; `streams` gives its noise.
- `voiceEnd` (function): Where the voice ends in the sound, in samples, its echo included.
- `voiceSamples` (function): The voice's length in samples, without its echo.

### [`engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts`](../engine/audio/dsp/voice.ts)

- `DelaySpec` (interface): A feedback echo after the voice.
- `FilterSpec` (interface): A filter with its own settings.
- `FmSpec` (interface): Simple two-operator FM: a sine modulator at `ratio` times the pitch modulates the voice's phase.
- `MAX_SECONDS` (const): The longest a sound may last, in seconds.
- `normalizeSound` (function): A definition checked and filled: one normal voice per voice, at `rate` samples per second.
- `NormalVoice` (interface): A checked voice with every default filled, as engine/audio/dsp/synth.ts renders it.
- `noteFreq` (function): A frequency in Hz from a pitch: numbers pass through, `noteFreq('A4')` is 440 (equal temperament).
- `Pitch` (type): A pitch: a frequency in Hz, or a note name such as `'A4'`, `'C#5'` or `'Bb2'`.
- `PluckSpec` (interface): The Karplus–Strong string's settings.
- `SoundDef` (type): A sound: one voice, or several played together.
- `Voice` (interface): One voice of a sound: every field is optional.
- `VOICE_CODES` (const): The codes a definition's checks raise, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `Wave` (type): One of the waves.
- `WAVES` (const): Every wave: the tonal ones, white noise, and a Karplus–Strong pluck.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/audio.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/audio.ts)

- `Audio` (interface): A page's sound (see the file comment).
- `AUDIO_CODES` (const): The runtime's codes, with their fixes.
- `AudioInfo` (interface): What `info()` reports: plain data.
- `AudioOptions` (interface): How `createAudio` is set up; in a page every field has its default.
- `AudioState` (type): The runtime's state: `locked` until a gesture, then the context's; `off` without Web Audio.
- `createAudio` (function): Makes a page's sound (see the file comment).

### [`engine/audio/runtime/buffers.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/buffers.ts)

- `foldLoop` (function): `samples` (one pass of `pass` samples, then tails) folded onto one pass: what every pass sounds like looped.
- `loopLayout` (function): `samples` (one pass of `pass` samples, then tails) as the head pass followed by the folded loop pass.
- `passSamples` (function): The samples of one pass of `song` at `rate`.
- `renderLayers` (function): Each layer of `song` rendered at `rate`, laid out to loop when the song loops (else as rendered).
- `SongLayer` (interface): One intensity layer of a song.
- `songLayers` (function): The layers of `song`, by ascending intensity (see the file comment).
- `toBuffer` (function): `samples` as a one-channel `AudioBuffer` of `context` at `rate`.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/gesture.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/gesture.ts)

- `GESTURE_EVENTS` (const): The events that may be gestures, as `addEventListener` names them.
- `GestureEvent` (interface): What `isGesture` reads of an event.
- `GestureTarget` (type): Where gestures arrive: `window`, or any `EventTarget`.
- `isGesture` (function): Whether `event` lets a page start sound: a trusted key other than Escape, click or pointer release.
- `onGesture` (function): Calls `listener` on every gesture at `target` (capture phase); returns the function that stops listening.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/mixer.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/mixer.ts)

- `AudioBus` (type): One of the buses.
- `BUS_VOLUMES` (const): The starting volumes, the master's included.
- `BUSES` (const): The mixer's buses.
- `createMixer` (function): Makes the mixer's graph on `context`, into its destination.
- `DUCK` (const): How ducking sounds: the level the ducked buses fall to, and how fast, s.
- `Mixer` (interface): The mixer of a context.
- `MixerInfo` (interface): What `info()` reports.
- `ROOM_FADE` (const): Seconds a room change takes to fade from the old reverb to the new.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/music.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/music.ts)

- `createMusic` (function): Makes the music player of `context`, playing into `output` (the mixer's `music` bus).
- `LAYER_FADE` (const): How long a layer takes to fade in or out, s.
- `Music` (interface): The music of one context.
- `MUSIC_LEAD` (const): How far ahead of `currentTime` a change is scheduled at the earliest, s.
- `MusicChange` (interface): When and how a change happens.
- `MusicOptions` (interface): What the player needs beyond its context and output.
- `MusicPosition` (interface): Where the music is.
- `nextLine` (function): The first line of a grid of `period` seconds from `start` at or after `time`.
- `Quantize` (type): Where a change lands: the next bar line, the next beat, or at once.
- `SECTION_FADE` (const): How long the old song fades out at a section change, s.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/reverb.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/reverb.ts)

- `ABSORPTION` (const): The share of a sound a surface soaks up (its absorption coefficient), at the mids (500 Hz to 1 kHz) and the highs (4 kHz), by a footstep's tag (engine/world/footsteps.ts); `'*'` for any other.
- `CONTENTS` (const): How much a furnished room's contents soak up at the mids, as a share of its floor's area; the highs 1.4 times it.
- `impulseResponse` (function): The room's stereo impulse response at `rate` samples per second, or null when it has no reverb.
- `REVERB_CODES` (const): The codes the rooms raise, with their fixes.
- `roomAcoustics` (function): A room's reverb from what it is made of (see the file comment): a `RoomSpec`.
- `RoomMake` (interface): What `roomAcoustics` hears a room as: its floor's area (m²), its height (m) and its surfaces' tags.
- `RoomName` (type): A preset's name.
- `roomReverb` (function): The preset for a level's room (WP 13.15: rooms as data for sound): by its volume, its `area` (m², the room descriptor's) times `height` (m, its storey's clear height): `small` under 30 m³, `room` under 200 m³, `hall` past.
- `ROOMS` (const): The room presets, from no reverb to a cave.
- `roomSpec` (function): The numbers of `room`, a preset's name or a spec; throws `AUDIO_BAD_ROOM` for an unknown name or a bad value.
- `RoomSpec` (interface): A room's reverb, as numbers.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/sound.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/sound.ts)

- `checkPlay` (function): Checks `options` for an effect with `variants` variants; throws `AUDIO_BAD_OPTION` naming the first bad one.
- `createVoice` (function): Wires and starts one voice (see the file comment).
- `PlayOptions` (interface): How `play` plays one effect.
- `RuntimeSound` (interface): A sound as the runtime holds it: it can be occluded.
- `Sound` (interface): A sound playing.
- `SOUND_CODES` (const): The codes of a sound's options, with their fixes.
- `STOP_FADE` (const): Seconds a sound fades out over when it is stopped or makes room for another.
- `VoiceSpec` (interface): What `createVoice` wires.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/spatial.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/spatial.ts)

- `listenerAxes` (function): The listener's forward and up directions (unit vectors) for `pose`.
- `ListenerPose` (interface): Where the listener is and where it looks: the engine's camera pose (engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts) satisfies it.
- `muffling` (function): The lowpass cutoff (Hz) and the gain a sound behind `walls` walls goes through: open at 0 (see the file comment).
- `occluded` (function): Whether a wall of the level stands between `from` (the listener) and `to` (the sound).
- `OCCLUSION` (const): How an occluded sound is muffled, and how occlusion is tested.
- `PANNER` (const): How every placed sound is panned and fades with distance (`PannerNode`'s options).
- `placeListener` (function): Puts the context's listener at `pose` at `time`.
- `placePanner` (function): Puts `panner` at `position` at `time`.
- `Vec3` (type): A point or a direction, world space, m: `[x, y, z]`.
- `wallsBetween` (function): How many walls of the level stand between `from` (the listener) and `to` (the sound), up to `most`: a ray to each wall, another from inside it to its far side (`solid: false`), on from just past it; stopping `OCCLUSION.margin` short of the sound, as `occluded` does.

### [`engine/audio/runtime/voices.ts`](../engine/audio/runtime/voices.ts)

- `createVoicePool` (function): Makes an empty pool with `limits` over the defaults.
- `PooledVoice` (interface): What the pool knows of a voice.
- `VOICE_LIMITS` (const): The default limits.
- `VoiceLimits` (interface): How many voices may play.
- `VoicePool` (interface): The voices playing, and the rules for a new one.

### [`engine/core/color.ts`](../engine/core/color.ts)

- `COLOR_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `ColorInput` (type): A colour as given to the helpers: a hex string, or bytes.
- `fromLinear` (function): Linear RGB floats as `#rrggbb` (sRGB, rounded and clamped), as three.js's `Color.getHexString` writes them.
- `hex` (function): A hex colour (or bytes, of which the first three are kept) as bytes.
- `hsl` (function): Hue (degrees, any value), saturation and lightness (clamped to 0–1) as `#rrggbb`.
- `mix` (function): The colour `t` of the way from `a` to `b` (0 gives `a`, 1 gives `b`), mixed per byte.
- `ramp` (function): `n` colours from dark to light around a colour (hue-shifted like `tones`), for palettes and gradients.
- `Rgb` (type): A colour as three bytes, 0–255 (fractions allowed): red, green, blue.
- `shade` (function): A darker (`amount` < 0, down to −1) or lighter (> 0, up to 1) version of a colour, hue-shifted as painted pixel art is: darker drifts toward blue-violet, lighter toward warm yellow; greys only darken or lighten.
- `toHex` (function): Bytes as `#rrggbb`, each rounded and clamped to 0–255.
- `toHsl` (function): A colour as `[hue in degrees 0–360, saturation 0–1, lightness 0–1]`.
- `toLinear` (function): A colour as linear RGB floats (0–1), as three.js's `Color` holds a hex given to it: for shaders and instances.
- `tones` (function): Five shades of a colour for painted-looking art: shadows drift toward blue-violet, highlights toward warm yellow, by `strength` (0–2, default 1).
- `Tones` (interface): The five shades of `tones`: deep shadow, shadow, the base itself, light and highlight.

### [`engine/core/events.ts`](../engine/core/events.ts)

- `createEvents` (function): Makes an emitter.
- `EVENT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `EventMap` (type): Event type → payload type.
- `Events` (interface): A typed emitter: `on`, `once`, `off`, `emit`, scopes and the trace.
- `EventsOptions` (interface): How an emitter is made: the log its failures go to (the shared one) and how many emits it traces (256).
- `EventsSnapshot` (interface): The listeners and scopes of an emitter at one moment: `restore` puts them back (see the file comment).
- `Listener` (type): A listener of one event type.
- `RegistrationInfo` (interface): One registration as a snapshot lists it: its event type, whether it runs once, and its scope's label.
- `Scope` (interface): Listeners that leave together: `dispose()` removes every one added through this scope or its children.
- `TraceRecord` (interface): One traced emit.

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/cbrt.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/cbrt.ts)

- `cbrt` (function): The real cube root of `x`, as V8's ieee754::cbrt computes it.

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/exp.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/exp.ts)

- `exp` (function): e^x, as V8's ieee754::exp computes it.
- `expm1` (function): e^x − 1, accurate near 0, as V8's ieee754::expm1 computes it.

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/hyperbolic.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/hyperbolic.ts)

- `acosh` (function): The inverse hyperbolic cosine of `x`, NaN below 1, as V8's ieee754::acosh computes it.
- `asinh` (function): The inverse hyperbolic sine of `x`, as V8's ieee754::asinh computes it.
- `atanh` (function): The inverse hyperbolic tangent of `x`, NaN beyond ±1, as V8's ieee754::atanh computes it.
- `cosh` (function): The hyperbolic cosine of `x`, as V8's ieee754::cosh computes it.
- `sinh` (function): The hyperbolic sine of `x`, as V8's ieee754::sinh computes it.
- `tanh` (function): The hyperbolic tangent of `x`, as V8's ieee754::tanh computes it.

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/inverse.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/inverse.ts)

- `acos` (function): The arccosine of `x`, in [0, π], as V8's ieee754::acos computes it.
- `asin` (function): The arcsine of `x`, in [−π/2, π/2], as V8's ieee754::asin computes it.
- `atan` (function): The arctangent of `x`, in [−π/2, π/2], as V8's ieee754::atan computes it.
- `atan2` (function): The angle of the point (x, y) from the +x axis, in [−π, π], as V8's ieee754::atan2 computes it.

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/log.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/log.ts)

- `log` (function): The natural logarithm of `x`, as V8's ieee754::log computes it.
- `log10` (function): The base-10 logarithm of `x`, as V8's ieee754::log10 computes it: n·log10(2) + log(x·2^-n)/ln(10).
- `log1p` (function): ln(1 + x), accurate near 0, as V8's ieee754::log1p computes it.
- `log2` (function): The base-2 logarithm of `x`, as V8's ieee754::log2 computes it (exact at powers of two).

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/remPio2.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/remPio2.ts)

- `NPIO2_HW` (const): The high words of n·π/2 for n = 1 … 32: a reduction near one of them takes the slower, longer path.
- `remPio2` (function): Writes x − n·π/2 into y as two doubles (|y[0] + y[1]| ≤ π/4) and returns n, as V8's __ieee754_rem_pio2 does.
- `TWO_OVER_PI` (const): 2/π's first 1,584 bits, in 24-bit chunks (fdlibm's two_over_pi).

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/tan.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/tan.ts)

- `tan` (function): The tangent of `x` (radians), as V8's ieee754::tan computes it.

### [`engine/core/fdlibm/words.ts`](../engine/core/fdlibm/words.ts)

- `fromWords` (function): The double whose high word is `hi` and low word `lo` (INSERT_WORDS).
- `high` (function): The high word of `x`, as a signed int32.
- `low` (function): The low word of `x`, unsigned.
- `withHigh` (function): `x` with its high word replaced by `hi` (SET_HIGH_WORD).
- `withLow` (function): `x` with its low word replaced by `lo` (SET_LOW_WORD).

### [`engine/core/gallery.ts`](../engine/core/gallery.ts)

- `Gallery` (interface): How the gallery shows an entry: its camera, how long it plays (s) and the states it is shown in.
- `GALLERY_CAMERAS` (const): The camera words a `gallery` field takes besides a camera code.
- `galleryField` (function): The `gallery` field of a kind's schema, with the kind's own defaults (see the file comment).
- `galleryKinds` (function): The kinds of `registry` whose schema has the field `gallery`, sorted.

### [`engine/core/hash.ts`](../engine/core/hash.ts)

- `Canonical` (type): A value the canonical form holds; see the file comment.
- `deserialize` (function): Reads text written by `serialize` back into plain data (arrays for typed arrays and math classes).
- `Fnv64` (class): The 64-bit FNV-1a hash, fed piece by piece: `new Fnv64().number(x).string(id).hex()`.
- `HASH_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `hashNumbers` (function): The 64-bit FNV-1a digest of numbers by their float64 bits, as 16 hex digits: equal state, equal hash.
- `hashValue` (function): The 64-bit FNV-1a digest of a canonical value (plain data, keys in any order), as 16 hex digits.
- `MAX_DEPTH` (const): How deep the canonical form nests before it is refused as a cycle.
- `mix32` (function): murmur3's 32-bit finaliser: spreads every bit of an int over every bit of the unsigned result.
- `serialize` (function): The canonical text of a value: JSON with object keys sorted, no spaces, numbers exact (the shortest round-trip form, `-0` kept), typed arrays and `toArray()` values as arrays.
- `TAG` (const): Type tags of the canonical byte stream, one byte before each value (engine/sim/entities.ts `feedData` feeds them too).

### [`engine/core/log.ts`](../engine/core/log.ts)

- `AdviceRecord` (interface): One piece of advice the log printed: its code, what it is about, its first message and fix, and how often.
- `closest` (function): The candidates closest to `wanted`, best first, at most `count`: a case-insensitive match, then names one starts with the other or ending in `.wanted` (`runSpeed` finds `hero.runSpeed`), then those a few edits away (one per three letters, at least one; a swap of neighbours is one edit).
- `codeError` (function): An `EngineError` for `code`, to throw: `throw codeError('CORE_NO_ENTRY', { kind, id })`.
- `codeInfo` (function): The registered code `code`, or undefined.
- `CodeInfo` (interface): A registered code: its text, its name and its area.
- `CodeText` (interface): One code's text: the message (`{name}` marks a value), what to do about it, and more detail for docs/ERRORS.md.
- `CodeValues` (type): The values a template's `{name}` markers are filled with.
- `createLog` (function): Makes a log; `log` is the engine's shared one.
- `defineCodes` (function): Registers a module's codes and returns the table as given, typed.
- `didYouMean` (function): ` (did you mean "a" or "b"?)` for the names closest to `wanted`, or `''` when none is close.
- `EngineError` (class): A thrown engine error: its code, the filled message, the code's fix and the values that filled it.
- `ErrorRecord` (interface): One structured error: its code, message, fix and values, how often it happened, and its cause when there was one.
- `fill` (function): `template` with each `{name}` replaced by `values.name` (a marker without a value stays as written).
- `listCodes` (function): Every registered code, sorted by name.
- `log` (const): The engine's shared log: registry, events and settings report through it unless given another.
- `Log` (interface): Warn-once advice and structured errors, with what was raised kept for `__engine.advice` and `__engine.errors`.
- `LOG_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `LogConsole` (interface): Where a log prints; tests pass their own to keep the console quiet.
- `LogOptions` (interface): How a log is made: where it prints (the console by default) and how many errors and advice records it keeps.

### [`engine/core/math.ts`](../engine/core/math.ts)

- `angDiff` (function): The signed angle from `a` to `b` the short way round, in [−π, π).
- `approach` (function): `a` moved toward `b` by at most `step` (≥ 0), never past it.
- `approachAng` (function): The angle `a` turned toward `b` by at most `step` (≥ 0) the short way round; exactly `b` once within reach.
- `Box3` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's axis-aligned box.
- `Color` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's colour (linear RGB floats inside; a hex given to it is sRGB).
- `ease` (const): Easing curves over u in [0, 1], each 0 at 0 and 1 at 1: `outCubic`, `outQuad`, `inQuad`, `inOut` (quadratic in and out) and `outBack`, which overshoots to about 1.12 at u ≈ 0.55 (c1 = 1.9; easings.net's easeOutBack uses 1.70158).
- `Euler` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's Euler angles (radians, an axis order).
- `lerpAng` (function): The angle `t` of the way from `a` to `b`, the short way round (`t` = 1 lands on `b` plus whole turns).
- `MathUtils` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's scalar helpers: `clamp`, `lerp`, `damp`, `smoothstep`, `degToRad`, `euclideanModulo` and more.
- `Matrix4` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's 4×4 matrix: transforms.
- `Plane` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's plane: a unit normal and a constant.
- `Quaternion` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's quaternion: every rotation in the engine.
- `Ray` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's ray: an origin and a unit direction.
- `smoothDamp` (function): A critically damped spring toward `target` (Game Programming Gems 4's, as Unity's `SmoothDamp`): reaches it in about `smoothTime` seconds without overshoot.
- `Sphere` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's sphere.
- `swingTwist` (function): Splits the rotation `q` into a twist about the unit vector `axis` and a swing about an axis perpendicular to it, with `q = swing · twist` (twist applied first): a joint's roll and its bend.
- `Vector3` (re-export from `three/webgpu`): three.js's 3D vector: positions, directions, velocities (metres, +Y up).

### [`engine/core/noise.ts`](../engine/core/noise.ts)

- `createNoise2D` (function): A seeded 2D noise of `kind` (gradient by default); see the file comment for ranges, tiling and octaves.
- `createNoise3D` (function): A seeded 3D noise of `kind` (gradient by default); see the file comment for ranges, tiling and octaves.
- `hash2` (function): my-3d2dge's integer hash of a lattice point: a number in [0, 1), bit-exact.
- `NOISE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `noise2` (function): my-3d2dge's value noise: smoothstep between `hash2` lattice values, in [0, 1], bit-exact.
- `Noise2D` (type): A 2D noise: a pure function of the point.
- `Noise3D` (type): A 3D noise: a pure function of the point.
- `NoiseKind` (type): The kinds of noise: value (lattice values), gradient (Perlin's) and cell (Worley's F1 distance).
- `NoiseOptions` (interface): How a noise is made; every field is optional.

### [`engine/core/registry.ts`](../engine/core/registry.ts)

- `createRegistry` (function): Makes an empty registry; `registry` is the engine's shared one.
- `def` (function): Defines an entry on the shared registry (`Registry.def`).
- `defineKind` (function): Declares a kind on the shared registry (`Registry.defineKind`).
- `Entry` (type): A registry entry: the parsed spec plus its `id` and `kind`.
- `EntryDescription` (interface): What `describe(kind, id)` returns: each field's value, marked where it differs from the default.
- `get` (function): Reads an entry from the shared registry (`Registry.get`).
- `has` (function): Whether the shared registry's kind has the id (`Registry.has`).
- `Kind` (interface): A declared kind, bound: the same as the registry's functions with the kind filled in, typed by its schema.
- `KindDescription` (interface): What `describe(kind)` returns: the kind's fields and ids.
- `KindsDescription` (interface): What `describe()` returns: every kind, with its entry count.
- `KindSpec` (interface): How a kind is declared.
- `list` (function): The shared registry's entries of a kind, sorted by id (`Registry.list`).
- `registry` (const): The engine's shared registry: what `x describe` and `__engine.describe()` list.
- `Registry` (interface): A set of kinds and their entries.
- `REGISTRY_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `sameValue` (function): Deep equality of plain data (arrays, plain objects, numbers by `Object.is`).

### [`engine/core/rng.ts`](../engine/core/rng.ts)

- `derive` (function): A seed derived from `seed` and `keys` (strings or numbers), as an unsigned 32-bit integer: the 64-bit FNV-1a hash of `[seed, …keys]` in canonical form, folded and mixed.
- `Rng` (class): One Mulberry32 stream: `next()` and the usual helpers, all drawn from `next()` in order.
- `RngStreams` (class): Named streams from one seed (the scene's): `stream('ai')`, `entity(7, 'anim')`.

### [`engine/core/schema.ts`](../engine/core/schema.ts)

- `checkField` (function): The problems of one field definition (not of a value): the checks `defineSchema` runs on each field.
- `checkValue` (function): Checks one value against its field, pushing each problem onto `problems`; returns the value with the defaults of nested objects filled (a copy when it is an array or a plain object, for any type, `any` included).
- `copyValue` (function): A copy of arrays and plain objects (functions and other values as they are), so defaults are never shared.
- `defineSchema` (function): Checks a schema's fields and returns it unchanged; throws `CORE_BAD_SCHEMA` naming every problem.
- `describeSchema` (function): A schema as plain, JSON-ready rows, in its own key order (for `x describe` and `__engine.describe`).
- `EntryOf` (type): What `parse` returns for schema `S`: required fields and fields with a default are always present.
- `Field` (interface): One field: what its values are, documented.
- `FIELD_TYPES` (const): Every `FieldType`, in documentation order.
- `FieldRow` (type): One field as `describe` lists it: its keywords, with a function default shown as `'function'`.
- `FieldType` (type): The value types: JSON's, plus `integer`, `function` (a hook) and `any`.
- `freezeValue` (function): Freezes arrays and plain objects all the way down (other values as they are) and returns `value`: stored data.
- `isPlainObject` (function): True for `{}` literals and `Object.create(null)`.
- `listProblems` (function): Joins problems into one sentence list for an error message.
- `parse` (function): `validate`, throwing `CORE_BAD_SPEC` with every problem when there is one; `where` names the spec in the message.
- `Problem` (interface): One thing wrong with a spec or a schema: where (`roughness`, `layers[2].color`) and a plain sentence.
- `Schema` (type): A schema: field name → field.
- `SCHEMA_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `show` (function): How a value reads in a message: strings quoted, other values as JSON would write them.
- `SpecOf` (type): What `parse` and `def` accept for schema `S`: the required fields, and any of the others.
- `suggestKey` (function): ` (write minimum)` for a word the language spells differently, else the closest of `keys`, else `''`.
- `validate` (function): Checks `input` against `schema`: the filled value (every given key plus absent defaults) and every problem found.
- `ValueOf` (type): The TypeScript type of a field's values.
- `When` (type): When a change takes effect: at once, for what spawns next, or when the scene next starts.

### [`engine/core/settings.ts`](../engine/core/settings.ts)

- `createSettings` (function): Makes a settings store over `registry`'s settings, each at its default.
- `defineSettings` (function): Declares settings, path → field, on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `SettingChange` (interface): What `set` reports: the new and previous values, and when the change takes effect.
- `SettingRow` (interface): One setting as `describe` lists it.
- `Settings` (interface): A settings store over the `setting` entries of a registry.
- `SETTINGS_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `SettingsOptions` (interface): How a store is made: the registry whose `setting` entries it serves (the shared one by default).
- `SettingValue` (type): A setting's value: plain data.
- `SimSettings` (interface): What sim-side code reads settings through (`w.settings` in a scene): no view settings, no writes.

### [`engine/core/simMath.ts`](../engine/core/simMath.ts)

- `inSimMath` (function): True while a `withSimMath` call is running.
- `SIM_MATH` (const): What the swap puts into `Math`, by function name (PLAN.md §6.5): the functions that differ between runtimes.
- `SIM_MATH_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `SIM_MATH_NAMES` (const): Every swapped name, in `SIM_MATH`'s order.
- `SimMathEntry` (interface): A `Math` function the sim swaps: its pure-JavaScript port, where the port comes from, and the native one.
- `SimMathName` (type): The names of the swapped `Math` functions.
- `withSimMath` (function): Runs `fn` with the fdlibm ports in `Math` and returns its result; the previous functions are back afterwards, whether `fn` returns or throws; a `fn` that returns a promise throws `CORE_SIM_ASYNC`.

### [`engine/core/time.ts`](../engine/core/time.ts)

- `Clock` (interface): Turns frame timestamps into fixed steps: the accumulator, the time scale, slowdowns, hit-stop and pause.
- `ClockOptions` (interface): How a clock is made.
- `ClockState` (interface): The clock's state as plain data, for the inspector and tests (never hashed: it changes no step).
- `createClock` (function): Makes a frame clock; it reads `time.*` from its settings store on every frame.
- `createVirtualClock` (function): Makes a virtual clock starting at `start` milliseconds.
- `Frame` (interface): What one `advance` hands out.
- `SIM_DT` (const): One sim step in seconds, 1/60.
- `SIM_HZ` (const): The sim's steps per second: gameplay time is counted in 60 Hz ticks (ADR-0005).
- `TIME_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `TIME_SETTINGS` (const): The time settings, path → field; `defineSettings(TIME_SETTINGS, registry)` declares them on another registry.
- `VirtualClock` (interface): A clock for tests that moves only when told: `now()` in milliseconds, as a page's timestamps are.

### [`engine/core/timers.ts`](../engine/core/timers.ts)

- `advanceEntityClock` (function): Advances `clock` by the world's (or its owner's) `dt` seconds and returns the entity's own dt for this step.
- `createEntityClock` (function): Makes an entity clock running at `rate`.
- `createTimers` (function): Makes timers counting ticks at `hz` steps per second (`time.hz`, 60 by default).
- `EntityClock` (interface): A per-entity clock: plain numbers a component holds, so captures and the hash take it as data.
- `freezeEntityClock` (function): Freezes `clock` for `seconds` of world time; a longer freeze already running is kept.
- `Timer` (interface): A timer's handle.
- `TimerCallback` (type): What a timer calls: it gets its own handle, so `every` can cancel itself.
- `Timers` (interface): Timers in sim time; the world steps them once per sim step.
- `TimersCapture` (interface): The timers with their callbacks, for `restore` in the same process.
- `TimersState` (interface): The timers as plain numbers, for the hash, in firing order: `[id, due tick, period in ticks (0 for one-shot), start tick, firings so far]`.

### [`engine/dev/actions.ts`](../engine/dev/actions.ts)

- `ActionRow` (interface): One dev action as `actions.list()` shows it.

### [`engine/dev/bot.ts`](../engine/dev/bot.ts)

- `Bot` (class): The bot: one goal at a time, the intents for each step (see the file comment).
- `BOT_FIELDS` (const): How the bot moves and when it gives up: `new Bot(level, options)` and every run take them.
- `BotOptions` (type): What `new Bot` takes: each field of `BOT_FIELDS`, optional.
- `BotPlan` (interface): What a run plays (see the file comment), with the bot's options.
- `BotReport` (interface): What a run did.
- `BotRun` (interface): What the bot plays: a world to read and a recorded step.
- `BotSample` (interface): One sample of a run's trace.
- `BotStatus` (type): Where a bot stands with its goal.
- `BotWorld` (type): The world as the bot reads it: the session's, or the inspector's read-only view of it.
- `runBot` (function): Plays `run` with the bot over `level` or a site (see the file comment) and reports what happened.

### [`engine/dev/botNav.ts`](../engine/dev/botNav.ts)

- `BotNav` (interface): What the bot navigates by (see the file comment).
- `BotPoint` (type): A point the bot reads: on the ground (x, z), its height where a site has storeys, and what the body does there (the shooter model's mode, `ladder`, `air`…, and stance, `stand` or `crouch`).
- `BotWay` (interface): The way to one goal: the walking distance from a point (Infinity where none leads), the unit way to walk, and whether to crouch there (under a low ceiling, or for one a little way along it: a site's attic, a crawlspace's door; never on a level's grid).
- `closedDoorAhead` (function): Whether `actor`'s interactor (engine/sim/interact.ts) is on a closed door it can open: one shut, not locked, not broken and on no switch (engine/sim/doors.ts).
- `levelBotNav` (function): A level's grid as the bot reads it, a step climbing at most `climb` metres.
- `siteBotNav` (function): A site's graph as the bot reads it (see the file comment), a step climbing at most `climb` metres, `blocked` closed.
- `tourStream` (const): The bot's own stream for a run's tour: `derive(seed, 'bot')`, never the world's.

### [`engine/dev/botSweep.ts`](../engine/dev/botSweep.ts)

- `BotRow` (interface): One row of the bot's report: a scene, its seeds' runs and their sums.
- `parseSeeds` (function): Seeds as a sweep takes them: `1-20`, `5` (1 to 5), `3,7,9`, a count or a list; 1 to 500 whole numbers from 0.
- `sweepBot` (function): Plays `plan` from a fresh session of `scene` per seed (see the file comment): one row for the scene.
- `SweepOptions` (interface): How a sweep starts each run: the scene's settings over its own, its registry and its level.

### [`engine/dev/eye.ts`](../engine/dev/eye.ts)

- `asciiOf` (function): `view` as text, a character a cell, and its legend (see the file comment).
- `EYE_SIZE` (const): The raster's size by default (cells across and down): the page's 16:9 at a tenth of 960 × 540.
- `EyeCamera` (interface): What the eye reads of a three.js camera as placed: its matrices and its depth's convention.
- `eyeJson` (function): `view` as plain data (see `EyeJson`).
- `EyeJson` (interface): The eye's answer as plain data, for `__engine.eye` and `x eye`: the raster as text, its legend and what it sees.
- `EyeOptions` (interface): How the eye looks: the raster's cells across and down (`EYE_SIZE`), a body to look past, and what the view draws.
- `EyeOwner` (interface): Who holds a body: its entity, a name for the legend, and whether it is the player or an actor.
- `EyeThing` (interface): One thing the eye sees: its key (`entity:7`, `level`), its kind, its entity, and the cells it covers.
- `EyeView` (interface): What a camera sees (see the file comment).
- `FLOOR_UP` (const): How far up a surface's normal points for the picture to draw it as floor (0.7: the walkable slope's, 45.57°).
- `look` (function): What `camera`, as placed, sees of the bodies `queries` reach, named by `owners` (see the file comment).
- `ownersOf` (function): Each body held by an entity's component (its `body`, a whole number), by body id; the first holder wins.
- `seen` (function): Whether `view` sees `entity` in at least one cell.
- `WEBGPU_COORDINATES` (const): three.js's `WebGPUCoordinateSystem`, the view's cameras' (engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts): depth from 0 to 1.

### [`engine/dev/eyeFaces.ts`](../engine/dev/eyeFaces.ts)

- `drawnFaces` (function): Indexes what `root` draws (see the file comment).
- `EyeAttribute` (interface): What `drawnFaces` reads of a three.js buffer attribute: its count and each item's components.
- `EyeFaces` (interface): The drawn faces (see the file comment).
- `EyeObject` (interface): What `drawnFaces` reads of a three.js object: `Object3D`, `Mesh` and `InstancedMesh`, as far as it needs.
- `FACE_CELL` (const): The grid's cube, m: a triangle is listed in every cube its box, `FACE_NEAR` wider, overlaps.
- `FACE_NEAR` (const): How far from a drawn face a struck point may lie and be on it, m: a collider and its mesh meet within it.

### [`engine/dev/feel/anim.ts`](../engine/dev/feel/anim.ts)

- `AnimTrack` (type): An animation track: what `createAnimTrack` returns.
- `createAnimTrack` (function): An animator posed once a step as the page poses it, and the anim QA's numbers over its frames; with the sim's read-only `queries`, its feet stand on their ground as the page's do, and a sole's height is from the ground under it.
- `HAND_SOCKETS` (const): The hands, as sockets: what `handGap` measures from.
- `TrackTraverse` (interface): What a traversing body is on (the ride, its component: engine/anim/traversal/contacts.ts `rideOf`), its hull and its look.

### [`engine/dev/feel/camera.ts`](../engine/dev/feel/camera.ts)

- `armsClipped` (function): Whether `arms`, drawn by their lens for `pose`, are covered by the world along their rays or cut by its near plane: any of their points that lands in the picture (across and up, in front of the eye) nearer than the near plane, or with a wall between it and the eye.
- `ArmsFrame` (interface): First person's arms in a frame: their grips, the points along their shown parts (world, m), and their lens.
- `CAMERA_CHECK` (const): What the frames are checked with: the picture's aspect, the camera's ball (m) and where the player's chest is (m).
- `CameraFrame` (interface): One frame of a camera track: its pose, the player's feet, what the frame found, and what it may move and turn.
- `CameraMetrics` (interface): A camera track's numbers (see the file comment).
- `CameraTrack` (type): A camera track: what `createCameraTrack` returns.
- `createCameraTrack` (function): A camera stepped once a sim step behind the player, and its frames (see the file comment).
- `inPicture` (function): Whether `point` is in the picture of `pose`, a frame of `aspect`: in front of it, within its lens or frustum.
- `LOOK_CAMERAS` (const): The cameras that look along the sim's look (first person, the shooter's): the look's turn swings them.
- `TrackFrame` (interface): What a frame of the track takes beside the feet.

### [`engine/dev/feel/course.ts`](../engine/dev/feel/course.ts)

- `ANIM_METRICS` (const): The metrics of the player's animation, posed as the page poses it.
- `CAMERA_METRICS` (const): The metrics of a camera following the player.
- `Course` (type): A course, as the registry holds it.
- `COURSE_FIELDS` (const): A course's fields: what `defineCourse` takes (see the file comment).
- `courseKind` (function): Declares the kind `course` on `registry`, once.
- `defineCourse` (function): Registers a course (on the shared registry by default).
- `getCourse` (function): The course `id`.
- `listCourses` (function): Every course, sorted by id.
- `Measure` (interface): A measure, as a course holds it.
- `MEASURE_FIELDS` (const): One number a course measures (see the file comment).
- `Metric` (type): A measure's metric.
- `METRICS` (const): Everything a measure reads off the run (see the file comment).
- `MOVE_METRICS` (const): The metrics of the move, read off the player's samples: `speed`, the mean speed across the ground from `from` to `to`, and `topSpeed`, the highest; `speedGain`, the speed across the ground at `to` less that at `from`, and `velocityChange`, how far the velocity across the ground moved between them (a lurch's, m/s); `apex`, how far the feet rise above where they were at `from`; `height`, the feet's height at `to`; `distance`, across the ground from the feet at `from` to the feet at `to`; `time`, seconds from `from` to the first sample that meets `until` (`speedAbove` or `speedBelow` `value`, `grounded` or `airborne`; on the shooter model `crouched` or `standing`, its hull, `sliding` or `stopsSliding`, `mantling`, `grabbing`, `hanging`, `pulling` or `climbing`, and `riding` a zipline, `onLadder`, `skydiving` or in its `landingPose`), and `duration`, how long from the first sample that meets it it goes on meeting it (0 if none does); `top`, the highest its feet go; `heightAt`, the feet's height at the first sample that meets `until`; `topRise` and `topFall`, the fastest it rises and falls (m/s); `standHeight`, the highest its feet stand on the ground (what it mantled or climbed onto); `grounded`, 1 when it stands at `to`; `rideSpeed`, its speed along a zipline or up a ladder at `to`, and `rideGain`, that at `to` less that at `from`; `catches`, the most zipline catches it made since it last stood.
- `UNTILS` (const): When a `time` measure stops: the first sample at which this holds.

- `createFeelPanel` (function): Builds the feel panel on `document` over `inspector` (see the file comment).

- `profileText` (function): The `defineMovement` call of `spec` as `id`, then `camera`'s settings (path → value) as a preset when any differ.
- `tunedSpec` (function): `base` with `overrides` over its model, as a spec that states only what differs from Apex's numbers.

### [`engine/dev/feel/run.ts`](../engine/dev/feel/run.ts)

- `CourseRecord` (interface): What a run recorded, which `measure` reads: the samples, the posed animation, each camera measure's track.
- `CourseResult` (interface): What `runCourse` gives: every measure's verdict, whether all but the watched passed, the final hash and the samples.
- `CourseSample` (interface): The first player actor's state after a step: what a move measure reads.
- `judge` (function): `m`'s verdict on `value`: within its tolerance (any one it names) of its reference.

- `runCourse` (function): Plays `course` in a session of its own and judges its measures (see the file comment).

### [`engine/dev/gallery.ts`](../engine/dev/gallery.ts)

- `burstLife` (function): How long an emitter's burst plays in the gallery (s): while every particle of its longest-lived part still lives, its own (with a count or a rate) and each layer's (its `set.life`, else its emitter's), the shortest life of each.
- `fitCamera` (function): The camera code of a frame's view: a code as written, or a fixed camera (engine/gfx/cameras/fixed.ts) standing at `azimuth` round `bounds` (the subject, as the stage draws it; azimuth from +Z toward +X, as an orbit's), 25° above its middle and looking at it, far enough for its bounding sphere to fill the lens's height with a margin.

- `GALLERY_STAGING` (const): The kinds the gallery stages (engine/dev/galleryScene.ts), with how it films each.
- `GalleryFrame` (interface): One frame of an entry: what the scene stages for it, how long it holds and plays, and where the camera stands.
- `galleryFrames` (function): The frames of entry `id` of `kind` (see the file comment); the kind must be one the gallery films.
- `galleryKindsOf` (function): The kinds the gallery films: those whose schema has the `gallery` field and that it stages.
- `galleryProblem` (function): Whether `kind` and `id` name an entry the gallery films; else the warning's values (see `DEV_GALLERY_UNKNOWN`).
- `galleryRoute` (function): Reads a deep link (see the file comment): null when `hash` is no gallery link, else the entry it shows, after warning about a wrong kind or id (`DEV_GALLERY_UNKNOWN`), which shows the first instead.
- `GalleryRoute` (interface): What a deep link names: the kind and the entry to show.
- `galleryStart` (function): The settings a page opened on `route` starts with: what the scene stages first, its first frame's view settings.

- `FIGURE_STATES` (const): Every name `figureState` knows: walk and run, the sample states, the poses and the stances.

### [`engine/dev/galleryShoot.ts`](../engine/dev/galleryShoot.ts)

- `BURST_REACH` (const): The most an emitter's frame takes in, across (m): a burst's 3; an effect spread over an area wider than 1 m (rain, snow, fireflies), a 1.2 m patch of it, so its drops are drops and not specks.

### [`engine/dev/governor.ts`](../engine/dev/governor.ts)

- `createGovernor` (function): Makes a governor; `log` takes its advice (the shared log by default).

- `GOVERNOR` (const): The governor's numbers (see the file comment): seconds, milliseconds a frame, and the scale's steps.

### [`engine/dev/inspector.ts`](../engine/dev/inspector.ts)

### [`engine/dev/stats.ts`](../engine/dev/stats.ts)

- `COUNT_KEYS` (const): The count fields of `EngineStats`, in report order.
- `createStatsMeter` (function): Makes a meter (see the file comment).
- `EngineStats` (interface): What `__engine.stats()` returns: means in milliseconds, then the renderer's counts (null when not measured).
- `meterOf` (function): The meter `host` carries; throws `DEV_NO_METER` without one.
- `ProbedSystem` (interface): A system as the probe sees it: its phase, of engine/sim/systems.ts's `PHASES`.
- `RenderCounts` (type): The renderer's counts the meter reports (engine/gfx/renderer.ts `GfxStats`), and its GPU time where it has one.
- `STATS_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `STATS_WINDOW` (const): How many steps or frames the means cover: the last second at 60 Hz.
- `StatsHost` (interface): An inspector host that carries a meter (engine/app/headless.ts gives every engine's host one).
- `StatsMeter` (interface): The meter: times steps, phases and frames, and reads them back as `EngineStats`.
- `StatsMeterOptions` (interface): How a meter is made: its clock (ms), its window, and the renderer's counts (absent headless).
- `TIMED_PARTS` (const): What the meter times: the whole sim step, its `physics` and `anim` phases, and a drawn frame's CPU side.
- `TimedPart` (type): One timed part.

### [`engine/gfx/atmosphere.ts`](../engine/gfx/atmosphere.ts)

- `AMBIENT_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a sky preset's `ambient` (engine/gfx/sky.ts); see `AmbientSpec`.

- `Atmosphere` (interface): The atmosphere: its ambient light and fog; see the file comment.

- `FOG_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a sky preset's `fog` (engine/gfx/sky.ts); see `FogSpec`.

### [`engine/gfx/backdrop.ts`](../engine/gfx/backdrop.ts)

- `BACKDROP` (const): The backdrop strip's size in texels, and its band round the camera (m): radius, height, foot below the eye.
- `BACKDROP_KINDS` (const): The kinds of backdrop layer.
- `BackdropLayers` (interface): A backdrop as a `sky` entry gives it (engine/gfx/sky.ts `BackdropSpec`): the haze colour and the layers.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/api.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/api.ts)

- `AnyCamera` (type from [`engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts)): Any camera `createCamera` makes: codes.ts's (`Camera`), or a follow camera, whose inputs add the hero's.
- `AnyCameraSpec` (type from [`engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts)): The code data of any camera: codes.ts's, a follow camera's, or a game camera's.
- `apexFov` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): The lens (vertical degrees) of Apex's field of view `h`: horizontal degrees at 4:3.
- `applyEffects` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): `pose` with the effects of `frame` on it, each part scaled by `weights` (see the file comment).
- `BLEND_TIME` (const from [`engine/gfx/cameras/blend.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/blend.ts)): How long a switch blends, real seconds.
- `blendCameras` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/blend.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/blend.ts)): The pose `w` (0 to 1) of the way from `a` to `b` (see the file comment).
- `Camera` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): A camera: its state, stepped once per rendered frame, and its pose.
- `CAMERA_SETTINGS` (const from [`engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts)): The view settings the rig reads, declared on the shared registry.
- `CameraInput` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): What the devices give a camera in a frame; every field is optional (orbit and fly turn, fly moves, views zoom).
- `CameraKindSpec` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts)): What `defineCamera` takes: `create` makes the camera from its code and the camera before it.
- `cameraPlayer` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): What the cameras read of the player actor `entity` (`actor`, and `motion` on the shooter model); null for another.
- `CameraPlayer` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): What the effects and the follow cameras read of the player after a sim step: plain data.
- `CameraRig` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts)): The camera rig (see the file comment).
- `createCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts)): The camera `code` names (a code, or its data from `readCameraCode`): `cam=iso`, `cam3=orbit,…`, `cam3=chase`.
- `createCameraEffects` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): The effects' springs and phases (see the file comment).
- `createCameraRig` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts)): Makes a rig on the camera `code` names (see the file comment).
- `createChaseCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts)): A chase camera: behind the hero on its arm, following `input.follow`, in front of the walls `input.queries` sees.
- `createFirstCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/first.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/first.ts)): A first-person camera: at the hero's eyes (`input.eye`), turned by the devices; it takes every view effect.
- `createFollowCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts)): A follow camera: orbiting the hero and following him (see the file comment).
- `createShoulderCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts)): A shoulder camera: over the hero's shoulder (`input.eye`), turned by the devices, in front of the walls.
- `createViewCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/presets.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/presets.ts)): A classic view as a `Camera` (`options.view` names it; codes.ts's `VIEW_LABELS` has the names in words).
- `defineCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts)): Adds a game's camera mode on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `EFFECTS` (const from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): The effects' numbers (see the file comment): metres, radians, seconds.
- `EffectsFrame` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): One frame of the effects (see the file comment).
- `EffectWeights` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)): How much of each effect a camera takes, 0 to 1 (see the file comment).
- `FOLLOW_RIG` (const from [`engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts)): The rig's numbers (see the file comment): metres, seconds, rad/s; `lens` its lens, degrees.
- `followCamera` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts)): Wraps a camera's pure steps and first state in a camera, as `cameraFrom` does for the cameras codes.ts lists; it takes the view `effects` (engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts) and `fade` (see `FollowCamera`) when given.
- `FollowCamera` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts)): A WP 3.9 camera: a `Camera` (engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts) whose type and code data codes.ts does not list yet.
- `FollowInput` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts)): A follow camera's input: the devices', the hero (his eye and what he does) and the walls.
- `FollowSpec` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/follow.ts)): A follow camera's code as data: without the numbers it keeps the heading of the camera before it.
- `FollowSteps` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts)): What a WP 3.9 camera gives `followCamera`: its pure steps, as `CameraSteps`, and its code and words.
- `makePose` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): A checked, frozen pose: `fields` over `POSE_DEFAULTS`.
- `poseForward` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): The unit view direction (three.js's `camera.getWorldDirection()`).
- `poseRight` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): The unit right direction on screen: forward × up, level whatever the pitch, tipped down by a `roll` (if any).
- `poseTarget` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): The point the camera looks at: `distance` along its view direction.
- `poseUp` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)): The unit up direction on screen: right × forward (the heading when the camera looks straight down), tipped right by a `roll`.
- `readCameraCode` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts)): Reads any camera's code: a follow camera's (`cam3=chase…`, `cam3=first…`, `cam3=rail…`, `cam3=shoulder…`, `cam3=follow…`) by its module, a game camera's (`defineCamera`) as its name and code, every other by `parseCameraCode`.
- `RigInput` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts)): What the rig's cameras take each frame: the devices', the hero (his eye, his look, his state) and the walls.
- `rigOptions` (function from [`engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts)): The rig's options from the view settings `cam.*`, read by `get` (a settings store's).
- `RigOptions` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rig.ts)): The rig's options (see the file comment).
- `SHOULDER` (const from [`engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts)): The rig's numbers (see the file comment): metres and real seconds; `lens` its own lens, degrees (Apex's 90 at 4:3).
- `ShoulderInput` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts)): A shoulder camera's input: the devices', the hero's eye and the walls.
- `ShoulderSpec` (interface from [`engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts)): A shoulder camera's code as data: without the numbers it looks where the camera before it looked.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/blend.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/blend.ts)

- `BLEND_LENS` (const): The lens an orthographic pose blends with, degrees: narrow, so the swap of projections barely shows.
- `BLEND_TIME` (const): How long a switch blends, real seconds.
- `blendCameras` (function): The pose `w` (0 to 1) of the way from `a` to `b` (see the file comment).
- `blendGap` (function): How far (m) and how much (rad) the blend from `a` to `b` moves the picture from weight `from` to weight `to`.
- `blendWeight` (function): The eased share of a blend `t` seconds into `time` (a smoothstep; 1 when `time` is 0).
- `turnBetween` (function): The angle between two poses' view directions, rad.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/boost.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/boost.ts)

- `applyBoost` (function): Multiplies `camera`'s projection by V·S·V⁻¹ (S: world y × `k`), with its current matrices.
- `boost` (function): The prototype's `boost()`: updates `camera`'s world and projection matrices, then stretches heights by `k` in the projection.
- `Boosted` (interface): A camera that keeps a height boost through `updateProjectionMatrix()`.
- `BoostedOrthographicCamera` (class): three.js's `OrthographicCamera` with a height `boost` its projection keeps (see the file comment).
- `BoostedPerspectiveCamera` (class): three.js's `PerspectiveCamera` with a height `boost` its projection keeps (see the file comment).
- `isBoosted` (function): Whether `camera` keeps its own boost (one of this module's camera classes).

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/chase.ts)

- `CHASE_DEFAULTS` (const): The arm's starting pitch (rad, + up), length (m) and the lens (degrees, `PerspectiveCamera.fov`).
- `CHASE_HEIGHT` (const): The pivot's height above the followed point, m: the hero's head.
- `CHASE_LAG` (const): The time constant of the pivot's follow, real seconds.
- `CHASE_LIMITS` (const): The range of the pitch (rad) and the arm's length (m).
- `CHASE_RADIUS` (const): The radius of the ball cast along the arm, m: collide.ts's `COLLIDE_RADIUS`.
- `CHASE_RETURN` (const): The time constant of the arm easing back out after a wall, real seconds: collide.ts's `COLLIDE_RETURN`.
- `CHASE_SKIN` (const): How far short of a surface the ball stops, m: collide.ts's `COLLIDE_SKIN`.
- `CHASE_TURN_SPEED` (const): Turn rates at full `input.turn`, rad/s: `[right, up]` (the prototype's [ ] keys turn 2.2).
- `ChaseInput` (interface): A chase camera's input: the devices' and the hero's, and the walls it keeps out of (collide.ts).
- `ChaseOptions` (interface): Options for a chase camera: its code's data, the lens, and the camera before it.
- `chasePose` (function): The chase camera's pose: `arm` metres back from the pivot along its view direction, looking at the pivot.
- `chaseSpec` (function): The chase camera's code data.
- `ChaseSpec` (interface): A chase camera's code as data: without the numbers it keeps the heading of the camera before it.
- `chaseState` (function): A checked chase state for `options`.
- `ChaseState` (interface): A chase camera's state: plain data, replaced by each step.
- `codeDegrees` (function): Radians as a code writes them: degrees to 0.01, wrapped into (−180, 180] when `wrap` (headings).
- `codeNumber` (function): A number as a camera code writes it: rounded to `places` decimals, shortest form, never `-0` (as codes.ts).
- `CodePart` (type): One number of a code: its name and the range it must be in, as written (degrees, metres).
- `createChaseCamera` (function): A chase camera: behind the hero on its arm, following `input.follow`, in front of the walls `input.queries` sees.
- `describeChase` (function): A chase camera in words.
- `followCamera` (function): Wraps a camera's pure steps and first state in a camera, as `cameraFrom` does for the cameras codes.ts lists; it takes the view `effects` (engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts) and `fade` (see `FollowCamera`) when given.
- `FollowCamera` (interface): A WP 3.9 camera: a `Camera` (engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts) whose type and code data codes.ts does not list yet.
- `FollowSteps` (interface): What a WP 3.9 camera gives `followCamera`: its pure steps, as `CameraSteps`, and its code and words.
- `formatChaseCode` (function): The canonical code of a chase camera's data (numbers rounded: 0.01°, 0.001 m).
- `parseChaseCode` (function): Reads a chase camera's code: `cam3=chase[,<yaw>,<pitch>,<distance>]`.
- `readCode` (function): The numbers of `cam3=<name>[,…]` (with or without the `?` and the key): as many as one of `counts`, each within its `parts` range.
- `stepChase` (function): Steps a chase camera by one rendered frame: turned by `look` and `turn`, `zoom` on the arm, following, walls.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/codes.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/codes.ts)

- `CAMERA_3D` (const): The 3D cameras of `cam3=`.
- `CAMERA_CODES` (const): The codes the cameras raise, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `CameraSpec` (type): A camera code as data.
- `CameraType` (type): The kinds of camera: a classic view, an orbit round a target, a free fly camera, a fixed one.
- `describeCamera` (function): `spec` in words, as the prototype's `camDesc`: `Isometric view, orthographic, zoom 1x, following`.
- `FOLLOW_CAMERAS` (const): The cameras that follow the hero and read their own codes (`readCameraCode`): WP 3.9's chase, first person and the rail, and WP 13.8's shooter (`shoulder`) and platformer (`follow`).
- `formatCameraCode` (function): The canonical code of `spec`: `cam=…` or `cam3=…`, numbers rounded (0.001 m, 0.01°), defaults left out.
- `FreeSpec` (interface): A fly or fixed camera's code as data: without a position it starts from the camera before it.
- `OrbitSpec` (interface): An orbit camera's code as data.
- `parseCameraCode` (function): Reads a camera code (see the file comment for the grammar): `cam=…`, `cam3=…`, with or without a leading `?`, or a bare value (`iso`, `orbit`, `30,40,1,0.5,1`).
- `VIEW_LABELS` (const): Each view's name in words.
- `VIEW_NAMES` (const): Every view name, in the order the 2D engine cycles them, then WP 13.8's `overhead` (`custom` last).
- `ViewName` (type): The classic views (engine/gfx/cameras/presets.ts has their numbers), and `custom` (any azimuth and elevation).
- `ViewSpec` (interface): A classic view's code as data: missing fields take the camera's defaults.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/collide.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/collide.ts)

- `ArmFrame` (interface): Where an arm's base stands and which way its view looks: what carries a `moveCamera` camera.
- `CameraBall` (interface): A `moveCamera` camera's state: where it stood, and how long it has stood more than a metre from where it wants.
- `CameraKeep` (interface): How a `moveCamera` camera keeps the base: the sight it keeps, and the trail's points it heads for.
- `carry` (function): Where `at`, placed relative to the arm `from` (its base and view), stands relative to the arm `to`.
- `COLLIDE_PULL` (const): The fastest a `moveCamera` camera closes in on its arm's end beyond what carries it, m/s: 1/6 m a frame at 60 Hz.
- `COLLIDE_RADIUS` (const): The radius of the ball cast, m: wider than the near plane's corners (0.09 m at 60° and 21:9).
- `COLLIDE_RETURN` (const): The time constant of an arm easing back out after a wall, real seconds.
- `COLLIDE_SKIN` (const): How far short of a surface the ball stops, m.
- `COLLIDE_STUCK` (const): How long a `moveCamera` camera may stand more than a metre from where it wants before it goes there, s.
- `COLLIDE_TELEPORT` (const): A carry longer than this in one frame is the player put somewhere else, m: the camera goes with him at once.
- `easeArm` (function): An arm's length after the walls (see the file comment): `arm` eased toward `want`, never past `clear`.
- `follow` (function): A point that follows `to` and never passes through a wall: slid from where it was (`last`), at most `step` m this frame (what `to` itself moved plus `COLLIDE_PULL`·dt, so one held at a lip catches up, never jumps), or swept from `from` (the hero's eye, clear of the walls) on the first frame or when `to` is further than `COLLIDE_TELEPORT` from it and the step allows that (the hero put elsewhere).
- `moveCamera` (function): Moves a camera on by a frame (see the file comment): from `ball` (null on the first frame), carried to `carried`, then toward `want`, the arm's end, where the ball fits there, else as far along the arm as a sweep from `base` clears, keeping in the base's sight (`keep.room` to spare); out of it, along the base's trail no nearer the base than `keep.trail`.
- `QueryGroups` (type): The collision groups a query hits, as the `QueryView` names them.
- `reach` (function): How far a ball of `COLLIDE_RADIUS` gets from `from` along the unit `dir`, up to `max`: `COLLIDE_SKIN` short of a hit.
- `slide` (function): Where a ball of `COLLIDE_RADIUS` gets from `from` toward `to`, sliding along up to three surfaces it meets: it stops `COLLIDE_SKIN` short of each and moves on along it; a ball already within the skin of one is first lifted off it.
- `sweep` (function): Where a ball of `COLLIDE_RADIUS` gets from `from` toward `to`: `to`, or twice the skin short of the first surface.
- `TRAIL_KEEP` (const): The nearest to the base a trail's point a camera heads for stands by default, m: it never closes in on him so.
- `TRAIL_LENGTH` (const): How much of its base's way a camera's trail keeps, m.
- `TRAIL_STEP` (const): How far apart the points of a camera's trail of its base stand, m.
- `Walls` (interface): The walls a camera keeps out of: the sim's queries, the groups that stop it and a body it passes through.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts)

- `CAMERA_FIELDS` (const): A game camera's fields.
- `CAMERA_NAMES` (const): Every name the engine's cameras and views take: a game's camera takes another.
- `cameraEntry` (function): The game camera named `name` on `registry`, or undefined.
- `CameraKindSpec` (interface): What `defineCamera` takes: `create` makes the camera from its code and the camera before it.
- `defineCamera` (function): Adds a game's camera mode on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `GAME_CAMERA_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `madeCamera` (function): What a game camera's `create` returned, checked: a camera, else `GFX_BAD_GAME_CAMERA` naming the camera.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/effects.ts)

- `apexFov` (function): The lens (vertical degrees) of Apex's field of view `h`: horizontal degrees at 4:3.
- `applyEffects` (function): `pose` with the effects of `frame` on it, each part scaled by `weights` (see the file comment).
- `CAMERA_EYE` (const): The eye's height over the feet on the shooter model, m: Apex's, standing and crouched.
- `CameraEffects` (interface): The effects' state (see the file comment).
- `cameraPlayer` (function): What the cameras read of the player actor `entity` (`actor`, and `motion` on the shooter model); null for another.
- `CameraPlayer` (interface): What the effects and the follow cameras read of the player after a sim step: plain data.
- `createCameraEffects` (function): The effects' springs and phases (see the file comment).
- `crouchShare` (function): How far a shooter model's duck has gone down, 0 standing to 1 crouched, from its `motion` (WP 13.5's duck).
- `EFFECTS` (const): The effects' numbers (see the file comment): metres, radians, seconds.
- `EffectsFrame` (interface): One frame of the effects (see the file comment).
- `EffectWeights` (interface): How much of each effect a camera takes, 0 to 1 (see the file comment).
- `FIRST_EFFECTS` (const): First person's: every effect.
- `NO_EFFECTS` (const): None: the views, the orbit, the free cameras.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/first.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/first.ts)

- `createFirstCamera` (function): A first-person camera: at the hero's eyes (`input.eye`), turned by the devices; it takes every view effect.
- `CullOptions` (interface): Options for `nearBodyCull`.
- `describeFirst` (function): A first-person camera in words.
- `eyePoint` (function): The head socket: the midpoint of the eye sockets of `skeleton` posed as `world` (engine/anim/fk.ts), m.
- `FIRST_ARMS` (const): The joints first person's viewmodel draws as the arms (engine/gfx/viewmodel/).
- `FIRST_BOB_LAG` (const): The time constant of the eye's height, real seconds: it softens the head's bob.
- `FIRST_DEFAULTS` (const): The starting pitch (rad, + up) and lens (degrees, `PerspectiveCamera.fov`).
- `FIRST_EYE_HEIGHT` (const): The eye's height above the followed point without a rig, m.
- `FIRST_KICK` (const): The joints it draws as a kick's leg, while the body kicks.
- `FIRST_NEAR_BODY` (const): A shown part closer to the eye than this is culled too, m.
- `FIRST_SHOWN` (const): The joints whose parts the camera shows (unless near the eye): the hands, which hold the weapons.
- `FIRST_TRAIL` (const): The most the eye's height trails the eye, m: a fall or a climb is followed, and a stop never overshot.
- `FIRST_TURN_SPEED` (const): Turn rates at full `input.turn`, rad/s: `[right, up]`.
- `firstBodyCull` (function): The joints the body hides from a first-person camera at `eye`, whose arms the viewmodel draws (see the file comment): every one; with `fullBody`, the head, the arms and those near the eye (`nearBodyCull`).
- `FirstInput` (interface): A first-person camera's input: the devices', and the hero's eye.
- `FirstOptions` (interface): Options for a first-person camera: its code's data, and the camera before it.
- `firstPose` (function): The first-person camera's pose: at the eye, looking along its yaw and pitch.
- `firstSpec` (function): The first-person camera's code data.
- `FirstSpec` (interface): A first-person camera's code as data: without the numbers it looks where the camera before it looked.
- `firstState` (function): A checked first-person state for `options`.
- `FirstState` (interface): A first-person camera's state: plain data, replaced by each step.
- `formatFirstCode` (function): The canonical code of a first-person camera's data (numbers rounded to 0.01°).
- `nearBodyCull` (function): Near-body culling: the joints, in `JOINTS` order, whose body parts a first-person camera at `eye` hides from the character `skeleton` posed as `world`: those not in `options.show`, the head, and those whose part comes within `options.near` of the eye (see the file comment).
- `parseFirstCode` (function): Reads a first-person camera's code: `cam3=first[,<yaw>,<pitch>[,<fov>]]`.
- `stepFirst` (function): Steps a first-person camera by one rendered frame: turned by `look` and `turn`, `zoom` on the lens, at the eye.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/fixed.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/fixed.ts)

- `createFixedCamera` (function): A fixed camera: at `position`, else where `from` (the camera on screen) is, else at eye height over the origin.
- `FixedOptions` (interface): Options for a fixed camera: its code's data, and the pose to fix when the code has no position.
- `fixedPose` (function): The fixed camera's pose.
- `fixedSpec` (function): The fixed camera's code data.
- `fixedState` (function): A checked fixed state for `options`: the code's place, else `from`'s, else the origin at eye height.
- `FixedState` (interface): A fixed camera's state: plain data.
- `stepFixed` (function): Steps a fixed camera: only `input.zoom` changes it (its lens).

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/fly.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/fly.ts)

- `createFlyCamera` (function): A fly camera: at `position`, else where `from` (the camera before it) was, else at eye height over the origin.
- `FLY_FAST_SPEED` (const): Flying speed with `input.fast`, m/s (the prototype's 170 units/s).
- `FLY_FOV` (const): The fly camera's lens, degrees (`PerspectiveCamera.fov`).
- `FLY_FOV_RANGE` (const): The lens range of zoom steps, degrees.

- `FlyOptions` (interface): Options for a fly camera: its code's data, a pose to start from when the code has no position, and bounds.

- `flyState` (function): A checked fly state for `options`.
- `FlyState` (interface): A fly camera's state: plain data, replaced by each step.
- `stepFly` (function): Steps a fly camera by one rendered frame: turned by `look` and `turn`, moved by `move`, its lens by `zoom`.

- `FollowInput` (interface): A follow camera's input: the devices', the hero (his eye and what he does) and the walls.
- `FollowOptions` (interface): Options for a follow camera: its code's data, the lens, and the camera before it.
- `followPose` (function): The follow camera's pose: where its ball stands (the arm back from the pivot), looking along its view.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/place.ts)

- `AnyCamera` (type): Any camera `createCamera` makes: codes.ts's (`Camera`), or a follow camera, whose inputs add the hero's.
- `AnyCameraSpec` (type): The code data of any camera: codes.ts's, a follow camera's, or a game camera's.
- `CameraPair` (interface): One three.js camera per projection, and `place`, which aims the one a pose needs.

- `createCameraPair` (function): A perspective and an orthographic camera, made once (see the file comment).
- `FOLLOW_CAMERAS` (re-export): (undocumented)
- `GameCameraSpec` (interface): A game's own camera's code (engine/gfx/cameras/define.ts): its name and the code its `create` reads.

- `readCameraCode` (function): Reads any camera's code: a follow camera's (`cam3=chase…`, `cam3=first…`, `cam3=rail…`, `cam3=shoulder…`, `cam3=follow…`) by its module, a game camera's (`defineCamera`) as its name and code, every other by `parseCameraCode`.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts)

- `approach` (function): Exponential smoothing toward `to`: `k` = 1 − e^(−dt/τ) moves the same share per second at any frame rate.
- `Camera` (interface): A camera: its state, stepped once per rendered frame, and its pose.
- `cameraFrom` (function): Wraps a camera's pure steps and its first state in a `Camera` (the factories use it).
- `CameraInput` (interface): What the devices give a camera in a frame; every field is optional (orbit and fly turn, fly moves, views zoom).
- `CameraPose` (interface): Where a camera is, where it looks and its lens, in a frame: plain, frozen data (see the file comment).
- `CameraSteps` (interface): The steps a camera type supplies to `cameraFrom`.
- `frameSize` (function): The picture's size at the camera's target, m: the frustum (orthographic), or the lens's frame at `distance`.
- `headingOf` (function): The heading of a camera that stands at `azimuth` round its target and looks at it: azimuth + π, wrapped.
- `lookAt` (function): The yaw, pitch and distance that look from `from` at `to` (as `Object3D.lookAt`); straight up or down keeps yaw 0.
- `makePose` (function): A checked, frozen pose: `fields` over `POSE_DEFAULTS`.
- `orbitPoint` (function): The point at `distance` from `target`, at `azimuth` round it (from +Z toward +X) and `elevation` above its horizon: three.js's `Vector3.setFromSphericalCoords(distance, π/2 − elevation, azimuth)`, added to the target.
- `perspectiveFrom` (function): A perspective framing of `pose` with a `fov` lens: an orthographic pose becomes a camera on the same line of sight to the same target, as far from it as frames the same picture height; a perspective pose keeps its place.
- `pointProblems` (function): A finite point, or a problem.
- `POSE_DEFAULTS` (const): Defaults for the fields `makePose` is not given (the lens is three.js's `PerspectiveCamera` default).
- `poseForward` (function): The unit view direction (three.js's `camera.getWorldDirection()`).
- `poseRight` (function): The unit right direction on screen: forward × up, level whatever the pitch, tipped down by a `roll` (if any).
- `poseTarget` (function): The point the camera looks at: `distance` along its view direction.
- `poseUp` (function): The unit up direction on screen: right × forward (the heading when the camera looks straight down), tipped right by a `roll`.
- `Projection` (type): The two projections three.js has: `PerspectiveCamera` and `OrthographicCamera`.
- `rangeProblems` (function): A problem for each value that is missing, not finite, or outside `[min, max]`.
- `refuse` (function): Throws `GFX_BAD_CAMERA` for `where` when `problems` is not empty.
- `Vec3` (type): A point or direction, world space, m: `[x, y, z]`.
- `wrapAngle` (function): `angle` wrapped into (−π, π].

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/presets.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/presets.ts)

- `createViewCamera` (function): A classic view as a `Camera` (`options.view` names it; codes.ts's `VIEW_LABELS` has the names in words).
- `ORTHO_DISTANCE` (const): How far back an orthographic view stands from its target, m, and how far it sees.
- `ORTHO_FAR` (const): An orthographic view's far plane, m.
- `stepView` (function): Steps a view by one rendered frame: zoom steps, 45° turns, and the target following `input.follow`.
- `stepZoom` (function): The next zoom step from `zoom`, `steps` up (+) or down (−) `zooms` (`VIEW_ZOOMS`).
- `VIEW_FOV` (const): A view's perspective lens, degrees (`PerspectiveCamera.fov`).
- `VIEW_LAG` (const): The time constant of a view's follow, real seconds (the 2D camera's lag).
- `VIEW_LIFT` (const): How high above the followed point a view looks, m.
- `VIEW_PRESETS` (const): The classic views, from the 2D engine's `E.VIEWS`; `custom` holds a custom view's defaults.
- `VIEW_TRAIL` (const): The most a view's target trails the followed point, m: a fall is followed, and a stop never overshot.
- `VIEW_ZOOMS` (const): The zoom steps `input.zoom` moves through.
- `ViewOptions` (interface): Options for a view beyond its code: the lens and the frame.
- `viewPose` (function): A view's pose (see the file comment for the framing).
- `ViewPreset` (interface): One classic view: where it stands, how many pixels a metre takes in its picture, and its height boost.
- `viewSpec` (function): A view's code data: a custom view's angles and boost, or a preset's name and turn.
- `viewState` (function): A checked view state for `options` (a view's code data, plus the lens and frame).
- `ViewState` (interface): A view camera's state: plain data, replaced (never changed) by each step.
- `WHOLE_STEPS` (const): The overhead view's zoom steps: whole numbers, so its pixels stay square.

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/rail.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/rail.ts)

- `createRailCamera` (function): A depth rail: beside the hero, following `input.follow` along the rail and keeping him within near and far.

- `CAMERA_SETTING_FIELDS` (const): The view settings the rig reads (see the file comment), as fields; never in the hash.
- `CAMERA_SETTINGS` (const): The view settings the rig reads, declared on the shared registry.

- `createCameraRig` (function): Makes a rig on the camera `code` names (see the file comment).

- `RigOptions` (interface): The rig's options (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts`](../engine/gfx/cameras/shoulder.ts)

- `createShoulderCamera` (function): A shoulder camera: over the hero's shoulder (`input.eye`), turned by the devices, in front of the walls.
- `describeShoulder` (function): A shoulder camera in words.
- `formatShoulderCode` (function): The canonical code of a shoulder camera's data (numbers rounded: 0.01°, 0.001 m; the side only when left).

- `SHOULDER` (const): The rig's numbers (see the file comment): metres and real seconds; `lens` its own lens, degrees (Apex's 90 at 4:3).
