- `SHOULDER_TURN_SPEED` (const): Turn rates at full `input.turn`, rad/s: `[right, up]`.
- `ShoulderInput` (interface): A shoulder camera's input: the devices', the hero's eye and the walls.
- `ShoulderOptions` (interface): Options for a shoulder camera: its code's data, the lens, and the camera before it.
- `shoulderPose` (function): The shoulder camera's pose: where its ball stands (the arm back from the shoulder point), looking along the view.
- `shoulderSpec` (function): The shoulder camera's code data.

### [`engine/gfx/caps.ts`](../engine/gfx/caps.ts)

- `adapterLimits` (function): The adapter's limits, by name: what `requestDevice` asks for.

- `GfxCaps` (interface): The GPU as the engine reports it: the adapter's identity, the device's features and limits.

### [`engine/gfx/cutaway.ts`](../engine/gfx/cutaway.ts)

- `AIM_STEEP` (const): Looking down at least this steeply (rad, 60°), only the hero's head and feet are aimed at, not the floor round him.
- `createCutaway` (function): Gives `meshes`' cutting parts their twins (see the file comment), and fades `options.objects` too.
- `CUT_AIMS` (const): The points aimed at (m): the head and the feet above the focus, and the floor this far round it.
- `CUT_FACING` (const): A wall is cut when the cosine between its outward direction and the way to the camera is above this.
- `CUT_MARGIN` (const): How far round a blocking piece's box a line of sight still counts as through it (m): 4 prototype units.
- `CUT_STEEP` (const): Looking down steeper than this (rad, 85°), the camera sees over every wall: none is cut.
- `Cutaway` (interface): A level's cutaway (see the file comment).
- `cutawayAims` (function): The points the camera must see, round `focus`, for a camera at `pitch` (rad): the hero's head and feet, and unless it looks down `AIM_STEEP` or more, the floor `CUT_AIMS.around` metres round him, where the fight is.
- `CutawayOptions` (interface): What `createCutaway` takes beside the meshes.
- `CutawayReport` (interface): How many of each cutting part's pieces are cut, after an `update`, and what the fade took out of the picture.
- `CutTarget` (interface): What the cutaway decides over: the pieces of one part, how they cut, and their heights (m).
- `FADE_AIMS` (const): The points the fade keeps in sight above the focus (m), and how far inside a box a line must pass to fade it.
- `FADE_THIN` (const): A ride part thinner than this, m (its geometry's least extent): a cable, a rail, a rung or a pole hides no one.
- `planCutaway` (function): For each target, for each cell: whether `pose`, looking at `focus`, cuts it.
- `planFade` (function): For each target, for each cell, whether a line from `pose` to the head or the chest over `focus` (`FADE_AIMS`) passes through the cell's box, shrunk by `FADE_AIMS.inset`: an orthographic camera looks from its plane, as in `planCutaway`.
- `segmentHitsBox` (function): Whether the segment `a` → `b` passes through the box `min`–`max` (slabs; the prototype's `segBox`).

### [`engine/gfx/daylight.ts`](../engine/gfx/daylight.ts)

- `DAYLIGHT` (const): The key skies by the hour (0 to 24): between two, the sky eases from one to the next.
- `daylightAt` (function): The sky at `hour` (see the file comment): the key skies about it blended, the light where `lightAt` puts it.
- `defineDaylight` (function): Declares the key skies on `registry`, unless it has them, the backdrop sky:daylight's under each key's tint.
- `lightAt` (function): Where the light stands at `hour` (radians, as a sky's sun takes them), how strongly it shines (0 to 1), and whose.
- `SUN` (const): The sun's day (hours): it rises at `rise` and sets at `set`; the moon has the rest.

### [`engine/gfx/enhanced/aa.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/aa.ts)

- `createTemporalAa` (function): Makes the smoothing (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/features.ts`](../engine/gfx/features.ts)

- `AirLights` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/air.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/air.ts)): What the march reads of the scene, as uniforms and textures, gathered each frame (see the file comment).
- `CascadedSun` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/csm.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/csm.ts)): A sun casting through cascades (see the file comment).
- `cascadeSunFor` (function): Makes `sun` cast through cascades (engine/gfx/enhanced/csm.ts, WP 11.5) when `feature:cascadedShadows` is on in `report`; null otherwise (and with no report), so it casts its one shadow map.
- `defineFeatures` (function): Declares the kind `feature`, the built-in features and `gfx.featuresOff` on `registry`, unless it has them.
- `FEATURE_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `feature` entry.
- `FEATURE_SETTINGS` (const): The gfx settings this module reads; all are view settings, never in the hash.
- `FeatureEntry` (type): A `feature` entry.
- `FeatureOff` (interface): One feature that is off: its id, the advice raised and why.
- `FeatureReport` (interface): What `resolveFeatures` found: the features on, those off and why, and the downgrades as advice codes.
- `FEATURES_CODES` (const): The advice codes of the built-in features, with their fixes.
- `GpuParticles` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/particles.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/particles.ts)): GPU particles (see the file comment).
- `gpuParticlesFor` (function): The GPU's particle ring's maker (engine/gfx/enhanced/particles.ts, WP 11.3) when `feature:gpuParticles` is on in `report`, else null (and with no report): the CPU pool takes every emitter's particles.
- `GpuTiming` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/timing.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/timing.ts)): A renderer's GPU timing (see the file comment).
- `gpuTimingFor` (function): The GPU timing a renderer gets (engine/gfx/enhanced/timing.ts, WP 11.2): measuring when `feature:timestamps` is on in `report`, which also says whether to make the renderer with `trackTimestamp`; idle (no `gpuMs`) when it is off.
- `lightingFor` (function): Gives `renderer` tiled lighting (engine/gfx/enhanced/lighting.ts, WP 11.5) when `feature:tiledLighting` is on in `report`, before its first frame; returns the light pool a sky on it may make: `TILED.pool` lights tiled, else the pool's default.
- `lightPoolOf` (function): The light pool a sky may make on a renderer whose features are `report` (none: the pool's default).
- `LightPoolSize` (interface): The light pool a renderer lights: how many lights, and whether tiled lighting lets it pass `POOL_SIZES.max`.
- `Occlusion` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/ao.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/ao.ts)): The occlusion pass (see the file comment).
- `Reflections` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/ssr.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/ssr.ts)): The reflections (see the file comment).
- `resolveFeatures` (function): Checks every `feature` entry against `caps` and `gfx.featuresOff`, raises each off feature's advice once, and reports what is on and off.
- `sceneTargetsFor` (function): The scene pass's extra targets the techniques on in `report` read, for a chain smoothing with `aa` (mrt.ts).
- `shadingFor` (function): The shading techniques whose features are on in `report` (none without a report).
- `ShadingTechniques` (interface): The post chain's shading techniques a renderer whose features are `report` has (engine/gfx/post/shading.ts).
- `shellsOn` (function): Whether the stage makes outline shells (engine/gfx/stageShells.ts): `feature:shells` on in `report`, or no report.
- `TemporalAa` (interface from [`engine/gfx/enhanced/aa.ts`](../engine/gfx/enhanced/aa.ts)): The smoothing (see the file comment).
- `temporalAaFor` (function): TRAA (engine/gfx/enhanced/aa.ts) when `feature:traa` is on in `report`, else null (the chain smooths with FXAA).

### [`engine/gfx/fx/decals.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/decals.ts)

- `createDecals` (function): Makes the decals; see the file comment.
- `DECAL` (const): How far above the floor a decal lies (m), and how wide its rim is (m).
- `decalMaterial` (function): The decals' material: see the file comment.
- `Decals` (interface): The decals of a frame: see the file comment.
- `DecalsOptions` (interface): What `createDecals` takes.

### [`engine/gfx/fx/effects.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/effects.ts)

- `BOLT` (const): How a bolt looks: the Stress test's hero bolt by default.
- `createEffects` (function): Makes the effects; see the file comment.
- `Effects` (interface): The effects of a view: see the file comment.
- `EffectsOptions` (interface): What `createEffects` takes.
- `FX_BUDGET` (const): The pools' sizes: see the file comment.
- `FxStats` (interface): What `stats()` reports.

### [`engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/emitters.ts)

- `defineEmitter` (function): Defines an emitter on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `Emitter` (type): An `emitter` entry: see the file comment.
- `EMITTER_FIELDS` (const): The fields of an `emitter` entry.
- `emitterKind` (function): Declares the kind `emitter` on `registry`, with the engine's emitters, unless it has it.
- `EmitterLayer` (interface): One layer of an emitter, filled.
- `EmitterSpec` (type): What `defineEmitter` takes: any field; of `ring` and `light`, any key.
- `FxLight` (interface): A light of the frame, as three.js's `PointLight` takes it.
- `getEmitter` (function): The emitter `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `emitter:sparks`, with a warning.
- `lightLevel` (function): Shardfall's flicker and pulse of an object light at time `t` from `seed`, times `intensity`.
- `PARTICLE_FIELDS` (const): How particles start, move and look: an emitter's own fields, and what a layer may change (`set`).
- `ParticleFields` (type): The particle fields as an emitter entry holds them.
- `particleSpec` (function): `entry`'s particle fields with `set`'s changes, as the pool takes them; cached per entry and `set` object.
- `ParticleSpec` (interface): What the particle pool takes: an emitter's particle fields as numbers, colours linear (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/fx/particles.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/particles.ts)

- `BurstOptions` (interface): How a burst differs from its spec.
- `BurstPlan` (interface): What every particle of one burst shares: its scale, origin, added velocity, floor and colours (`planBurst`).
- `PARTICLE_FLOATS` (const): The floats a particle keeps, by name: offsets into its stride.
- `PARTICLE_STRIDE` (const): Floats per particle.
- `ParticleBounds` (interface): The box round live particles (m).
- `ParticlePool` (class): The CPU particle pool: see the file comment.
- `ParticleRing` (interface): What bursts the particles of an emitter whose entry says `gpu`, as the effects meet it: the GPU's ring (engine/gfx/enhanced/particles.ts, WP 11.3), moved by `update` and counted by `stats` as the pool is.
- `ParticleStats` (interface): What a pool did.
- `ParticleView` (interface): A particle as the drawing reads it.
- `planBurst` (function): The plan of a burst of `spec` at `origin` (m) as `options` change it (see the file comment).
- `writeParticle` (function): Writes one particle of a burst into `d` from float `o` (a slot's first, `PARTICLE_STRIDE` floats), drawing from `rng` in a fixed order: its place in the area, its direction in the unit ball, its life, and its age when prewarmed.

### [`engine/gfx/fx/payload.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/payload.ts)

- `eventOptions` (function): The burst options an event's payload asks for (see the file comment).
- `eventPosition` (function): Where an event happens (see the file comment), or null.
- `FxEventPayload` (interface): What an event carries for its effects (any other keys are left alone).

### [`engine/gfx/fx/presets.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/presets.ts)

- `BUILT_IN_EMITTERS` (const): The engine's emitters, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/fx/ribbons.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/ribbons.ts)

- `createRibbons` (function): Makes the ribbons; see the file comment.
- `Ribbons` (interface): The ribbons of a frame: see the file comment.
- `RibbonsOptions` (interface): What `createRibbons` takes.
- `TRAIL_TINTS` (const): The tints of the Stress test's trails: the hero's blade and the monsters' claws.
- `TrailSampleLike` (interface): One sample of a trail: where the part's base and tip were, and its ribbon's weight (1).

### [`engine/gfx/fx/rings.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/rings.ts)

- `createRings` (function): Makes the rings: at most `capacity` at once.
- `Rings` (interface): The floor rings (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/fx/shake.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/shake.ts)

- `ScreenShake` (class): Camera shake: see the file comment.
- `SHAKE` (const): The shake's tuning: the 2D engine's, in metres.

### [`engine/gfx/fx/sprites.ts`](../engine/gfx/fx/sprites.ts)

- `createSprites` (function): Makes the sprites; see the file comment.
- `spriteMaterial` (function): The sprites' material: see the file comment.
- `Sprites` (interface): The sprites of a frame: see the file comment.
- `SpritesOptions` (interface): What `createSprites` takes.
- `STREAK` (const): How far a streak reaches per m/s of its speed across the view, seconds: its length is `size + speed × STREAK`.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/box.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/box.ts)

- `boxGeometry` (function): A box standing on the ground, UVs in metres (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/builtins.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/builtins.ts)

- `BUILT_IN_GEOMETRY` (const): The kit's entries by id, as `defineGeometry` specs.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/checks.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/checks.ts)

- `assertSegments` (function): Throws `GFX_BAD_GEOMETRY` unless `value` is a whole number of segments of at least `min`.
- `assertSizes` (function): Throws `GFX_BAD_GEOMETRY` unless every size is a finite number above 0 (or, with `orZero`, at least 0).
- `badGeometry` (function): Throws `GFX_BAD_GEOMETRY` for `shape` with `problem`, naming what to pass.
- `GEOMETRY_CODES` (const): The codes the geometry kit raises, with their fixes.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/frustum.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/frustum.ts)

- `frustumGeometry` (function): A frustum standing on the ground (see the file comment).
- `FrustumOptions` (interface): A frustum's sizes in metres and its tessellation.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/geometry.ts)

- `buildGeometry` (function): Builds geometry `ref` (an id, or `{ geometry, params }`) from `registry` (the shared one by default): a new `BufferGeometry` the caller owns and disposes.
- `defineGeometry` (function): Defines a geometry on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `GEOMETRY_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `geometry` entry.
- `GeometryEntry` (type): A `geometry` entry: one builder.
- `geometryKind` (function): Declares the kind `geometry` on `registry`, with the kit's built-in shapes, unless it has it.
- `GeometryRef` (interface): A geometry by id with parameters: what a prop's or a level's `geometry` field may hold beside a bare id.
- `GeometrySpec` (interface): What `defineGeometry` takes: the entry's fields (`params` and `budget` have defaults), `create` typed by `params`.
- `getGeometry` (function): The geometry `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `geometry:box`, with a warning.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/groups.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/groups.ts)

- `mergeGeometries` (function): Joins `geometries` into one, in order: their attributes end to end, their indices offset.
- `sidesThenTops` (function): Sorts the triangles of `geometry` into its sides (group 0, material 0) then its tops and bottoms (group 1, material 1), and returns it (changed in place).

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/inspect.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/inspect.ts)

- `DEGENERATE_AREA` (const): A triangle smaller than this (m²) is degenerate.
- `GeometryReport` (interface): What `inspectGeometry` measured.
- `inspectGeometry` (function): Measures `geometry` (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/limb.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/limb.ts)

- `limbGeometry` (function): A tapered limb from the origin up +Y (see the file comment).
- `LimbOptions` (interface): A tapered limb's sizes in metres and its tessellation.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/pillar.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/pillar.ts)

- `pillarGeometry` (function): A pillar as one geometry standing on the ground: its parts' boxes, sides then tops.
- `PillarOptions` (interface): A pillar's footprint and height in metres.
- `PillarPart` (interface): One part of a pillar: a square slab `width` across, from height `from` to `to` (m).
- `pillarParts` (function): A pillar's parts, bottom to top (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/ramp.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/ramp.ts)

- `rampGeometry` (function): A ramp or wedge standing on the ground, rising towards +Z (see the file comment).
- `RampOptions` (interface): A ramp's sizes in metres.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/ring.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/ring.ts)

- `ringGeometry` (function): A ring lying on the ground (see the file comment).
- `RingOptions` (interface): A ring's radii and height in metres, and its tessellation.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/roundedBox.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/roundedBox.ts)

- `roundedBoxGeometry` (function): A rounded box standing on the ground (see the file comment).
- `RoundedBoxOptions` (interface): A rounded box's size and rounding, in metres.

### [`engine/gfx/geometry/writer.ts`](../engine/gfx/geometry/writer.ts)

- `createWriter` (function): Makes an empty writer.
- `cross` (function): `a × b`.
- `dot` (function): `a · b`.
- `normalize` (function): `a` scaled to length 1 (the zero vector stays zero).
- `ProfilePoint` (interface): One ring of a lathe's profile: its radius and height, its normal in the (radial, y) plane, and its v (m).
- `Vec3` (type): A point or direction in metres: `[x, y, z]`.
- `Writer` (interface): What the builders write with.

### [`engine/gfx/idmarks.ts`](../engine/gfx/idmarks.ts)

- `drawMarks` (function): Draws each mark onto a frame of RGBA bytes (top row first): a ring around `at` and the number in a dark box above it (below it at the top edge), at 2 × scale.
- `Mark` (interface): A numbered mark on what the ID pass sees, for the legend.
- `marksOf` (function): Numbers the visible objects, largest first: at most `max` (40), each covering at least `minPx` (4) pixels.

### [`engine/gfx/idpass.ts`](../engine/gfx/idpass.ts)

- `decodeIds` (function): Decodes an ID-pass readback (RGBA, top row first) into the result, and each pixel's visible object (1-based).
- `Drawable` (interface): A drawable object of the scene, as the ID pass knows it.
- `idColour` (function): The ID colour of the `n`-th drawable (1-based): an odd multiple modulo 2^24, so distinct and never 0.
- `IdEntry` (interface): One visible object: its pixels, share of the frame, bounding box `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` (inclusive, from the top left).
- `IdPass` (interface): The ID pass's result: every drawable object, visible or not.
- `IdTable` (interface): The drawables of a scene, with their colours.
- `IdUnseen` (interface): One object drawn in no pixel, and why.
- `listDrawables` (function): Lists the scene's drawable objects with their colours, and why the hidden and out-of-view ones cannot be seen.
- `UnseenReason` (type): Why a drawable object covers no pixel.
- `withIdScene` (function): Runs `draw(root)` with `root` a stand-in for `scene` that draws the ID pass: it shares the scene's children, has no background, and overrides every material with the ID material reading `table`; the clear colour is transparent black meanwhile.

### [`engine/gfx/instancing.ts`](../engine/gfx/instancing.ts)

- `createInstancedBatch` (function): Makes an instanced batch (see the file comment).
- `INSTANCE_SYNC` (const): What importing this module did to r182's `InstanceNode` (see `syncBeforeUpload`): `patched` is true on r182.
- `InstanceColor` (type): A colour: three.js's `Color` (linear `r`, `g`, `b`) or linear `[r, g, b]`.
- `InstancedBatch` (interface): An instanced batch (see the file comment).
- `InstancedBatchOptions` (interface): How `createInstancedBatch` makes a batch.
- `InstancedBatchStats` (type): A batch's pages, slots and instances, and the pages and bytes its last `end()` uploaded.
- `instancePath` (function): Where r182 reads an instanced mesh's matrices from, for a mesh of `slots` slots (see the file comment).
- `INSTANCING_CODES` (const): The codes the instancing service raises, with their fixes.
- `PAGE_SLOTS` (const): The default page size: above `UNIFORM_INSTANCE_LIMIT`, so every page shares one shader.
- `syncBeforeUpload` (function): Makes r182's `InstanceNode` sync its buffers' versions before the renderer uploads them (see the file comment): every instance node gets an `updateBefore` that runs its own `update` once per render.
- `UNIFORM_INSTANCE_LIMIT` (const): r182's threshold: up to this many slots, an instanced mesh's matrices go to a uniform buffer (a shader per mesh).

### [`engine/gfx/level/brazier.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/brazier.ts)

- `brazierGeometry` (function): The stands on `pieces` of `level`, from `bottom` to `top` (m), and the ground under them (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/level/cells.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/cells.ts)

- `LevelCell` (interface): One piece of a block mesh: its tiles, its centre on the ground (m), its size across (m), and the way it faces out ([x, z], length 1).
- `levelCells` (function): The cells of `pieces` in `level`, standing at height `bottom` (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/level/dais.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/dais.ts)

- `daisGeometry` (function): The daises `daises`, and the ground at `ground` over `pieces` (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/level/faces.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/faces.ts)

- `Ground` (type): A point on the ground (m): `[x, z]`.
- `polygon` (function): Writes the flat polygon `points` (a fan from the first) with `uvs`, facing `outward`: its points are taken in the other order when they wind against it.
- `slotted` (function): Makes an empty set of slot writers (see the file comment).
- `Slotted` (interface): One writer per material slot, joined by `build` into one geometry with a draw group per slot used.
- `tread` (function): Writes the level rectangle `[x0, z0, x1, z1]` at height `y`, facing up.
- `upright` (function): Writes the upright quad over the ground edge `a` → `b` from height `y0` to `y1`.

### [`engine/gfx/level/flights.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/flights.ts)

- `flightGeometry` (function): The flights of `ramps`, standing on their storey's floor at `ground` (m), tiles `tile` metres wide.
- `RISER` (const): A house stair's riser (m): about 7 inches.
- `risersOf` (function): How many steps a flight climbs: its rise in `RISER`s, at least one.

### [`engine/gfx/level/meshes.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/meshes.ts)

- `createLevelMeshes` (function): Draws `level`'s mesh descriptors (see the file comment).
- `LEVEL_MESH_CODES` (const): The codes the level meshes raise, with their fixes.
- `LevelMeshes` (interface): A level's meshes (see the file comment).
- `LevelMeshesOptions` (interface): What `createLevelMeshes` needs: where materials come from, and optionally more recipes and a log.
- `LevelMeshPart` (interface): One level mesh: its descriptor's recipe and glyphs, the mesh, and for an instanced shape one cell per instance.
- `meshDrawCalls` (function): The draw calls `mesh` costs a frame: its groups (one with a single material), once in colour and once per shadow map when it casts; none while it is hidden or an instanced mesh with no instances.

### [`engine/gfx/level/openings.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/openings.ts)

- `boxBetween` (function): A box from `[x0, y0, z0]` to `[x1, y1, z1]` (m), UVs in metres.
- `FRAME` (const): A frame's width round an opening (m).
- `framesGeometry` (function): The frame round each of `openings` (see the file comment); null when there are none.
- `headsGeometry` (function): The wall over `storey`'s openings and low ceilings (see the file comment), `roof` its pitched roof when it has one; null when it has none.
- `POST_GAP` (const): How far apart a railing's posts stand, at most (m).
- `PROUD` (const): How far a frame stands out of the wall's faces (m), so its faces never share the wall's.
- `railingGeometry` (function): A railing along each run of `pieces` (tiles `tile` m wide), from `bottom` to `top` (m); null when there are none.

### [`engine/gfx/level/ramp.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/ramp.ts)

- `rampGeometry` (function): The wedges of `ramps`, standing on the ground at `ground` (m), tiles `tile` metres wide (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/level/recipes.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/recipes.ts)

- `CutWhen` (type): When the cutaway cuts a piece: `'facing'`, when the camera stands on the side the piece faces out to (walls); `'blocking'`, when it stands between the camera and what the camera follows (pillars); `'either'`, both (a house's walls: a wall with rooms on both sides faces no one way out, so one between the camera and the player is cut too).
- `FALLBACK_RECIPE` (const): What a recipe nobody defined draws: grey blocks (`material:default`), casting and receiving shadows.
- `LEVEL_RECIPES` (const): The engine's recipes, by the name a glyph's `mesh` gives.
- `LevelCut` (interface): How the cutaway cuts a recipe's pieces: to a twin `height` metres tall, `when` the view needs it.
- `LevelRecipe` (interface): A level mesh recipe: its shape, materials, shadows and cut.
- `LevelShape` (type): How a recipe draws its pieces, with what each material slot draws: - `surface`: one welded surface over the pieces at their bottom height, facing up, UVs in metres along X and -Z (one draw call): the floor.

### [`engine/gfx/level/roofs.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/roofs.ts)

- `roofGeometry` (function): The roof's slab (see the file comment): tops in slot 0, undersides and edges in slot 1.

### [`engine/gfx/level/runs.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/runs.ts)

- `levelLooks` (function): The looks the level `id` of `registry` gives its meshes; none for an id it lacks.
- `LevelLooks` (interface): A level's looks, its entry's presentation fields (engine/world/level/level.ts): swaps, rooms' floors, recipes.
- `runMeshes` (function): The level's meshes, each run named by its tiles (see the file comment).
- `RunMeshesOptions` (interface): How `runMeshes` draws: the materials, the level's looks (`LevelLooks`) and where advice goes.
- `splitRuns` (function): The level with each block descriptor split into one descriptor per run (merged rectangle), surfaces whole, and for each descriptor the run it draws (null for one that was not split).

### [`engine/gfx/level/shapes.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/shapes.ts)

- `buildShape` (function): Builds `descriptor`'s mesh in `recipe`'s shape, with `materials` (the recipe's, compiled).
- `BuiltShape` (interface): One descriptor's mesh, its cells (one per instance; none for a single mesh) and its cut.
- `drawnWith` (function): Each slot's material: `materials` one per slot, a slot past the last taking the last; the first for the whole when there is one, or the geometry has no slots (a surface).
- `instanced` (function): One instance per cell, standing at the cell's centre.
- `instanceSlots` (function): The slots of an instanced level mesh of `count` pieces: at least `PAGE_SLOTS`, so it shares its shader.
- `PartCut` (interface): How the cutaway cuts a part: its recipe's cut, and the geometry of its twin (a new one each call).
- `placeInstances` (function): Stands `mesh`'s instances on `cells`, as many as there are, and refits its bounds.

### [`engine/gfx/level/slab.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/slab.ts)

- `slabGeometry` (function): A raised block over `pieces` from `bottom` to `top` (m), tiles `tile` metres wide (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/level/slabs.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/slabs.ts)

- `ceilingGeometry` (function): The underside and void edges of `storey`'s slab (see the file comment), or null when there is nothing to draw.

### [`engine/gfx/level/stairs.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/stairs.ts)

- `frameOf` (function): A ramp's frame on the ground: the point `s` metres up its run and `w` metres across it (from its left side, seen climbing), so the flight is written once for the four ways a ramp can rise (engine/gfx/level/ramp.ts's wedge too).
- `runOf` (function): The ramp's run (m), along the way it rises.
- `stairsGeometry` (function): The flights of `ramps`, standing on the ground at `ground` (m), tiles `tile` metres wide (see the file comment), each in `steps(ramp, tile)` steps (`stepsOf` by default; a storey's flights rise by the riser: engine/gfx/level/flights.ts).
- `STEP_RUN` (const): The run of one step (m): two steps per metre, as the prototype's two per tile.
- `StepCount` (type): How many steps a ramp's flight is drawn in.
- `stepsOf` (function): How many steps a ramp's flight has: its run in `STEP_RUN`s, at least one.

### [`engine/gfx/level/surface.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/surface.ts)

- `surfaceGeometry` (function): A flat surface at height `y` over every tile of `pieces`, tiles `tile` metres wide (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/level/walls.ts`](../engine/gfx/level/walls.ts)

- `axesOf` (function): A face's UV axes, `u × v` its `normal`: upright, u along it and v up; level, u along X and v along -Z (or +Z facing down); sloped, u level along it and v across it, in its plane.
- `underRoofGeometry` (function): The rectangles `rects` (m, `[x0, z0, x1, z1]`) from `bottom` up to `roof`'s underside, or null when none clears it.
- `writeHull` (function): Writes the convex hull of `points` into `writer`, each face with UVs in metres (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/lights.ts`](../engine/gfx/lights.ts)

- `createLightPool` (function): Makes a light pool of `size` lights (8 to 16, or to 64 on a renderer with tiled lighting, `tiled`; 12 by default).
- `defineLight` (function): Declares a light kind (`light:<tag>`, the tag a level's light spots carry); see `LIGHT_FIELDS`.
- `defineLights` (function): Declares the kind `light` and the built-in light kinds on `registry`, unless it has them.
- `FADE` (const): The share of the cut-off rank over which the last lights chosen fade out.
- `fadeOf` (function): How much a source of `rank` shines when the first left out ranks `cutoff`: 1, fading to 0 at the cut-off.
- `flicker` (function): The prototype's torch flicker at `time` (s), shifted by `phase` (s) and scaled by `amount` (0 is steady).
- `LIGHT_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `light` entry: three.js's `PointLight` parameters, and how the pool treats it.
- `LightEntry` (type): A `light` entry.
- `LightPool` (interface): A fixed pool of point lights; see the file comment.
- `LIGHTS_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `LightSource` (interface): A light source the pool may light: a `light` entry's id and where it shines (m).
- `lightSources` (function): The light sources of a compiled level: one per light spot, of the kind `light:<tag>`.
- `POOL_SIZES` (const): The pool's sizes: the fewest and most lights, the default, and the most with tiled lighting (WP 11.5).
- `PoolLamp` (interface): A lamp the pool may light this frame: a prop's light spot in the world (engine/gfx/props.ts `PropLight`).
- `PoolSlot` (interface): One slot of the pool, as the last `update` left it.
- `Ranking` (interface): What `rankSources` chose: the sources best first, their ranks, and the rank of the first left out.
- `rankSources` (function): The `count` sources that matter most at `focus` (see the file comment); `priorities` default to 1.

### [`engine/gfx/lookMetrics.ts`](../engine/gfx/lookMetrics.ts)

- `judgeLook` (function): The notes on `metrics`, `where` naming the frame in each sentence (`tests/pages/shot.html from cam iso`), and the ID pass's objects, when measured, naming the protagonist: a blank frame fails (and is the only note); the others warn, each with its number, its limit and a fix.
- `LOOK_LIMITS` (const): The limits the notes use (shares in [0, 1], luma spread in [0, 1], the palette in colours).
- `LookIds` (interface): What the ID pass tells the metrics: the visible objects with their shares, and the protagonist, if any.
- `lookMetrics` (function): Measures a frame of row-major RGBA bytes (4 a pixel), with the ID pass's objects when given.
- `LookMetrics` (interface): The look metrics of one frame.
- `LookNote` (interface): A note on a frame: its id, whether it fails, the number and its limit, and the sentence with the fix.

### [`engine/gfx/materials/builtins.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/builtins.ts)

- `BUILT_IN_MATERIALS` (const): The built-in materials, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/materials/compile.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/compile.ts)

- `compileMaterial` (function): The three.js material of `entry`, with `maps` baked from its map (null when it has none).
- `drawnAs` (function): How `entry` is drawn in v1: `basic` when unlit, else `lambert`.
- `DrawnAs` (type): The three.js material class a v1 material compiles to.

### [`engine/gfx/materials/library.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/library.ts)

- `createMaterialLibrary` (function): Makes a material library over `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `MaterialLibrary` (interface): A page's compiled materials and baked maps.

### [`engine/gfx/materials/material.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/material.ts)

- `bakeRefOf` (function): The bake source of a map (what `bakeTexture` takes).
- `defineMaterial` (function): Defines a material on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getMaterial` (function): The material `id` of `registry`; a missing id warns once (`CORE_UNKNOWN_ID`) and gives `material:default`.
- `mapProblems` (function): The problems of a `map` value against `registry`'s textures, one sentence each.
- `MapRef` (interface): A material's map, filled: the texture and how it is baked and shown.
- `MATERIAL_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `material` entry: three.js's classic material parameters, as data.
- `MaterialEntry` (type): A `material` entry.
- `materialKind` (function): Declares the kind `material` (and `texture`, which maps need) on `registry`, with the built-ins, unless it has it.
- `MaterialSpec` (type): What `defineMaterial` takes: any of the fields, each with its default.
- `textureRefOf` (function): A material's `map` filled (null for none).

### [`engine/gfx/materials/nodeCopy.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/nodeCopy.ts)

- `nodeCopy` (function): A node material drawn as `material` is, with an id of its own (null when three.js has none for it).

### [`engine/gfx/materials/outline.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/outline.ts)

- `createOutline` (function): Makes an outline (see the file comment).
- `Outline` (interface): An outline: its material and the shells it gives (see the file comment).
- `OUTLINE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `OUTLINE_MODES` (const): How a shell's vertices are pushed: along their normals, or away from the part's centre.
- `OutlineMode` (type): An outline mode (see `OUTLINE_MODES`).
- `OutlineOptions` (interface): How `createOutline` makes an outline.
- `OutlineShells` (interface): The shells of an instanced batch's pages (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/materials/styles.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/styles.ts)

- `checkStyle` (function): Throws `GFX_UNKNOWN_STYLE` unless `style` is a material style.
- `compileStyled` (function): The three.js material of a lit `entry` in `style` (not `lambert`, which v1 compiles), with `maps` baked from its map and the toon look `toon`.
- `createStyleSet` (function): Makes a style set (see the file comment).
- `FlatStyleLighting` (class): The flat style's light: each light's colour where it reaches (shadow and falloff), with no N·L; ambient as Lambert.
- `MATERIAL_STYLES` (const): The material styles: v1's Lambert, toon, flat and pbr.
- `MaterialStyle` (type): A material style (see `MATERIAL_STYLES`).
- `MeshFlatStyleNodeMaterial` (class): The flat style's material: Lambert's parameters, drawn by `FlatStyleLighting`.
- `STYLE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `STYLE_WARMUP_IDS` (const): The warm-up entries' ids: one per style, then the one that puts every material back; after every other entry.
- `StyleSet` (interface): A page's materials in every style (see the file comment).
- `StyleSetOptions` (interface): How `createStyleSet` makes a set.
- `StyleWarmup` (interface): A style set's part in a warm-up (`attach`): the styles it warms, more added later, all undone by `dispose()`.

### [`engine/gfx/materials/toon.ts`](../engine/gfx/materials/toon.ts)

- `BandedToonLighting` (class): The toon lighting model (see the file comment): banded direct light and a gated rim per light, on Lambert's diffuse scale; indirect light and the environment as Lambert's on the material's shade (it extends three.js's Phong model without specular).
- `bandsOf` (function): A share of light, 0–1, cut into `bands` bands: the levels 0, 1/(bands − 1) … 1, each edge smoothed over about a pixel (`fwidth`) so it never shimmers; 2 bands or fewer is lit wherever the share passes 0.02.
- `bayer4` (function): The 4 × 4 ordered pattern's threshold (0–1, a cell's rank plus a half, over 16) at the whole cell `cell`: the composite's table (engine/gfx/post/shaders/common.ts `post_bayer4`), built from the 2 × 2 order, any cell (negative ones too) in the pattern.
- `createToonUniforms` (function): Makes a look's uniforms, from `TOON_LOOK` and `look`: render-group uniforms, so a still mesh draws a change the next frame (an object-group one waits for its object or material to change, engine/gfx/sky.ts).
- `ditheredBandsOf` (function): A share of light, 0–1, in `bands` hard bands (the levels of `bandsOf`), each step's edge at its middle moved by `threshold` (0–1; 0.5 is the middle), so a threshold from an ordered pattern dithers the edge; 2 bands or fewer is lit wherever the share passes 0.02.
- `gradientToonMaterial` (function): The measured baseline (see the file comment): three.js's toon material with the carried gradient map.
- `gridThreshold` (function): The ordered threshold this fragment takes on `grid` (cells counted from the snapped camera; see the file comment).
- `MeshBandedToonNodeMaterial` (class): The toon material: Lambert's parameters (`color`, `map`, `normalMap`, `emissive`…), drawn by `BandedToonLighting`.
- `SHADE_TINT` (const): What a shade multiplies a colour by before its saturation is raised: cooler, toward violet (see the file comment).
- `shadeOf` (function): A colour's shade (see the file comment): `colour` times `SHADE_TINT`, more saturated, `shade` (0–1) of the way.
- `TOON_BANDS` (const): The carried gradient map's levels (0–255): shadow, base, lit, as the prototype's puppets drew them.
- `TOON_LOOK` (const): The default look: three bands (shadow, base, lit), shardfall's rim, shadows darkened, smoothed edges.
- `toonGradientMap` (function): The carried baseline's gradient map: one texel per level (`TOON_BANDS`), grey, nearest, for `MeshToonMaterial`.
- `ToonLook` (interface): A toon look: how many bands of light, how strong the rim is, how far shadows shift in hue, and the bands' dither.
- `ToonUniforms` (interface): A toon look as uniforms: set `.value` (or `set`) and every material reading them follows, building nothing.

### [`engine/gfx/pipelines.ts`](../engine/gfx/pipelines.ts)

- `advanceFrame` (function): Starts a new frame for three.js's nodes, so a post pass and every other node updated once per frame draws afresh, also off r182's own animation-frame loop, and gives it its own `info.frame`, as that loop does, so its timestamp queries are its own.
- `checkPinned` (function): What no longer matches the r182 internals this module reads: another three.js revision, `renderer._pipelines` without its `caches` and `programs` maps, or no `renderer._nodes.nodeFrame.update`.
- `countPipelines` (function): The counter of `device`, made on first call: wraps the device's pipeline and shader-module methods with counting forwarders.
- `PINNED_REVISION` (const): The three.js release whose internals this module reads.
- `PipelineCount` (interface): What the counter reports.
- `PipelineCounter` (interface): The counter of one device.
- `PIPELINES_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.

### [`engine/gfx/post/aa.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/aa.ts)

- `Aa` (interface): The smoothing's output, and its passes' gate for `updateBefore`.
- `AA_CHOICE` (const): The one the chain uses: the one that measured better (see the file comment).
- `AA_KINDS` (const): The edge smoothing three.js r182 offers as TSL display nodes; `traa` with `feature:traa` (WP 11.5).
- `AA_MEASURED` (const): What decided it (tests/e2e/post.spec.ts): the mean absolute error, in 0–255 luma levels, over the pixels where the unsmoothed frame differs from the supersampled one by more than 8, of the unsmoothed frame and of each smoothing, and the full-screen passes each adds.
- `AaKind` (type): An edge smoothing.
- `aaKindFor` (const): What a chain smooths with for `asked`: TRAA only while its feature is on (`temporal`), else FXAA in its place.
- `createAa` (function): Smooths `display` with `kind`, while `gate` is above 0.5; SMAA's and TRAA's passes run only while `runs()` (see above).
- `gateUpdates` (function): Wraps a node's `updateBefore` so its passes run only while `runs()` holds, and in any frame that set it up again.

### [`engine/gfx/post/chain.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/chain.ts)

- `createPost` (function): Makes the chain on `gfx.renderer` (see the file comment).
- `Post` (interface): A post-processing chain (see the file comment).
- `PostOptions` (interface): How `createPost` makes a chain.

### [`engine/gfx/post/composite.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/composite.ts)

- `CompositeInputs` (interface): What the composite reads.
- `createComposite` (function): The composite's output node: every filter over `display`, gated by `uniforms` (see the file comment).
- `POST_SHOW` (const): The views `show` picks, in the uniform's order.
- `PostShow` (type): What the composite draws.

### [`engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts)

- `colorProblem` (function): Checks an outline colour: '' (the line darkens the surface), hex (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`) or a CSS colour name three.js knows (`Color.NAMES`).
- `fixColor` (function): `spec` with an outline colour `colorProblem` refuses left out, so the line darkens the surface, and that colour (null when there was none): a layer over a look (the setting `post.filters`) is fixed and reported this way.
- `fixLevels` (function): `spec` with every level count of 1–7 raised to 8 (see the file comment), and what was raised: a layer over a look (the setting `post.filters`) is fixed and reported this way; looks are checked when they are defined.
- `levelsProblem` (function): Checks a level count: 0, or 8 and more (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/post/filters.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/filters.ts)

- `chainOf` (function): A whole chain from part of one: every filter and field `spec` leaves out at its default (off).
- `colorProblem` (function from [`engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts)): Checks an outline colour: '' (the line darkens the surface), hex (`#rgb`, `#rrggbb`) or a CSS colour name three.js knows (`Color.NAMES`).
- `createFilterUniforms` (function): Makes the composite's uniforms, every filter off.
- `FILTER_FIELDS` (const): The filters of a chain; see the file comment.
- `FILTER_NAMES` (const): Every filter, in the composite's order (the shading's, bloom and aa run before it).
- `FilterChain` (type): A filter chain: every filter with its scope and numbers.
- `FilterName` (type): A filter's name.
- `FilterSpec` (type): Part of a chain: some filters, each with some of its fields (a look's `filters`, the setting `post.filters`).
- `FilterUniforms` (interface): The composite's uniforms: one vec4 per filter (and a second for the long ones), render-group, set up once.
- `fixColor` (function from [`engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts)): `spec` with an outline colour `colorProblem` refuses left out, so the line darkens the surface, and that colour (null when there was none): a layer over a look (the setting `post.filters`) is fixed and reported this way.
- `fixLevels` (function from [`engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts)): `spec` with every level count of 1–7 raised to 8 (see the file comment), and what was raised: a layer over a look (the setting `post.filters`) is fixed and reported this way; looks are checked when they are defined.
- `isPlain` (function): Whether `chain` has every filter off, so it would leave the picture as the scene draws it (`look:clean`).
- `layerChain` (function): `chain` with `over` laid on it, filter by filter and field by field.
- `levelsProblem` (function from [`engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/filterChecks.ts)): Checks a level count: 0, or 8 and more (see the file comment).
- `PALETTES` (const): The fixed palettes (sRGB): Game Boy greens, PICO-8's sixteen, CGA, 1-bit, an amber terminal.
- `partialSchema` (function): `schema` with every default left out, so a value holds only what was given (`post.filters` layers it).
- `Scope` (type): A filter's scope.
- `scopeMask` (function): The bits of a scope: characters 1, objects 2, environment 4; `off` 0.
- `SCOPES` (const): Where a filter applies: nowhere, everywhere, or one or two parts of the scene (engine/gfx/post/mrt.ts).
- `SCREEN_SCOPES` (const): The scopes of the filters that cover the whole screen.
- `STYLIZE_KINDS` (const): The painterly and print styles.
- `writeFilters` (function): Writes `chain` into `uniforms`: a uniform write per filter, nothing more.

### [`engine/gfx/post/grid.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/grid.ts)

- `ART_LINES` (const): The lines pixel art's picture keeps to: at least `least`, at most `most` wherever a whole block allows it.
- `artBlock` (function): The art block for a picture `lines` high: the largest whole block giving it at least 240 lines (1 below that).
- `frameGrid` (function): Snaps `camera` for a frame of `chain` drawn `size` big (see the file comment); call `restore()` after it.
- `FrameGrid` (interface): A frame's grid: its pixel art's block, the snap's cells and the picture's glide, and how to put the camera back.
- `inkWidth` (function): The outline's width in pixels on a picture `lines` high: `width`, scaled when `lines` is set (see the file comment).
- `pixelBlock` (function): The pixel filter's block for a picture `lines` high: its `size`, or the art block for `size` 0.
- `QUAD` (const): How many drawn pixels a gliding snap of one drawn pixel moves the camera by: the GPU's derivative quads (above).
- `snapBlock` (function): The block grid the camera snaps to for `chain` on a picture `lines` high: pixel art's when it covers the environment and snaps (characters and objects in pixel art move on their own, and a snapping camera would make a sharp world jump), one drawn pixel included; else the whole screen's low resolution of 2 px or more; 0 for none.

### [`engine/gfx/post/looks.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/looks.ts)

- `defineLook` (function): Declares a look (`look:<name>`); see `LOOK_FIELDS`.
- `defineLooks` (function): Declares the kind `look` and the built-in looks and presets on `registry`, unless it has them.
- `LOOK_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `look` entry; see the file comment.
- `LOOK_GROUPS` (const): Where a menu lists a look: `look` for a whole look, else the filter it presets, or `shading` for a style.
- `LookEntry` (type): A `look` entry.
- `LOOKS` (const): The whole looks, from shardfall's `[[look]]` tables (see the file comment), and the clean picture.
- `LookSpec` (type): What `defineLook` takes: any of the fields, the filters as part of a chain.

### [`engine/gfx/post/mrt.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/mrt.ts)

- `clearMrt` (function): Turns any MRT off, as the frame's own drawing expects.
- `createFlagTable` (function): Makes an empty flag table: each drawable object gets a slot, for life, and `write` puts every object's flags at its slot, in one render-group uniform array the GPU reads at the slot.
- `createScenePass` (function): The scene pass: `scene` through `camera` into colour, normals with flags, and depth (the fixed MRT), and the `extra` targets the page's features ask for, fixed from then on.
- `FLAG_BITS` (const): The packed value's bits: +512 on characters, +1024 on characters and objects.
- `FLAG_SLOTS` (const): Slots in a flag table: four to a `vec4`, 4,096 of them, 64 KiB (WebGPU's smallest uniform buffer limit).
- `Flags` (interface): A tag as the composite reads it.
- `flagsOf` (function): The flags `object` is drawn with: its tag (`setPart`), or its nearest tagged ancestor's; untagged objects count as characters when they are a puppet (`userData.body`) or the protagonist (`userData.protagonist`), as objects when they stand for an entity (`userData.entity`), and as the environment otherwise.
- `FlagTable` (interface): The flags of every object a scene pass draws, by slot (see the file comment).
- `foldGroup` (function): `n` folded into the groups 1..511 (0 and below stay 0, the background's).
- `GROUPS` (const): Groups fold into 1..511; the bits above carry the part and the sign the pixel-art flag.
- `packFlags` (function): The packed value of a part, group and pixel-art flag (see the file comment).
- `Part` (type): A part of the scene: a character (puppets, the hero), an object (props, entities) or the environment.
- `PART_BITS` (const): Each part's bit in a filter's scope mask (engine/gfx/post/filters.ts).
- `PARTS` (const): The parts of the scene a filter can be scoped to.
- `PostTag` (interface): What `setPart` records on an object (`userData.post`).
- `SceneTargets` (interface): The scene pass's targets beyond colour and normals (WP 11.5): metalness and roughness for SSR, motion for TRAA.
- `setPart` (function): Tags `object` (and what it holds) with a part of the scene, an outline group and the pixel-art flag.
- `unpackFlags` (function): The part, group and pixel-art flag of a packed value; 0 or 1 (the cleared background) is the environment.
- `useSceneMrt` (function): Turns the scene pass's MRT on for what the renderer compiles or draws next (the warm-up's compile steps).
- `writeFlags` (function): Writes the flags of everything `scenePass` draws into its table, as they are now: call it before each frame, so a tag takes effect on the next one.

### [`engine/gfx/post/particles.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/particles.ts)

- `createParticleLayer` (function): Makes the layer over `scenePass`, whose camera and depth it shares (see the file comment).
- `ParticleLayer` (interface): The chain's particle layer (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/post/presets.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/presets.ts)

- `PRESETS` (const): The presets, by id (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/post/settings.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/settings.ts)

- `definePostSettings` (function): Declares the chain's settings (`POST_SETTINGS`) and the setting `quality` it reads on `registry` (the shared one by default), unless it has them: on the shared one when this module loads, so `node x set post.look look:game-boy` knows them in Node (tools/cmd/set.ts imports the modules that declare settings), and on any other when `createPost` or `createEngine` runs.
- `POST_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `POST_SETTINGS` (const): The view settings the chain reads, declared by `definePostSettings`: `post.look` (a `look` id, engine/gfx/post/looks.ts), `post.filters` (part of a filter chain laid over the look's, filter by filter and field by field) and `post.show` (`picture`, or what the MRT holds: `parts`, `normals`, `groups`).

### [`engine/gfx/post/shaders/common.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shaders/common.ts)

- `postAimed` (const): Whether a filter with scope mask `mask` applies to a pixel whose flags are `w`.
- `postBase` (const): The display colour at a pixel, clamped to the target (shardfall's \`base_color\`).
- `postBayer` (const): The 4 × 4 Bayer threshold of a cell, 0 to 1; any whole cell, negative ones too, wraps into the pattern.
- `postFlags` (const): The MRT's normal and flags at a pixel, clamped to the target.
- `postHash` (const): A hash of a position, 0 to 1.
- `postHex` (const): A 0xRRGGBB colour as 0–1 channels.
- `postLuma` (const): Rec.
- `postNoise` (const): Smooth value noise, 0 to 1.
- `postPalette` (const): The nearest colour of a fixed palette (1 Game Boy, 2 PICO-8, 3 CGA, 4 1-bit, 5 amber) at dither threshold `th` (0.5 is none): the monochrome ones spread the brightness range over their shades, the others pick the nearest.
- `postPart` (const): A pixel's part as a scope bit: 1 a character, 2 an object, 4 the environment.
- `postViewDepth` (const): The distance in front of the camera at a pixel, from the depth target and the inverse projection.
- `wgsl` (function): A WGSL function for TSL (`wgslFn`); `includes` are the functions it calls.
- `WgslFunction` (type): A WGSL function as TSL calls it: with its arguments by name, `fn({ c: colour })`.

### [`engine/gfx/post/shaders/edges.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shaders/edges.ts)

- `postArtRim` (const): Whether the block centred on `c` (block size `art`) gets pixel art's dark rim; `mask` is the pixel filter's scope.
- `postCel` (const): Comic cel over the picture `s` at `p`: `bands`, colour `punch`, `ink` strength and `ink_w` (px); see above.
- `postEdge` (const): 1 where pixel `px` is on an outline `t` px wide (see the file comment), else 0.

### [`engine/gfx/post/shaders/stylize.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shaders/stylize.ts)

- `postAscii` (const): Text mode: a grid of character cells, each cell's brightness picking a glyph of " .-:+=o&*8#@".
- `postBrush` (const): Brush strokes: a brightness factor round 1 (see the file comment).
- `postDots` (const): Coverage of one dot screen turned by `angle`, `cell` px apart; ink 0–3 is C, M, Y, K, below 0 brightness alone.
- `postHalftone` (const): Print: process-colour dot screens on cream paper, or black dots alone as `keep` falls to 0.
- `postHatch` (const): One family of parallel pencil lines across `dir`, `spacing` px apart: 1 on a line, 0 between.
- `postPaint` (const): Oil paint at pixel `c` (see the file comment); `mask` is the filter's scope mask (7 lets every sample in).
- `postSketch` (const): Pencil on paper over the picture `s` at `p`; `bp` is the picture there before the outline; `time` in seconds.
- `postStylize` (const): A style (1 paint, 2 halftone, 3 ASCII, 4 pencil) over the picture `s` at `p`; `size` in px, `keep` the colour kept, `mask` the scope mask, `time` in seconds.

### [`engine/gfx/post/shading.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/shading.ts)

- `createShading` (function): Makes the stage over `scenePass` (see the file comment).
- `Shading` (interface): The chain's shading stage (see the file comment).
- `SHADING_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.

### [`engine/gfx/post/snap.ts`](../engine/gfx/post/snap.ts)

- `blockSize` (function): The size of one block in world units, across and up, for `camera` drawing `size` pixels.
- `SNAP_FALLBACK_DEPTH` (const): How far ahead a perspective camera snaps when its line of sight never meets the ground, in metres.
- `snapGrid` (function): Moves `camera` to the nearest whole block (1 px or more) in its screen plane; see the file comment.
- `SnapGrid` (interface): Where `snapGrid` put the camera: its whole blocks, the remainder as the picture's offset, and how to undo it.
- `snapToBlocks` (function): Moves `camera` to the nearest whole block of 2 px or more in its screen plane; returns how to undo it.

### [`engine/gfx/propLooks.ts`](../engine/gfx/propLooks.ts)

- `CRATE_TEXTURE` (const): The crate's face generator: a dark edge, a frame with a nail in each corner, planks across and a brace.
- `PROP_MATERIALS` (const): The props' materials, by id: `material:crate` (texture:crate, my-3d2dge's `crateTex`, a 0.75 m face per tile), `material:barrelStaves` (texture:staves wrapped exactly once round the twelve-sided barrel, a stave per side), `material:barrelLid`, `material:flame` (unlit white, so tints show), the library's (WP 10.3) `material:iron` and `material:cloth`, and the fittings' (WP 13.16) `material:paint`; their pane is the built-in `material:glass`.
- `propLooks` (function): Defines the props' texture and materials on `registry`, unless it has them.

### [`engine/gfx/props.ts`](../engine/gfx/props.ts)

- `buildPropPart` (function): Builds `part`'s geometry (the caller's), with its tops and bottoms a group of their own when it has a `top`.
- `createPropMeshes` (function): Makes the prop meshes; see the file comment.
- `FLICKER` (const): A flame's flicker at time `t` (s): about 0.77 to 1.03, the 2D hall's (my-3d2dge's `FLICKER`).
- `OFF` (const): How bright a prop's `lit` parts are while it is off: a dark bulb, still there.
- `partMatrix` (function): Where `part` stands in its prop's frame (the base at the origin).
- `PropLight` (interface): A prop's light this frame, in world space, as three.js's `PointLight` takes it.
- `PropMeshes` (interface): The props of a scene, drawn: see the file comment.
- `PropMeshesOptions` (interface): What `createPropMeshes` takes.
- `PropMeshPose` (interface): A prop's pose: its centre (its body's origin) and its turn, and whether it is on (a switched lamp; true).
- `tongueMatrices` (function): Tongue `k`'s outer flame and core in its part's frame at `t` (s): the 2D hall's dance, in metres.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/actorLayers.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/actorLayers.ts)

- `dropLayers` (function): Takes `layers` off their animator and frees their meshes.
- `Held` (interface): What the actor puppets keep of one actor.
- `HeldRagdoll` (interface): A ragdoll as the view keeps it: its parts' poses a step ago and now, its hand-off step, and how long it has lain.
- `Layers` (interface): The view's own layers on one actor's puppet animator: its reactions, its secondary motion and their meshes.
- `layersFor` (function): The layers in `layers` of actor `id`, whose puppet animator is `animator` (its clip layer `clips`): made again when what they are made for changed (see the file comment), their chain meshes on `puppet`, drawn with `materials`.
- `Place` (interface): Where an actor stands: its feet (m) and heading (rad).

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/actors.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/actors.ts)

- `ACTOR_BODY` (const): The body every animated actor wears (engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/humanoid.ts).
- `ActorPuppets` (interface): Actors drawn as puppets (see the file comment).
- `createActorPuppets` (function): Draws actors as puppets (see the file comment); `registry` holds the bodies and gets the puppets' materials.
- `PlayerView` (interface): The player actor as the last draw put it.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/blobShadow.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/blobShadow.ts)

- `BLOB_SHADOW` (const): The shadow rule's numbers: the lift above the floor, the height where it stops shrinking, its smallest scale.
- `BLOB_SHADOW_MATERIAL` (const): The material blob shadows draw with.
- `blobScale` (function): How much a body `height` metres above its floor shrinks its shadow: 1 on the floor, down to 0.35 at 5 m.
- `blobShadowMaterial` (function): Defines `material:blobShadow` on `registry` (the shared one by default) unless it has it.
- `BlobShadows` (interface): Blob shadows (see the file comment).
- `createBlobShadows` (function): Makes the blob-shadow batch, drawn with the library's `material:blobShadow` (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/blob.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/blob.ts)

- `BLOB_BODY` (const): The slime: a blob with eyes and nothing else.
- `BLOB_BODY_RADIUS` (const): The blob's radius the sizes are written for (engine/anim/blob.ts `BLOB.radius`), metres.
- `blobBody` (function): A blob body with `features` (see the file comment).
- `BlobFeatures` (interface): The features `blobBody` can add.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/floater.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/floater.ts)
