- `PUPPET_HALO_MATERIAL` (const): The halo's material: unlit, see-through, writing no depth.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/humanoid.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/humanoid.ts)

- `HUMANOID_BODY` (const): The neutral humanoid (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/mannequin.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/mannequin.ts)

- `defineMannequin` (function): Registers `build:mannequin` (rest body `source` of `set`, its first by default) and `body:mannequin` (its `body`) on `registry` (the shared one), once; returns both.
- `MANNEQUIN_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `MANNEQUIN_SLOTS` (const): The source model's two materials: the body, and its joint rings.
- `mannequinBody` (function): `body` (a set's measured figure) as a body for `build`, the rest body `R`'s own (see the file comment).
- `MannequinData` (interface): A set's `body`, as the importer measured it (mm).

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/quadruped.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/bodies/quadruped.ts)

- `QUADRUPED_BODY` (const): The dog (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/chains.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/chains.ts)

- `ChainMeshes` (interface): The meshes of one `Secondary`'s chains (see the file comment).
- `ChainMeshOptions` (interface): What `createChainMeshes` takes: the material (lit, vertex-coloured), the colour (CSS hex) and the name's stem.
- `createChainMeshes` (function): The meshes of `secondary`'s chains (see the file comment).
- `STRAND` (const): A strand's width, metres: hair's and a tail's square tube.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/compile.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/compile.ts)

- `BodyPiece` (interface): One piece: a unit shape on one bone (see the file comment).
- `CAPE_THICKNESS` (const): How thick a cape strip is, in metres at size 1.
- `COMPILE_CODES` (const): The codes compiling a body raises, with their fixes.
- `compileBody` (function): Compiles `body` (or its id) for `build` (a skeleton, a build or a build id; `build:chibi` by default).
- `CompiledBody` (interface): A body compiled for one build (see the file comment).
- `PieceShape` (type): A unit shape a piece draws (see the file comment).
- `recolor` (function): `compiled` with its slots' colours replaced by `palette`'s (hex), the pieces shared.
- `restPositions` (function): Each joint's rest position on `skeleton`, 3 per joint (rest rotations are the identity).

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/crowd.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/crowd.ts)

- `createCrowd` (function): Makes a crowd's batches and level of detail (see the file comment).
- `Crowd` (interface): A crowd's batches and level of detail (see the file comment).
- `CROWD_CODES` (const): The codes crowd drawing raises, with their fixes.
- `CROWD_PAGE_SLOTS` (const): Instances per page of the crowd's batches.
- `CrowdDraw` (interface): How a body is drawn: its band (full detail when absent) and the floor under it, for a blob shadow.
- `CrowdRigDraw` (interface): How a rig is drawn: also its flags (`when`, `unless`) and its scale against its body.
- `CrowdStats` (interface): A frame's counts: the bands and culling (lod.ts), bodies drawn, and each batch's instances and shown pages.
- `HUMANOID_SHADOW` (const): A humanoid's blob shadow, metres at size 1 (the source's 5 units).
- `RigBody` (interface): A rig body (see the file comment).
- `RigJoints` (type): A rig's pose: each joint a world matrix, a point, or a list of points.
- `RigPart` (interface): One part of a rig body: a unit shape (compile.ts's file comment) on one joint of the rig's pose, a matrix, a point or a list of points (one part on each).
- `RigShape` (type): A unit shape a rig part draws: any but the limb.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/draw.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/draw.ts)

- `createPuppet` (function): Draws `compiled` as one rigid-skinned mesh (see the file comment), at rest until `setPose`.
- `createPuppetBatches` (function): Makes instanced puppet batches (see the file comment).
- `PieceRange` (interface): Where one piece's vertices lie in a puppet's geometry (`geometry.userData.pieces`, in drawing order).
- `Puppet` (interface): One character drawn as a rigid-skinned mesh (see the file comment).
- `PUPPET_MATERIALS` (const): The materials puppets draw with by default.
- `PuppetBatches` (interface): Instanced parts for crowds (see the file comment).
- `puppetGeometry` (function): The rigid-skinned geometry of `compiled`: lit pieces (group 0), then glow pieces (group 1), see the file comment; `userData.pieces` lists each piece's vertices (`PieceRange`).
- `puppetMaterials` (function): Defines `PUPPET_MATERIALS` on `registry` (the shared one by default), those it lacks.
- `PuppetMaterials` (interface): Where materials come from: the page's material library.
- `unitGeometry` (function): The unit geometry of `shape`; `limb@k` is an open frustum of radius 1 at y = 0 and k at y = 1.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/grammar.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/grammar.ts)

- `Body` (type): A `body` entry: the parsed spec, its parts typed.
- `BODY_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `body` entry.
- `bodyKind` (function): Declares the kind `body` on `registry`, with the engine's bodies (`body:humanoid`), unless it has it.
- `BodyLength` (type): A size or an offset: metres, or `[k, ref]`, k times the head radius, the limb radius or the torso radius.
- `BodyPart` (type): One part, one line (see the file comment).
- `BodyPoint` (type): Where a part's end lies (see the file comment).
- `bodyProblems` (function): The problems of a body beyond its fields' types: colours that are not hex, builds giving other fields, and in every part an unknown type, the wrong number of arguments, a point that is no joint or socket, a slot the body lacks, a size that is not positive, a count outside 1–64, or options other than `{ on }`.
- `BodySpec` (interface): What `defineBody` takes: any field; absent ones keep their defaults.
- `defineBody` (function): Defines a body on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `getBody` (function): The body `id` of `registry`; a missing id warns once (`CORE_UNKNOWN_ID`) and gives `body:humanoid`.
- `mirrorName` (function): `name` with its side swapped (`thighL` → `thighR`), when the swapped name exists; else `name`.
- `mirrorPart` (function): `part` mirrored left to right: its points and its `on` bone (see the file comment).
- `mirrorPoint` (function): `point` mirrored left to right.
- `PART_TYPES` (const): Each part type's arguments after its name: `p` a point, `s` a size, `r` a size or three, `n` a number, `c` a count (1–64), `k` the slot.
- `PartOptions` (interface): A part's options: the bone it rides (a joint, or `'root'`).
- `PartType` (type): A part type's name.
- `pointProblem` (function): Why `point` is no point, or null.

### [`engine/gfx/puppets/lod.ts`](../engine/gfx/puppets/lod.ts)

- `createCrowdLod` (function): Makes a crowd's level of detail (see the file comment).
- `CROWD_LOD` (const): The default bands (see the file comment).
- `CROWD_LOD_CODES` (const): The codes the crowd's level of detail raises, with their fixes.
- `CrowdBand` (interface): One band of detail: the bodies whose distance is under its `upTo` and at least the band before's.
- `CrowdBandSpec` (type): A band as written: without its index.
- `CrowdLod` (interface): A crowd's level of detail (see the file comment).
- `CrowdLodCounts` (interface): A frame's counts so far: bodies drawn in each band, and those culled by the view, the distance and `near`.
- `CrowdLodOptions` (interface): How a crowd's level of detail is made.

### [`engine/gfx/quality.ts`](../engine/gfx/quality.ts)

- `QUALITY_SETTING_VALUES` (const): The `quality` setting's values.
- `QUALITY_SETTINGS` (const): The quality settings: view settings, never in the hash.
- `qualityBudget` (function): What `setting` affords on a touch screen (`touch`) or elsewhere (see the file comment).
- `QualityBudget` (interface): What a tier affords; `null` caps nothing.
- `QualitySetting` (type): The `quality` setting: a tier, or `auto`.
- `QualityTier` (type): A quality tier, as `auto` resolves.
- `resolveQuality` (function): The tier `setting` means on a touch screen (`touch`) or elsewhere.

### [`engine/gfx/renderer.ts`](../engine/gfx/renderer.ts)

- `createRenderer` (function): Starts three.js's `WebGPURenderer` on `canvas`, on WebGPU only: the adapter check, a device with every feature and limit the adapter offers, `await renderer.init()`, the backend assertion, then the report, the feature registry and the error routes.
- `FRAME_CODES` (const): The codes a running renderer raises through the log.
- `FrameReport` (interface): What `frame()` did.
- `FrameView` (interface): One frame to draw: the warm-up's view, plus the clock's interpolation alpha (1, the latest state, by default) and the GPU's particles the post chain draws in a pass of their own (engine/gfx/enhanced/particles.ts, WP 11.3).
- `Gfx` (interface): A started renderer: three.js's `WebGPURenderer`, its device, its report, and what draws a frame.
- `GFX_CODES` (const): The codes the renderer raises at startup, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `GfxCode` (type): A code the renderer raises at startup: a key of `GFX_CODES`.
- `GfxError` (class): A renderer failure: its code, the message from the code's template, and the code's fix.
- `GfxInfo` (interface): What the renderer reports about itself (the GPU half of `__engine.info()`, PLAN.md §8.3).
- `GfxOptions` (interface): How `createRenderer` is made: antialiasing, and the settings, registry and log it reads and reports to.
- `GfxStats` (interface): The renderer's counts: the last frame's from `renderer.info`, the pipelines' since startup.
- `requestWebGPU` (function): Asks `gpu` (by default the browser's `navigator.gpu`) for an adapter; rejects with `GfxError` `GFX_NO_WEBGPU` when there is no WebGPU or no adapter.

### [`engine/gfx/resolution.ts`](../engine/gfx/resolution.ts)

- `createResolution` (function): Keeps `renderer`'s drawing buffer fitted to `canvas` and the `gfx.resolution` setting.
- `Fit` (interface): What a mode gives for a canvas: the drawing buffer's size and how it maps to the screen.
- `fitResolution` (function): The drawing buffer `mode` gives a canvas of `css` size at `devicePixelRatio`, within `cap` (none by default).
- `keepWidth` (function): Widens a perspective camera placed for this frame when the picture is portrait (`portraitFov`); else no change.
- `MAX_PIXEL_RATIO` (const): The highest device pixel ratio drawn at: beyond it, pixels are too small to see and cost the same.
- `MAX_PORTRAIT_FOV` (const): The widest vertical field of view a portrait picture gets, in degrees.
- `PIXEL_LINES` (const): The most lines the `pixels` mode draws.
- `PixelCap` (interface): A cap on the drawing buffer (engine/gfx/quality.ts's budget); a null or absent field caps nothing.
- `portraitFov` (function): The vertical field of view (deg) that keeps `fov`'s width on a picture `aspect` (width / height) wide, below 1.
- `Resolution` (interface): A renderer's resolution, kept to its canvas and the setting.
- `RESOLUTION_MODES` (const): The resolution modes, chunkiest first.
- `RESOLUTION_SETTINGS` (const): The resolution settings: view settings, never in the hash.
- `ResolutionMode` (type): A resolution mode: the engine's pixels, half the screen's, or all of it.
- `ResolutionOptions` (interface): How `createResolution` measures: the canvas's CSS size and the device pixel ratio (the browser's by default).
- `Size` (interface): A size in CSS or device pixels.

### [`engine/gfx/sceneDump.ts`](../engine/gfx/sceneDump.ts)

- `DumpOptions` (interface): What `dumpScene` writes.
- `dumpScene` (function): The tree under `root` as text, one object a line (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/shadows.ts`](../engine/gfx/shadows.ts)

- `Casters` (interface): Who casts shadows: whether the sun does, and how many of the light pool's first slots.
- `configurePointCaster` (function): Gives a point light the caster's shadow settings (`POINT_SHADOW`); whether it casts is the budget's call.
- `enableShadows` (function): Turns the renderer's shadow map on, with the engine's one shadow map type.
- `MAX_SHADOW_CASTERS` (const): The most lights that cast shadows at once: the budget at the `high` tier.
- `POINT_SHADOW` (const): A point caster's shadow settings, carried from the prototype's shadow lights.
- `SHADOW_GRID` (const): The frame's pixel grid as the filters' noise reads it: (whole blocks across, whole blocks down, the block in pixels), the post chain's each frame (engine/gfx/post/grid.ts `frameGrid`), (0, 0, 1) outside its frames.
- `SHADOW_MAP_TYPE` (const): The shadow map type every caster uses (r182's `PCFShadowMap`; see the file comment).
- `shadowCasters` (function): How many lights may cast shadows under `budget` (a quality tier's, engine/gfx/quality.ts).
- `SNAPPED_PCF` (const): r182's `PCFShadowFilter` (ShadowFilterNode.js), its noise on the frame's grid: the sun's and its cascades'.
- `SNAPPED_POINT` (const): r182's `PointShadowFilter` (PointShadowNode.js), its noise on the frame's grid: the light pool's casters'.
- `snapShadow` (function): Gives `shadow` the engine's filter for its kind (see the file comment): a point light's for a cube map.
- `splitCasters` (function): Who casts under a budget of `casters`: the sun first when it shines, then the point lights when they shine.

### [`engine/gfx/shot.ts`](../engine/gfx/shot.ts)

- `Readback` (interface): The readback's padded layout: bytes per row as WebGPU copied them, and the buffer's length.
- `readPixels` (function): Reads an RGBA8 render target back: its pixels, top row first, without the padding, and the layout read.
- `rowBytes` (function): Bytes per row WebGPU copies for `width` pixels: aligned up to 256 (`copyTextureToBuffer`'s rule).
- `shot` (function): Shoots `view`: draws it as the frame does into a render target, draws the ID pass, reads both back, and returns what `options` asks for (see the file comment).
- `SHOT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `shotForJson` (function): The result as plain JSON, for `__engine.shot` and `x shot`: the pixels as base64.
- `ShotGfx` (interface): What a shot needs of the renderer (engine/gfx/renderer.ts's `Gfx`).
- `ShotJson` (type): A shot as plain JSON: `pixels` and `marked` as base64 RGBA.
- `ShotOptions` (interface): What to shoot and what to return.
- `ShotResult` (interface): What a shot returns: its size, the readback's layout, what was asked, pipelines built, and how long it took.
- `stripRowPadding` (function): Drops the row padding of a readback: `height` rows of `width` pixels from rows of `rowBytes(width)` bytes.
- `toBase64` (function): Base64 of bytes, in the browser and in Node.

### [`engine/gfx/sky.ts`](../engine/gfx/sky.ts)

- `BACKDROP` (const from [`engine/gfx/backdrop.ts`](../engine/gfx/backdrop.ts)): The backdrop strip's size in texels, and its band round the camera (m): radius, height, foot below the eye.
- `BACKDROP_KINDS` (const from [`engine/gfx/backdrop.ts`](../engine/gfx/backdrop.ts)): The kinds of backdrop layer.
- `BackdropSpec` (type): A backdrop as a `sky` entry gives it.
- `bakeBackdrop` (function from [`engine/gfx/backdrop.ts`](../engine/gfx/backdrop.ts)): Bakes a backdrop into RGBA bytes, `width` × `height`, row 0 at the bottom; above the skylines is clear.
- `createSky` (function): Puts a sky on `scene`: the light pool lit from `level`'s light spots (phases from `rng`, a visual stream), the sun, the dome, the backdrop and the atmosphere; shows `sky:daylight` until `set` names another preset.
- `defineSkies` (function): Declares the kind `sky` and the built-in presets on `registry`, unless it has them.
- `defineSky` (function): Declares a sky preset (`sky:<name>`); see `SKY_FIELDS`.
- `Sky` (interface): A sky on a scene; see the file comment.
- `SKY_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `sky` entry; see the file comment.
- `SkyEntry` (type): A `sky` entry.
- `SkyOptions` (interface): How `createSky` makes a sky.
- `SkyReport` (interface): What a sky shows now.
- `SkySpec` (type): What `defineSky` takes: any of the fields, and any of a nested object's (a backdrop's layers whole).

### [`engine/gfx/stage.ts`](../engine/gfx/stage.ts)

- `createStage` (function): Builds a stage (see the file comment).
- `placeableKinds` (function): The component kinds whose entities stand somewhere: they declare `x` and `z` as numbers in metres.
- `placeOf` (function): Where `entity` stands, from the first of `kinds` it holds; undefined when it holds none.
- `Stage` (interface): A running scene's presentation graph (see the file comment).
- `StageOptions` (interface): What a stage is made of: the level (none for an empty stage), where materials come from, and its registry.
- `StandInPlace` (interface): Where a stand-in stands and how it looks, read from its entity's placing component.

### [`engine/gfx/stageCrowd.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageCrowd.ts)

- `createStageCrowd` (function): Builds the crowd bodies of a stage (see the file comment).
- `StageCrowd` (interface): The crowd bodies on a stage (see the file comment).
- `StageCrowdOptions` (interface): What the stage's crowd is made from: where it goes, the materials, the level for the shadows' floor, a registry.

### [`engine/gfx/stageFx.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageFx.ts)

- `createStageFx` (function): Makes the stage's effects (see the file comment).
- `fxKinds` (function): The component kinds the effects draw: bolts and telegraphs (see the file comment), in registry order.
- `STAGE_FX_SETTINGS` (const): The view setting that turns the stage's effects on and off.
- `StageFx` (interface): The stage's effects (see the file comment).
- `StageFxOptions` (interface): What `createStageFx` takes.

### [`engine/gfx/stageGround.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageGround.ts)

- `GROUND_MARGIN` (const): How far the ground reaches beyond the level on every side, m: past what any view frames at zoom 0.5.
- `groundMesh` (function): The stage's ground round an area of `size` (m, along x and z: see the file comment).
- `GroundOptions` (interface): Where the ground lies: its area's north-west corner (m), the floor it stands under (m), and a terrain's hole.

### [`engine/gfx/stageProps.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageProps.ts)

- `createStageProps` (function): Draws the scene's props (see the file comment).
- `StageProps` (interface): Props drawn on the stage (see the file comment).
- `StagePropsOptions` (interface): What `createStageProps` takes.

### [`engine/gfx/stageRides.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageRides.ts)

- `createStageRides` (function): Makes the rides of a stage (see the file comment).
- `RIDE_KINDS` (const): The components it draws rides from: the stage reads these entities beside those it places.
- `RUNG` (const): A rung every this many metres up a ladder.
- `StageRides` (interface): The rides on a stage (see the file comment).
- `StageRidesOptions` (interface): What `createStageRides` takes.

### [`engine/gfx/stageShells.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageShells.ts)

- `createStageShells` (function): Makes the stage's shells over its props and its actors' puppets (see the file comment).
- `SHELL_LINES` (const): The lines a look's shell width is given at: scaled to the picture's height in whole pixels.
- `ShellLook` (interface): What a look asks of the shells: their width in pixels at 270 lines (0 for none), and their colour, hex.
- `StageShells` (interface): The stage's shells (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/stageSite.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageSite.ts)

- `createStageSite` (function): Draws `site` (see the file comment).
- `StageSite` (interface): A site as the stage draws it (see the file comment).
- `StageStructure` (interface): One structure as drawn: its group in the world, its meshes in its own frame, its cutaways.

### [`engine/gfx/stageSky.ts`](../engine/gfx/stageSky.ts)

- `createStageSky` (function): Makes the stage's lights on `scene` (see the file comment); the stage's own show until a sky is asked for.
- `StageSky` (interface): The stage's lights (see the file comment).
- `StageSkyOptions` (interface): What the stage's lights are made from.
- `StageSkyView` (interface): What a frame gives the stage's lights: the camera, the focus (m), the time (s), the hour and the frame's lamps.

### [`engine/gfx/storeyCut.ts`](../engine/gfx/storeyCut.ts)

- `aboveStorey` (function): Whether a thing at (x, y, z) of `level`'s frame stands on a storey above `storey` (≥ 0): the cut hides it too.
- `createStoreyCut` (function): The cutaway by storey over `meshes` (see the file comment).
- `cutPlace` (function): Where feet at (x, y, z) of `level`'s own frame stand for the cut: the storey (−1 outside or on a roof), indoors, and `low`, under a low ceiling of that storey.
- `planStoreys` (function): Which of `pieces` show with the player on `storey` (−1 outside or on a roof), `indoors` or not, under a `low` ceiling or not (see the file comment).
- `StoreyCut` (interface): A level's cutaway by storey (see the file comment).
- `StoreyPiece` (interface): What the plan reads of a mesh: its storey (none in a level of one storey), whether it is a roof, or its heads.

### [`engine/gfx/terrain.ts`](../engine/gfx/terrain.ts)

- `CHUNK` (const): A chunk's side, in cells, at most.
- `chunkGeometry` (function): One level of a chunk: cells `c0`… and `r0`… of `terrain`, `cols` × `rows` of them, taking every `step`-th corner, positions from `middle` (m), with its skirt (see the file comment).
- `createTerrainMeshes` (function): Draws `terrain` (see the file comment).
- `levelDistance` (function): How far `camera` stands from a chunk whose middle is `at`, as its level of detail reads it: the distance, from a perspective camera; from an orthographic one, how far a 50° lens stands to frame its height (m).
- `LOD_DISTANCES` (const): From how far (m) each level shows.
- `LOD_STEPS` (const): The levels of detail: the corners each takes, every one, every second, every fourth.
- `SKIRT` (const): How far a chunk's skirt hangs below its edge (m).
- `TerrainMeshes` (interface): A terrain's meshes (see the file comment).
- `TerrainMeshesOptions` (interface): What `createTerrainMeshes` needs: where materials come from.
- `terrainNormals` (function): Every corner's smooth normal: central differences of the heights (one-sided at the edges).

### [`engine/gfx/terrainSplat.ts`](../engine/gfx/terrainSplat.ts)

- `BAND` (const): How far either side of the steep grade (m a metre) the steep layer blends in.
- `createTerrainSplat` (function): Makes the splat of `terrain`, `layers` the steep and the high layers' materials (see the file comment).
- `TerrainSplat` (interface): The terrain's splat: its materials (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/bake.ts)

- `bakeKey` (function): The key of a bake from `source`: the canonical hash of its texture, seed, parameters and size.
- `BakeSource` (interface): What a texture was baked from: everything filled.
- `bakeTexture` (function): Bakes `ref` on `registry` (the shared one by default).
- `newTexel` (function): A fresh texel.
- `normalsFromHeight` (function): Tangent-space normals of a tiling height field (`width` × `height` floats, row 0 at the bottom): Sobel gradients with wrap-around, z out of the surface, scaled by `depth` (a height step of 1 slopes 45° at 2), as RGBA bytes.
- `TextureBake` (interface): A baked texture: its source, its maps and its hash.
- `TextureRef` (type): A texture by id, or by id with its seed, parameters and size.
- `textureSampler` (function): The filled source of `ref` on `registry`.
- `TextureSampler` (interface): A generator ready to sample: its filled source and the function writing texel (x, y) at any integer point.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/codes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/codes.ts)

- `TEXTURE_CODES` (const): The codes of the texture bake, with their fixes.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/contactShadow.ts)

- `CONTACT_SHADOW_CODES` (const): The codes of the level floor bake, with their fixes.
- `contactShadow` (function): The shadow at `d` texels from a block's foot (0–1), fading to 0 at `radius` texels in `steps` bands.
- `ContactShadowOptions` (interface): How the contact shadow at the foot of a block looks.
- `FloorMossOptions` (interface): How moss creeps in from the foot of the blocks.
- `FloorRuneOptions` (interface): The rune circle laid on each dais; sizes in metres.
- `LevelFloorOptions` (interface): What a level's floor is baked from; every part may be left out.
- `levelFloorTexture` (function): A texture generator for `level`'s whole floor: its base texture with moss at the walls' feet, rune circles on the daises and contact shadows along every block's foot (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/dataTexture.ts)

- `DataTextureOptions` (interface): How the textures are made: the look (the bake's own by default) and a repeat overriding the density.
- `TextureMaps` (interface): A bake's textures, by the material slot each fills.
- `toDataTextures` (function): The textures of `bake` for a material's slots (see the file comment).

- `METAL` (const): The metal generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/moss.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/moss.ts)

- `MOSS` (const): The moss generator's spec.
- `mossGrowth` (function): Moss growth over a texture of `size` texels: `grow(texel, x, y, cover)` lays moss over the texel when it grows there at `cover` (0–1, about the share of open stone it covers; joints and cracks take it first), and says whether it did.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/planks.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/planks.ts)

- `PLANKS` (const): The plank generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/runes.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/runes.ts)

- `paintRune` (function): Writes `mark` onto `texel` (nothing for 0): the inlay's colour, its glow, a little below the stone, smoother.
- `runeCircle` (function): A rune circle: `mark(i, j)` is the mark of the texel whose centre lies (i + ½, j + ½) texels from the circle's centre (i, j whole numbers; the centre on a texel corner).
- `RuneCircleOptions` (interface): The shape of a rune circle, in texels.
- `RuneMark` (type): What a texel of a rune circle is: nothing, a faint line (ring or spoke), or a bright rune or the centre.
- `RUNES` (const): The rune generator's spec.
- `RuneTones` (interface): The colours of a rune circle and how brightly its lines glow (its runes and centre glow at 1).

- `SHINGLES` (const): The shingle generator's spec.

- `STAVES` (const): The barrel-stave generator's spec.

- `STONE` (const): The dressed-stone generator's spec.

- `TILES` (const): The tile generator's spec.

- `WATER` (const): The water generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/generators/wood.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/generators/wood.ts)

- `WOOD` (const): The wood generator's spec.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/mips.ts)

- `linearToSrgbByte` (function): A linear value as the nearest sRGB byte.
- `mipChain` (function): The full mip chain of an RGBA map, level 0 (`data` itself) first, down to 1 × 1: each level the area-weighted box filter of the float level above, averaged as `encoding` says (see the file comment).
- `mipCount` (function): The number of levels of a `width` × `height` texture's full chain.
- `MipEncoding` (type): What a map holds, which says how its levels are averaged.
- `MipLevel` (interface): One level: RGBA bytes, row 0 at the bottom.
- `SRGB_TO_LINEAR` (const): Each sRGB byte's linear value.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/seams.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/seams.ts)

- `measureSeam` (function): The worst seam of `bake` over its channels and both axes (see the file comment).
- `mipProblems` (function): The problems of a mip chain for a `width` × `height` map, one sentence each: the wrong number of levels, a level of the wrong size or data length, the last level not 1 × 1, a colour or roughness level whose mean drifts from level 0's by more than `tolerance` (in linear units), or a normal more than 3% off unit length.
- `periodMismatch` (function): The share of texels (0–1) the sampler writes differently one period away: at (x + width, y), (x, y + height) and (x − width, y − height).
- `rangeProblems` (function): Every value the sampler writes checked against its range (see `RangeReport`).
- `RangeReport` (interface): What `rangeProblems` counts.
- `SEAM_LIMIT` (const): The largest seam delta a tiling texture may have: 2% of the value range.
- `SeamReport` (interface): The worst seam of a bake: where, by how much, and the numbers behind it.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/texture.ts)

- `assertSize` (function): Throws `GFX_TEXTURE_SIZE` when `entry` cannot bake at `size` with `params`.
- `defineTexture` (function): Defines a texture generator on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getTexture` (function): The texture `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); throws `CORE_NO_ENTRY` naming the closest ids.
- `sizeProblem` (function): Why `entry` cannot bake at `size` with `params` (a sentence), or '' when it can.
- `TEXTURE_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `texture` entry.
- `TextureEntry` (type): A `texture` entry: one generator.
- `textureKind` (function): Declares the kind `texture` on `registry`, with the engine's v1, v2 and v3 generators, unless it has it.
- `textureParams` (function): The parameters of `entry` with `given` set: every parameter filled; throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming each problem.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/tile.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tile.ts)

- `BondCell` (interface): One texel's place in a running bond: its cell's column and row (wrapped) and its position inside the cell.
- `cellHash` (function): A seeded value in [0, 1) for the integer point (x, y), with `salt` telling apart uses of one seed (a stone's tone, its crack).
- `palette` (function): A palette's hex colours as sRGB bytes; throws `GFX_EMPTY_PALETTE` naming `what` when it has none.
- `pickTone` (function): One of `colors`, picked by `value` in [0, 1).
- `runningBond` (function): Where texel (x, y) falls in a running bond of `cell` = [width, height] texels over a texture of `size`: courses (rows) of cells, odd courses shifted half a cell, the whole layout moved by `phase` texels.
- `tileNoise` (function): Value noise in [0, 1] over a texture of `size` texels, repeating exactly every `size`: lattice values from `cellHash`, blended with smoothstep, `cells` lattice cells across on each axis (stretched when they differ), summed over octaves and divided by the total weight.
- `TileNoiseOptions` (interface): How `tileNoise` is made.
- `wrapIndex` (function): `i` folded into [0, n) (n a positive integer): -1 → n − 1.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/tslNoise.ts)

- `fractalNode` (function): Fractal value noise in [0, 1] at the vec2 node `p` (`fractalNoise` on the GPU).
- `fractalNoise` (function): Fractal value noise in [0, 1] at (x, y): the weighted mean of `octaves` octaves.
- `latticeHash` (function): The lattice value at integer point (x, y) for `seed`, in [0, 1): the CPU twin of the shader's hash.
- `noiseNode` (function): Value noise in [0, 1] at the vec2 node `p`, one lattice cell per unit (`valueNoise` on the GPU).
- `valueNoise` (function): Value noise in [0, 1] at (x, y), one lattice cell per unit: the CPU twin of `noiseNode`.
- `variationAt` (function): The variation factor at world (x, z) metres: 1 + amount (2 · fractal noise at (x, z) / scale − 1).
- `variationNode` (function): The large-scale variation factor as a float node around 1 (`variationAt` on the GPU), sampled at `position`'s x and z (world space by default, so it runs on across meshes and instances): multiply a colour by it.
- `VariationOptions` (interface): How the large-scale variation is made.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/types.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/types.ts)

- `Texel` (interface): One texel as a generator writes it.
- `TexelFn` (type): Writes texel (x, y).
- `TextureContext` (interface): What `create` is given: the parameters (defaults filled), the seed, and the size the texture bakes at.
- `TextureLook` (type): How a texture is magnified: `pixel` keeps texels crisp (nearest), `smooth` blends them (linear).
- `textureSpec` (function): Returns `spec` unchanged, typed: `create` sees the parameters as the schema `params` declares them.
- `TextureSpec` (interface): A generator: its parameters, the size and look it bakes at, and the function that writes its texels.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v1.ts)

- `V1_TEXTURES` (const): The v1 generators, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/v2.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v2.ts)

- `V2_TEXTURES` (const): The v2 generators, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/textures/v3.ts`](../engine/gfx/textures/v3.ts)

- `V3_TEXTURES` (const): The v3 generators, by id.

### [`engine/gfx/thumbnail.ts`](../engine/gfx/thumbnail.ts)

- `compareThumbnails` (function): Compares two thumbnails cell by cell: a cell differs when one of its channels moved by more than `tolerance` (default 24 of 255).
- `MAP_SYMBOLS` (const): The symbols of the map, for the visible objects in order (largest first).
- `STRAY` (const): The per-pixel value of a pixel no object claims (an ID colour the pass did not assign).
- `THUMB_HEIGHT` (const): The grid's height.
- `THUMB_WIDTH` (const): The grid's size: 48 × 27 cells (16:9).
- `thumbnail` (function): Builds the 48 × 27 thumbnail of a frame of row-major RGBA bytes, with the map when the ID pass is given.
- `Thumbnail` (interface): A text thumbnail.
- `ThumbnailDiff` (interface): How two thumbnails differ.
- `ThumbnailIds` (interface): The ID pass's objects per pixel: 0 empty space, k the k-th name of `names` (1-based), `STRAY` unclaimed.

### [`engine/gfx/viewmodel/body.ts`](../engine/gfx/viewmodel/body.ts)

- `Animated` (interface): What the arms are posed from: the body's animator, posed this frame, its traversal plant, its hold and its weapon.
- `armsBody` (function): `compiled` with its arm and kicking-leg pieces alone (no glow): what the arms draw.
- `createViewmodel` (function): Gives `puppet` (the player's) its first-person arms and look (see the file comment).
- `FirstPersonParts` (interface): What a frame hid of the body and showed of the arms.
- `GUN_KICK` (const): A shot's kick of first person's gun: back along its barrel (m) and up (rad) at once, gone with a time constant (s).
- `Viewmodel` (interface): First person's player on a puppet (see the file comment).
- `ViewmodelFrame` (interface): A frame drawn by a first-person camera: its pose, the frame's real seconds and aspect, the player and the effects.

### [`engine/gfx/viewmodel/lens.ts`](../engine/gfx/viewmodel/lens.ts)

- `armsDepth` (function): The depth (m, along the view) the arms draw a point of theirs `z` deep at, in a picture whose near plane is `near`.
- `armsLens` (function): The arms' lens of the setting `cam.armsFov` (`h`, Apex's horizontal degrees at 4:3), vertical degrees.
- `armsSpread` (function): How far out across the picture the arms' lens `fov` (vertical degrees) moves a point beyond `pose`'s lens.
- `drawnPoint` (function): Where the arms draw their point `p` (world, m) for `pose`, with their lens `fov` (see the file comment).
- `inArmsFrame` (function): Whether the arms' frame (their lens `fov`, a picture of `aspect`) shows their point `p`, and their depth keeps it.
- `intoArmsFrame` (function): `p` kept within `margin` of the arms' half-frame (their lens `fov`, a picture of `aspect`), as far from the eye as it was: a point outside moves to the frame's nearest edge, one behind the eye to the edge it is beyond.
- `VIEWMODEL` (const): The arms' lens and depth (see the file comment): degrees, metres, shares.
- `VIEWMODEL_SETTING_FIELDS` (const): The view settings the viewmodel reads; never in the hash.
- `VIEWMODEL_SETTINGS` (const): The view settings the viewmodel reads, declared on the shared registry.

### [`engine/gfx/viewmodel/material.ts`](../engine/gfx/viewmodel/material.ts)

- `createViewmodelLook` (function): Makes the viewmodel's materials (see the file comment); `log` takes the advice.
- `VIEWMODEL_MATERIAL_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `ViewmodelLook` (interface): The viewmodel's materials (see the file comment).

### [`engine/gfx/viewmodel/rig.ts`](../engine/gfx/viewmodel/rig.ts)

- `ARMS` (const): The rig's numbers (see the file comment): places, metres, seconds.
- `ArmsInput` (interface): What the rig poses the arms from, beside the camera (see `armsInputOf`).
- `armsInputOf` (function): What the rig reads off the player's `animator` (its traversal plant `contacts`, its `hold`), with the frame's camera inputs.
- `ArmsRig` (class): First person's arms posed against the camera (see the file comment).
- `HeldHand` (interface): A hand the body holds on something: where its grip is (world), its world rotation, and how much it holds (0 to 1).
- `vec3Of` (const): The world point of `p` (a `Vector3`) as a `Vec3`.

### [`engine/gfx/warmup.ts`](../engine/gfx/warmup.ts)

- `createWarmup` (function): Makes the warm-up registry of `renderer`, counting builds with `counter`.
- `Warmup` (interface): A renderer's warm-up registry.
- `WARMUP_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `WarmupEntry` (interface): What a pool or batch registers: the objects it may show, each made drawable for the warm-up.
- `WarmupPass` (interface): One way a frame draws the scene: into a render target, with the renderer set up for it.
- `WarmupProgress` (interface): Progress, after each step: steps done of the total, and the step just done.
- `WarmupReport` (interface): What one warm-up did.
- `WarmupView` (interface): What a warm-up draws: the scene, its camera, how the frame draws it, and every way it draws the scene.

### [`engine/gfx/weapons.ts`](../engine/gfx/weapons.ts)

- `alongBarrel` (function): A turn putting +Z on the unit `barrel` and +Y as near the world's up as that leaves (a level gun when it is level).
- `createWeaponFx` (function): Makes the shots' effects over `effects` (the view's, for the flashes and the impacts; see the file comment).
- `gunGeometry` (function): `kind`'s prop as one geometry in its frame (the grip at the origin, +Z along the barrel), positions and normals, each vertex coloured by its part's tint over its material's colour (linear): what first person draws in the arms' vertex-coloured material (see the file comment).
- `gunPose` (function): Where a gun stands in a posed body's hand: at its grip (`weaponR`), +Z along `barrel` (unit, world), +Y up-most.
- `HeldGun` (interface): A gun in a hand as the view draws it: its weapon, and where its grip stands and its turn (world).
- `HOLES` (const): A bullet hole: its size (m), colour and how far off its surface (m); the latest `capacity` stay.
- `muzzlePoint` (function): Where `kind`'s shots leave a gun standing at `pose` (world, m): its muzzle in its frame.
- `TRACER` (const): A tracer's look: its life (s), width (m), colour, and how far ahead of where a shot left it starts without a gun.
- `WeaponFx` (interface): The shots' effects (see the file comment).
- `weaponOut` (function): The weapon `entity`'s component `weapons` has out (its kind, of `registry`), or null: holstered, or no weapons.

### [`engine/input/actionMaps.ts`](../engine/input/actionMaps.ts)

- `ActionMap` (type): An action map entry.
- `actionMapKind` (function): Declares the kind `actionMap` on `registry` unless it has it.
- `ActionMapSpec` (interface): How an action map is written.
- `defineActionMap` (function): Registers an action map (on the shared registry by default).
- `getActionMap` (function): The action map `id`.
- `listActionMaps` (function): Every action map, sorted by id.
- `PRESETS` (const): The presets, by id.
- `RESERVED_CODES` (const): Codes no action map binds: the pause buttons, and keys the browser or the system keeps.
- `SYSTEM_ACTIONS` (const): The system layer: action → codes.

### [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)

- `AIM_RANGE` (const): How far the centre's ray looks (m): one that meets nothing aims this far along it.
- `AIM_RULES` (const): The aim rules, in the order the docs list them.
- `AimDevices` (type): What the devices give aiming: the pointer and the right stick (see `AimView`).
- `aimPoint` (function): The point the rule aims at this frame (see the file comment), or undefined.
- `AimPose` (interface): A camera's pose as aiming reads it: engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts's `CameraPose` fits it.
- `AimRay` (interface): A ray: where it starts and its unit direction.
- `AimRule` (type): What aims a player's look or pointer, by an action map's `aim`: see the file comment.
- `AimView` (interface): What `aimPoint` aims from: the camera drawn, the picture's aspect, the devices and the world.
- `onFloor` (function): Where `ray` meets the level plane at height `y` ahead of its start, or null (level with it, or pointing away).
- `screenRay` (function): The ray through the point `at` of the picture (`[x, y]`, −1 to 1, +y up), in true heights (see the file comment).
- `STICK_REACH` (const): How far from the player a right stick pushed all the way aims (m): twin sticks aim by direction.
- `Vec3` (type): A point or direction, m.

- `ActionMap` (type from [`engine/input/actionMaps.ts`](../engine/input/actionMaps.ts)): An action map entry.

- `AimDevices` (type from [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)): What the devices give aiming: the pointer and the right stick (see `AimView`).
- `aimPoint` (function from [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)): The point the rule aims at this frame (see the file comment), or undefined.
- `AimPose` (interface from [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)): A camera's pose as aiming reads it: engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts's `CameraPose` fits it.
- `AimRay` (interface from [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)): A ray: where it starts and its unit direction.
- `AimRule` (type from [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)): What aims a player's look or pointer, by an action map's `aim`: see the file comment.
- `AimView` (interface from [`engine/input/aim.ts`](../engine/input/aim.ts)): What `aimPoint` aims from: the camera drawn, the picture's aspect, the devices and the world.
- `Bindings` (interface from [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)): An action map with the player's changes.
- `BindingsFile` (interface from [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)): A saved bindings file.
- `BindingsOptions` (interface from [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)): How bindings are made.
- `BindingsStorage` (interface from [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)): Where bindings are saved: the `localStorage` shape.
- `CameraInputSample` (interface from [`engine/input/input.ts`](../engine/input/input.ts)): What the camera takes each frame: mouse look `[right, up]` rad, the right stick `[right, up]`, wheel notches.
- `CameraLike` (interface from [`engine/input/input.ts`](../engine/input/input.ts)): A camera as the input reads it (the app's, over its view): its heading, its pitch for the look, and the aim.
- `codeLabel` (function from [`engine/input/codes.ts`](../engine/input/codes.ts)): What a prompt shows for `code`: `W`, `Space`, `LMB`, `A` / `Cross`, `L Stick Up`, `Hold X`.
- `connectVirtualDevice` (function from [`engine/input/devices/inspector.ts`](../engine/input/devices/inspector.ts)): Gives `host` (the app's inspector host) the page input's virtual device, so `__engine.input` drives the page.
- `createBindings` (function from [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)): Makes the bindings of the action map `map` (an id or an entry), loading saved changes from `options.storage`.
- `createInput` (function from [`engine/input/input.ts`](../engine/input/input.ts)): Makes the page's input.
- `createScriptedGamepad` (function from [`engine/input/devices/padScript.ts`](../engine/input/devices/padScript.ts)): Makes a scripted pad in slot `index` (0); call `next()` once per frame, before the input samples.
- `createVirtualDevice` (function from [`engine/input/devices/virtual.ts`](../engine/input/devices/virtual.ts)): Makes a virtual device, holding nothing.

- `DEGREES_PER_COUNT` (const from [`engine/input/look.ts`](../engine/input/look.ts)): One mouse count at sensitivity 1, degrees: Source's and Apex's `m_yaw` and `m_pitch`.
- `DeviceKind` (type from [`engine/input/codes.ts`](../engine/input/codes.ts)): The devices input comes from; `virtual` is the inspector's (engine/input/devices/virtual.ts).

- `GamepadLike` (interface from [`engine/input/devices/gamepad.ts`](../engine/input/devices/gamepad.ts)): The Gamepad API's `Gamepad`, as far as the device reads it (a test stub gives just this).

- `HOLD_PREFIX` (const from [`engine/input/codes.ts`](../engine/input/codes.ts)): The prefix of a held binding: `Hold:PadWest` is X kept down `HOLD_TIME` (see the file comment).
- `HOLD_TIME` (const from [`engine/input/codes.ts`](../engine/input/codes.ts)): How long a held binding's code stays down before its action presses, s (ours); let go sooner, it is a tap.

- `InputOptions` (interface from [`engine/input/input.ts`](../engine/input/input.ts)): How an input is made; in a page every field has its default.

### [`engine/input/bindings.ts`](../engine/input/bindings.ts)

### [`engine/input/codes.ts`](../engine/input/codes.ts)

- `codeLabel` (function): What a prompt shows for `code`: `W`, `Space`, `LMB`, `A` / `Cross`, `L Stick Up`, `Hold X`.

- `deviceOf` (function): The device a code belongs to.
- `heldBase` (function): The code a held binding waits on (`Hold:PadWest` → `PadWest`), or null for any other code.
- `HOLD_PREFIX` (const): The prefix of a held binding: `Hold:PadWest` is X kept down `HOLD_TIME` (see the file comment).
- `HOLD_TIME` (const): How long a held binding's code stays down before its action presses, s (ours); let go sooner, it is a tap.
- `holdCode` (function): The held binding of `code`: `holdCode('PadWest')` is `Hold:PadWest`.
- `InputSink` (interface): Where the devices write (engine/input/input.ts keeps it): codes going down and up, analog strengths, use.
- `isCode` (function): Whether `code` is one a binding may name.
- `LabelOptions` (interface): How labels are made: the keyboard layout's characters by code, and the pad family.
- `MOUSE_BUTTONS` (const): Mouse buttons by `MouseEvent.button` (0 left, 1 middle, 2 right, 3 back, 4 forward).
- `PAD_BUTTONS` (const): The W3C standard gamepad buttons by index, named by position.
- `PAD_STICKS` (const): The stick directions, each a code whose strength is how far the stick leans that way (after the deadzone).
- `padStyle` (function): The family of a gamepad, from its `Gamepad.id` (vendor 054c is Sony, 057e Nintendo).
- `PadStyle` (type): A gamepad family, for labels.
- `readKeyboardLayout` (function): The page's keyboard layout (`navigator.keyboard.getLayoutMap()`, Chromium), or undefined where it is missing.
- `TOUCH_PREFIX` (const): The prefix of the codes touch buttons write: `touch:jump` is the jump button (`touchCode`).
- `touchCode` (function): The code a touch button for `action` writes; every action binds its own (engine/input/input.ts).
- `WHEEL_CODES` (const): The wheel's codes: a notch is a tap, never held.

### [`engine/input/devices/gamepad.ts`](../engine/input/devices/gamepad.ts)

- `createGamepadDevice` (function): Makes the gamepad device over `source`, writing to `sink`.

### [`engine/input/devices/mouse.ts`](../engine/input/devices/mouse.ts)

- `attachMouse` (function): Listens to the mouse over `targets.element`; `lookSpeed` rad/px, `invertY` for flight-style look.

### [`engine/input/devices/touch.ts`](../engine/input/devices/touch.ts)

- `attachTouch` (function): Listens to fingers over the page (see the file comment).
- `BUTTON_SLOP` (const): A release on a button or tap control that moved less than this (CSS px) is a tap, however long it was down.
- `HOLD_FRAMES` (const): … and is seen by at least this many frames, so a slow frame never turns a tap into a hold.
- `HOLD_TIME` (const): A hold lasts at least this long (s) …
- `MOUSE_SLOP` (const): The mouse ends touch mode once it moves more than this (CSS px) from the last pointer.
- `STICK_DEAD` (const): The stick's dead zone, as a fraction of its reach.
- `STICK_FULL` (const): Where the stick reaches full speed, as a fraction of its reach.
- `STICK_RADIUS` (const): The stick's reach in CSS px: full speed at its rim.
- `stickAxis` (function): The stick's `[right, forward]` for a thumb `dx`, `dy` CSS px from the centre (`touch.rs:266-272`).
- `StickView` (interface): Where the stick is drawn, in client CSS px: its centre and its knob.
- `TAP_SLOP` (const): A tap on the game moves less than this (CSS px).
- `TAP_TIME` (const): A tap on the game is shorter than this (s), or seen by a single frame.
- `TOUCH_SETTINGS` (const): The touch settings: view settings, never in the hash.
- `TouchDevice` (interface): The touch device.
- `TouchOptions` (interface): How the device behaves beyond its targets.
- `TouchSetting` (type): The `touch` setting: touch mode as detected (`auto`), or forced `on` or `off`.
- `TouchTargets` (interface): Where the touch device listens.

### [`engine/input/devices/virtual.ts`](../engine/input/devices/virtual.ts)

- `createVirtualDevice` (function): Makes a virtual device, holding nothing.

### [`engine/input/input.ts`](../engine/input/input.ts)

- `CameraInputSample` (interface): What the camera takes each frame: mouse look `[right, up]` rad, the right stick `[right, up]`, wheel notches.

- `InputOptions` (interface): How an input is made; in a page every field has its default.

### [`engine/input/intents.ts`](../engine/input/intents.ts)

- `applyIntents` (function): The next step's intents: `prev`'s held keys with `change` applied (`null` clears a key), then normalized with `prev` as the step before, so `p` is the change's presses plus the new edges of `b`.
- `BUFFER_STEPS` (const): How long a press stays buffered by default, in steps: 9, the prototype's 0.15 s at 60 Hz.
- `buffered` (function): Whether `button` was pressed within the last `steps` steps (its press step counts as 0) and not consumed since.
- `consume` (function): Uses up `button`'s latest press, so `buffered` is false until it is pressed again (a jump done, say).
- `consumeAll` (function): Uses up every pending press, so closing a menu does not also attack with the press that closed it.
- `createInputBuffer` (function): A fresh input buffer: nothing held, pressed or consumed.
- `CustomIntentKey` (type): A namespaced key for game code's own intents: `'game:charge'`.
- `diffIntents` (function): The change-point from `prev` to `next` (both normalized, `prev` the step before): each held key whose value changed, `null` for one that went away, and `p` only for presses the edges of `b` do not explain.
- `fromCamera` (function): Turns a stick or keys into a world-space move, so pushing forward walks away from the camera: `axes` is `[right, forward]` (W is `[0, 1]`, D is `[1, 0]`) and `yaw` the camera heading.
- `held` (function): Whether `button` is held this step.
- `InputBuffer` (interface): What a body remembers of its buttons across steps: plain data for a component field (`type: 'object'`, default `createInputBuffer()`), so it is hashed, captured and restored.
- `INTENT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `INTENT_KEYS` (const): The built-in keys, in the order a normalized object holds them, each with what it means.
- `IntentChanges` (type): A replay change-point's intent part: the keys that changed, `null` for a key cleared, `p` for unexplained presses.
- `IntentKey` (type): A built-in key.
- `Intents` (type): One step's intents, as the sim reads them (systems get them as their second argument).
- `IntentValue` (type): A custom intent's value: plain data, as a replay file holds it.
- `NO_INTENTS` (const): No intents: what a step gets when nothing is given.
- `normalizeIntents` (function): Checks `raw` and returns the step's intents: frozen, keys in order (built-ins, then custom keys sorted), buttons sorted, `p` widened by the edges of `b` since `previous` (the step before; none at the start).
- `pressed` (function): Whether `button` was pressed this step: it went down (or was tapped) since the step before.
- `released` (function): Whether `button` went up on the buffer's step (a tap shorter than a step included).
- `REPEAT_DELAY` (const): Steps a button is held before it first repeats: 18, the prototype's 0.3 s at 60 Hz.
- `REPEAT_RATE` (const): Steps between repeats after the first: 5, the prototype's 0.08 s at 60 Hz, rounded.
- `repeated` (function): Whether `button` fires on the buffer's step as a held key repeats: on its press, then after `delay` steps held, then every `rate` steps (menu cursors, puzzle pieces).
- `updateInputBuffer` (function): Records one step's intents in `buffer` (changed in place, and returned): call it once per step, with the world's `tick`, before reading `released`, `buffered` or `repeated`.

### [`engine/input/look.ts`](../engine/input/look.ts)

- `DEGREES_PER_COUNT` (const): One mouse count at sensitivity 1, degrees: Source's and Apex's `m_yaw` and `m_pitch`.
- `LOOK_SETTING_FIELDS` (const): The view settings the input reads (see the file comment), as fields; never in the hash.
- `LOOK_SETTINGS` (const): The view settings the input reads, declared on the shared registry.
- `lookOptions` (function): The look settings through `get` (a settings store's `get`); a value it lacks is the field's default.
- `LookOptions` (interface): The look settings, read: what `scaleLook` takes.
- `RawLook` (interface): A frame's raw look: mouse counts `[right, up]` (up for a push away) and the right stick `[x, y]` (y down).
- `ScaledLook` (interface): What the camera takes (engine/gfx/cameras/pose.ts `CameraInput`): look `[right, up]` in rad, turn as rates.
- `scaleLook` (function): What the camera takes from `raw` under `options`, aiming down sights or not (see the file comment).

### [`engine/input/script.ts`](../engine/input/script.ts)

- `names` (const): Reads a comma-separated list of names: `South,North`.
- `numbers` (function): Reads `n` comma-separated finite numbers: `0,-1`.
- `parseScript` (function): Parses `text` with `keys` (key → reader); `match` admits extra keys by pattern (`game:charge`).
- `SCRIPT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `ScriptLine` (interface): One line of a script: how many frames or steps it lasts, its values by key, and its line number (from 1).
- `ValueReader` (type): Reads one value, or returns a problem as a string.

### [`engine/physics/binding.ts`](../engine/physics/binding.ts)

- `attachPhysics` (function): Binds `physics` to a sim world and steps it there: the system `physics`, in the phase of that name.
- `BINDING_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `bindPhysics` (function): Binds a physics world to a sim world, so `physicsOf(w)` finds it (the scene does this when it starts).
- `hasPhysics` (function): Whether a sim world has a physics world bound to it.
- `physicsOf` (function): The physics world of a sim world: its bodies and queries.
- `scenePhysics` (function): For a scene that asks for physics: a new physics world, with `physics.gravity` declared on `registry` if it lacks it.

### [`engine/physics/bodies.ts`](../engine/physics/bodies.ts)

- `addBall` (function): Adds a ball prop; returns its id.
- `addBox` (function): Adds a box prop, sized as BoxGeometry (full width, height, depth); returns its id.
- `addCapsule` (function): Adds a capsule prop, standing up (`height` is its straight middle, as CapsuleGeometry's); returns its id.
- `addCylinder` (function): Adds a cylinder prop, standing up (a barrel); returns its id.
- `addProp` (function): Adds a dynamic body of one `shape` (a hull too: a rock), of `PROP_MATERIAL` unless `spec` says otherwise; its id.
- `addSensor` (function): Adds a body whose one collider is a sensor of `shape`: it blocks nothing and detects bodies.
- `applyTorqueImpulse` (function): Turns a body: an angular impulse (N·m·s) about its centre of mass, waking it.
- `driveBody` (function): Sets a kinematic body's velocities so that it reaches `position` and `rotation` when the world steps `dt`.
- `driveMover` (function): Drives a mover's body toward its pose at `sim.time` (the end of the step being run): `driveMover(physics, m, w)`.
- `knock` (function): Knocks a body away from `from`: a push across the ground and up, a tip toward the push and a twist (`knockProp`).
- `KnockOptions` (interface): How hard `knock` hits: speeds, the same for every mass.
- `Mover` (interface): A mover: a kinematic body's path as a function of time (`MOVER_FIELDS` says what each field means).
- `MOVER` (const): A mover with every field at its default (no body).
- `MOVER_FIELDS` (const): A mover's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('platform', { description, fields: MOVER_FIELDS })`.
- `moverPose` (function): Where a mover is at `time` (s): back and forth along its offset, turning at its spin (shardfall's `amount`).
- `PROP_MATERIAL` (const): The props' material: a hollow wooden crate's (24 kg at 0.75 m), Coulomb friction, a little bounce, and damping that lets a knocked prop slide and roll to rest.
- `PropSpec` (interface): A prop as `addProp` takes it: a body's pose, velocities and options, and its material.
- `sensorHits` (function): The dynamic and kinematic bodies a body's sensors overlapped at the last step, in id order.
- `SensorSpec` (interface): Where a sensor goes and how it moves.
- `Trigger` (interface): A trigger: its sensor body and the bodies inside it.
- `TRIGGER_FIELDS` (const): A trigger's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('zone', { description, fields: TRIGGER_FIELDS })`.
- `updateTrigger` (function): Brings `trigger.inside` up to date with its sensor and returns the bodies that entered and left, in id order.

### [`engine/physics/capture.ts`](../engine/physics/capture.ts)

- `bodyId` (function): The body id of a Rapier handle: `slot + generation · 2³²`.
- `bodyIds` (function): Every body's id, in id order.
- `CAPTURE_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `capturePhysics` (function): The world as a capture: Rapier's snapshot, a fresh copy, with the build that took it.
- `handleOf` (function): The Rapier handle of a body id.
- `liveBody` (function): The body `id` names, or null: removed, never added, or its slot reused since by a newer body.
- `PhysicsCapture` (interface): The physics part of a capture: Rapier's snapshot, with the build and version that took it.
- `physicsState` (function): What the hash covers: per body, in id order, its id, translation, rotation, linear and angular velocity.
- `rapierBuild` (function): The Rapier build and version a capture records, `'simd-compat 0.21.0'`: snapshots restore only into the same.
- `restorePhysics` (function): A new world from a capture (checked first: `PHYSICS_BAD_CAPTURE`); the capture is left as it was.
- `STATE_STRIDE` (const): Numbers a body takes in the hashed state: id, translation (3), rotation (4), linear and angular velocity (3 each).

### [`engine/physics/carry.ts`](../engine/physics/carry.ts)

- `carried` (function): Runs `move` with the carry of the kinematic body `floor` (where the step takes the point under the feet: turned about its centre of mass and moved, as Rapier integrates it; zero for any other floor or none), that body's velocities held at zero meanwhile, so Rapier's kinematic friction adds nothing.

### [`engine/physics/character.ts`](../engine/physics/character.ts)

- `addCharacter` (function from [`engine/physics/characterBody.ts`](../engine/physics/characterBody.ts)): Adds a character's body (a kinematic capsule, group `actor`), its bottom just outside the skin above `feet`.
- `bodyAt` (function from [`engine/physics/characterBody.ts`](../engine/physics/characterBody.ts)): Where a character's body stands for its feet at `feet`: its capsule's bottom just outside the skin above them.
- `Character` (type): A character's settings, filled: what `createCharacter` returns and an actor's component holds.
- `CHARACTER_FIELDS` (const): A character's settings: `createCharacter` checks a spec against these and fills the defaults.
- `CHARACTER_SETTINGS` (const): The character's settings (the setting `physics.characterGravity`).
- `CHARACTER_STATE_FIELDS` (const): What a character remembers between ticks: plain data in its actor's component, hashed and captured with the sim.
- `CharacterInput` (interface): What a character wants this tick: from the intents (engine/sim/actors.ts) or from its AI.
- `CharacterState` (type): A character's own state, as `stepCharacter` reads and writes it (`CHARACTER_STATE_FIELDS` documents each field).
- `CharacterStep` (interface): What one tick did.
- `createCharacter` (function): Checks a character's settings and fills the defaults; throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming each problem.
- `createCharacterState` (function): A character's state at rest, every field at its default.
- `feetOf` (function from [`engine/physics/characterBody.ts`](../engine/physics/characterBody.ts)): Where a character's feet are: the bottom of its capsule as it is now (a crouch shrinks it, engine/physics/hull.ts), less the skin (on flat ground, the ground's height).
- `MoveEntered` (type): A move entered: a mode of the model's (a mantle, a climb, a ladder, a zipline, a skydive), a slide, a crouch or standing up.
- `stepCharacter` (function): One sim tick of a character: `steer` turns its intents into a velocity and a move (engine/physics/feel.ts), the controller makes the move (`moveCharacter`), `settle` fixes the velocity from what happened, walls stop the velocity going into them, it pushes what it walked into (both leave at (push·v + m·u)/(push + m)), probes the ground under it and presses a dynamic floor with push × world gravity.
- `StepOptions` (interface): What `stepCharacter` needs beside the character: the step length, the gravities and the one-way platforms.

### [`engine/physics/characterBody.ts`](../engine/physics/characterBody.ts)

- `addCharacter` (function): Adds a character's body (a kinematic capsule, group `actor`), its bottom just outside the skin above `feet`.
- `bodyAt` (function): Where a character's body stands for its feet at `feet`: its capsule's bottom just outside the skin above them.
- `feetOf` (function): Where a character's feet are: the bottom of its capsule as it is now (a crouch shrinks it, engine/physics/hull.ts), less the skin (on flat ground, the ground's height).

### [`engine/physics/crowd.ts`](../engine/physics/crowd.ts)

- `addAgent` (function): Adds a queued agent's body now (`updateCrowd` does it through the queue), its feet at `x`, `y`, `z`, moving at `vx`, `vy`, `vz`; returns its id.
- `AgentState` (type): Where an agent is in its life: see `CROWD_AGENT_FIELDS.state`.
- `CROWD_AGENT` (const): An agent with every field at its default: queued, a walker's capsule at the origin.
- `CROWD_AGENT_FIELDS` (const): A crowd agent's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('pusher', { description, fields: … })`.
- `CROWD_GROUNDED` (const): The grounded heuristic's thresholds (m/s, m): the prototype's 6 units/s, 2 units and 1 unit/s.
- `CROWD_LIMITS` (const): What `updateCrowd` does at most each step by default: bodies added (shardfall's load ramps), corpses kept.
- `CROWD_MATERIAL` (const): The crowd's material: the prototype's density (1 a cubic unit: a walker weighs about 50 kg), no friction under the min rule (an agent slides on everything), no bounce; a corpse's friction, averaged, so it slides to a stop.
- `CrowdAgent` (interface): A crowd agent: its body, its make and what the last readback saw (`CROWD_AGENT_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `CrowdChanges` (interface): What one `updateCrowd` changed: indices into the list it was given, in order.
- `CrowdOptions` (interface): How `updateCrowd` runs.
- `CrowdStepper` (interface): What the crowd's calls read from the sim: the step length (s).
- `killAgent` (function): Kills an agent: its body joins the group `corpse` (the world and props still stop it; the crowd walks through it) with `CROWD_MATERIAL.corpseFriction`, and a flyer falls.
- `knockback` (function): Adds `velocity` (m/s) to an agent or corpse in the world, the same for every mass, waking it.
- `launch` (function): Throws an agent or corpse up: its upward speed becomes at least `up` (m/s) and its speed across the ground is multiplied by `carry` (1; the prototype's kill launch: 1.3).
- `removeAgent` (function): Removes an agent's body now (`updateCrowd` does it for `leaving` agents and old corpses): it is `gone`.
- `setVelocity` (function): Moves a living agent's velocity toward `want` by at most `acceleration × dt` this step: across the ground (a flyer: up and down too), keeping the vertical speed gravity and the solver gave it.
- `updateCrowd` (function): The crowd's step, after the physics step (the phase `readback`), over every agent in id order: reads each body back (feet, velocity, `grounded`); brakes grounded corpses and removes those `corpseTime` old, then the oldest beyond `corpseCap`; removes `leaving` agents; adds the bodies of up to `spawnLimit` queued agents.
- `VelocityOptions` (interface): How `setVelocity` steers.

### [`engine/physics/feel.ts`](../engine/physics/feel.ts)

- `createFeelMeter` (function): A new meter for ticks of `dt` seconds.
- `FeelMeter` (interface): A meter: the report so far and what it is in the middle of measuring.
- `FeelReport` (interface): What `measureFeel` reports.
- `FeelSample` (interface): One tick of a character, as the meter reads it.
- `MotionFeel` (interface): The shooter model's feel numbers (engine/sim/feelCourse.ts): speeds in m/s, times in s, heights in m.
- `settle` (function): The feel of one tick, after the move: landing ends a fall (returns the landing speed when above 2 m/s, else 0), a head bump ends a rise, a dash's last tick leaves at most the run speed, and it faces where it dashes or is told to go.
- `steer` (function): The feel of one tick, before the move: timers count, a dash starts, the velocity across the ground follows the momentum model (acceleration, deceleration when let go, skid against its motion, `airControl` in the air), jumps start (coyote time, buffer, wall jump), letting go cuts a rise (`variableJump`), and gravity acts, integrated exactly.
- `Steering` (interface): What `steer` decided for a tick: the move it asks for, and what it started.
- `updateFeelMeter` (function): Reads one tick into the meter (the file comment gives the rules).

### [`engine/physics/groups.ts`](../engine/physics/groups.ts)

- `COLLISION_GROUPS` (const): The collision groups: each one's membership bit and the groups it touches.
- `dropGroups` (function): Rapier's interaction groups `bits` (a collider's `groupBits`) with the groups named taken out of what they touch: a character controller's query that passes through them (engine/physics/character.ts `shoves`), the collider itself still touching them in the solver.
- `GROUP_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `GROUP_NAMES` (const): The group names, in table order.
- `groupBits` (function): Rapier's interaction groups for a collider of `group`: its membership bit and the bits of what it touches.
- `GroupName` (type): A collision group's name.
- `queryBits` (function): Rapier's interaction groups for a query that hits the groups named (all of them when none are).
- `touches` (function): Whether colliders of groups `a` and `b` touch.

### [`engine/physics/heightfield.ts`](../engine/physics/heightfield.ts)

- `heightfieldDesc` (function): Rapier's collider description of `shape`, checked (see the file comment); `where` names it in errors.
- `HeightfieldShape` (interface): A heightfield, for bodies only (see the file comment).

### [`engine/physics/hull.ts`](../engine/physics/hull.ts)

- `hullFits` (function): Whether a capsule of straight middle `height` fits where `character`'s body is, its feet or its centre kept (see the file comment): what standing up asks before it stands.
- `hullHeight` (function): A character's capsule's straight middle now (m): its standing one, or what a crouch made it.
- `HullKeep` (type): What a new hull keeps where it is: the feet (on the ground) or the centre (in the air).
- `matchHull` (function): Gives `character`'s body the hull of straight middle `height` unless it has it: on the ground keeping the feet; in the `air` growing about the centre where that fits, else from the feet, and shrinking about the centre when the crouch began in the air (`tuck`: the feet tucked up), else from the top.
- `setHull` (function): Gives `character`'s body a capsule of straight middle `height`, its feet or its centre kept where they are.

### [`engine/physics/joints.ts`](../engine/physics/joints.ts)

- `addJoint` (function): Joins two bodies, or a body to the world, as `spec` says (see the file comment); returns the joint's id.
- `hasJoint` (function): Whether the joint exists.
- `JOINT_CODES` (const): The codes this module raises, with their fixes.
- `jointBodies` (function): The two bodies a joint holds: `a` and `b`, or the anchor and `a` for a joint to the world.
- `JointKind` (type): A joint's kind as data (see the file comment): springs and damping per second², angles in radians.
- `joints` (function): Every joint's id, in id order.
- `JointSpec` (interface): A joint as `addJoint` takes it.
- `removeJoint` (function): Removes a joint (a joint to the world leaves its anchor, `jointBodies(…)[0]`).

### [`engine/physics/ledge.ts`](../engine/physics/ledge.ts)

- `findLedge` (function): A ledge on top of `wall` that `character` can mantle onto, within `search.reach` above its feet, or null.
- `findWall` (function): A wall ahead of `character` along `dir` (a unit `[x, z]`) within `probe` of its hull, steeper than it walks, or null.
- `Ledge` (interface): A ledge `findLedge` found (see the file comment).
- `ledgePath` (function): The mantle's path for a ledge, the feet's (see the file comment): from `feet` across to the column `rise`, up it until the feet stand two skins over the lip and the landing, across to over `landing`, then down onto it.
- `LedgeSearch` (interface): How `findLedge` looks: how high a lip it takes above the feet (m).
- `Wall` (interface): A wall `findWall` found ahead.

### [`engine/physics/move.ts`](../engine/physics/move.ts)

- `CharacterHit` (interface): One obstacle the controller met: the body, the point it touched and that surface's outward normal.
- `CharacterMove` (interface): What `moveCharacter` did: the translation it made, whether it ended grounded, and what it hit.
- `halfHeightOf` (function): The half height of a character's capsule now: its standing one, exactly, unless a crouch changed it (engine/physics/hull.ts), when the capsule's own, which Rapier keeps as a float32.
- `isWalkable` (function): Whether `character` can stand on a surface: no steeper than it climbs.
- `isWall` (function): Whether a surface is a wall to `character`: steeper than it climbs, not a ceiling.
- `moveCharacter` (function): Moves a character's capsule by `desired` as far as it can: across first (sliding along walls, up slopes it climbs, pushing props), then down or up alone.
- `MoveOptions` (interface): How `moveCharacter` moves: whether it stands on the ground (and is not rising), and the one-way platforms.
- `oneWayFilter` (function): The filter that makes one-way platforms solid only to feet at or above their top, less a grace.
- `partsOf` (function): The Rapier body of a character, with its capsule (its first collider); throws `PHYSICS_BAD_ARGUMENT`.
- `QUERY_FLAGS` (const): Sensors never block a character: the flags of every query its controller makes.
- `queryGroups` (function): The groups a character's controller queries: its collider's, less the groups it `shoves` (groups.ts `dropGroups`).
- `sink` (function): How far a character goes down `by` (< 0) with its sinking `floor`, from where its last move left the capsule: a controller move that leaves the floor out, so a ledge it overhangs holds it up rather than taking it in.

### [`engine/physics/movement/air.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/air.ts)

- `airMove` (function): Quake's air acceleration (see the file comment): one tick of `h` toward `wish`, at most length 1.
- `hopSpeed` (function): The speed a jump `sinceLand` seconds after landing leaves of `speed` (m/s): the bunny-hop cost (see the file comment).
- `jumpScale` (function): The share of the jump's height a jump `sinceLand` seconds after landing gets (`fatigued`: that flight began with a jump).
- `land` (function): A landing: the fall height it counts (the impact `velocity`'s speed along the floor's unit `normal`, as v²/2g, at least what is left of the last landing's), written to `motion` with the landing's age reset; returns the share of speed the stun leaves at once, which the caller applies to the velocity across the ground.
- `landSlowdown` (function): The stun's share of speed `t` seconds after a landing that counted `fall` metres (see the file comment).
- `lurch` (function): The lurch of a new key (`newKey`) `t` seconds after the take-off: turns `h` toward the same speed along the move `wish`.
- `lurchStrength` (function): The lurch's strength `t` seconds after the take-off (see the file comment).
- `newKey` (function): Whether the move's `keys` (`[right, forward]` in their frame) are a new key against last tick's `before`: pressed from none, or turned by `lurch.turn` or more.

### [`engine/physics/movement/climb.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/climb.ts)

- `keepSpace` (function): Keeps the climb space's foot: the feet's height on the ground, dragged down by a fall below it off the ground.
- `stepClimb` (function): One tick of a climb (see the file comment): `'climb'` when it climbs on (its velocity set), `'mantle'` when it topped out (the grab started), `'air'` when it let go, bounced off or ended in the end boost.
- `tryClimb` (function): Starts a climb if one takes (see the file comment); true when it did.
- `wallBounce` (function): A jump off the wall (see the file comment): by the zone the feet at `feet` stand in over the climb space's foot.

### [`engine/physics/movement/crouch.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/crouch.ts)

- `crouchBlocks` (function): Whether its crouch keeps a jump from happening this tick (Apex's CheckJumpButton): a toggled crouch stands up instead (and ends, unless `crouch.jump`), and getting up never jumps; out of a slide, both jump.
- `ducking` (const): Whether the duck is down or going down (Apex's `ducking()`).
- `DuckInput` (interface): What `updateDuck` reads beside the model and the state: the crouch buttons, and the slide's start.
- `endSlide` (function): Ends the slide (Apex's EndSlide).
- `FloorNormal` (type): A floor's normal, `[x, y, z]`, unit.
- `hullFor` (function): The straight middle of the hull its stance has (m): the character's capsule standing, the model's crouched.
- `slideJump` (function): A boosted slide's jump (Apex's CheckJumpButton): jumped while its duck still goes, within `slide.dead` of its start, the boost comes back off (a dead slide); between `slide.longFrom` of `slide.long` and `slide.long`, the speed jumps at `slide.long` (the long jump).
- `SlideStart` (interface): What `tryStartSlide` reads beside the model and the state.
- `slopePull` (function): Part of the slide's pull along the floor (see the file comment): `h` gains `share · g · dt · n_y` of its slant.
- `tryStartSlide` (function): Apex's TryStartSlide (see the file comment).
- `updateDuck` (function): Apex's update_duck (see the file comment): updates the duck, the stance and the slide in `motion`.

### [`engine/physics/movement/ground.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/ground.ts)

- `accelerate` (function): Apex's Accelerate: adds along `dir` up to `wishSpeed`, at most `rate × dt`, never past max(old speed, wished).
- `decelerate` (function): Apex's Decelerate: brakes `h` in place, all but the part along `dir` the input pushes for (up to `wishSpeed`), at the standing rate (the sprint's above the run, the crouch's crouched; a slide's own, then its decay), never below 0.
- `directionShare` (function): The share of its gait's speed a move gets by its direction from the view: `gaits.side` straight across it, `gaits.back` straight back, blended by the squares of the move's parts across and back (so exactly 1 when both are 1, as in Apex); 1 with no view.
- `gaitSpeed` (function): The speed its gait goes at, before the move scale: the crouch-walk crouched, the walk walking, the sprint sprinting (dipping toward `gaits.sprintSide` as the move turns 45° off the view), else the run; every gait but the sprint times its `directionShare`.
- `groundAccel` (function): Apex's GetAccel: the acceleration at horizontal speed `speed`, by the speed at the tick's start (m/s²).
- `SlideBrake` (interface): How a slide brakes: hard (`slide.brake`) with crouch let go or the move against it, else `slide.decel`.
- `SprintInput` (interface): What `updateSprint` reads beside the model and the state.
- `updateSprint` (function): Apex's sticky sprint (see the file comment): updates `motion.sticky`, `stickyLeft` and `sprinting`.
- `walkMove` (function): Apex's WalkMove: one tick of `h` across the ground toward `wish` (at most length 1) at `maxSpeed`: the stick curve (a move shorter than 1 counts as length × (2 − length), a sprinting move 1.25 times longer, capped at 1), then `decelerate`, then `accelerate` at `groundAccel` of the speed it started with.

### [`engine/physics/movement/ladder.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/ladder.ts)

- `stepLadder` (function): One tick on a ladder (see the file comment): the feet's next point on it; `'mantle'` when it starts the mantle over its top (the caller steps the mantle); null once it let go or stepped off at its foot (the tick goes on in the air).
- `tryLadder` (function): Takes hold of a ladder in reach if one takes (see the file comment); true when it did.

### [`engine/physics/movement/mantle.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/mantle.ts)

- `crouchPressed` (const): Whether the crouch went down this tick: the held button's press or the toggle's.
- `glide` (function): The superglide (see the file comment), or with `boost` the mantle boost: across the ground at `mantle.glide` times the exit speed along the push (else over the ledge), less the slide's boost within its cooldown unless `boost`.
- `handsOf` (function): Where each hand goes on the lip, left then right as it faces the wall, `shoulder` metres apart along the edge: the contacts the animation reads (WP 13.11), from the lip and the wall's normal the motion state holds.
- `MantleTick` (interface): What a mantle's tick reads beside the states: the tick's own numbers, as steerMotion has them.
- `MantleTry` (interface): What `tryMantle` reads beside a tick's numbers.
- `startMantle` (function): Starts a mantle up `ledge` from the feet at `feet`: a grab, or for a low ledge only the pull (see the file comment).
- `stepMantle` (function): One tick of a mantle (see the file comment): the feet's next point on the path, or null once it hopped out or let go (the tick goes on in the air) or, its pull done the tick before, stepped off onto the top (it goes on there).
- `tryMantle` (function): Starts a mantle if one takes (see the file comment); true when it did.

### [`engine/physics/movement/model.ts`](../engine/physics/movement/model.ts)
