- `TouchButtonSpec` (interface): One button of a touch layout.
- `TouchLayer` (interface): The touch controls' layer in a page.
- `TouchLayerState` (interface): What the layer shows this frame.
- `TouchLayout` (type): A touch layout entry.
- `touchLayoutKind` (function): Declares the kind `touchlayout` on `registry` unless it has it.
- `TouchLayoutSpec` (interface): How a touch layout is written.
- `touchScale` (function): The scale of the touch controls for a screen `width` × `height` CSS px: `--touch-k`.
- `TouchSlot` (interface): Where a button sits: its centre's distance from the right and bottom edges, and its diameter, in k CSS px.

### [`engine/ui/widgets.ts`](../engine/ui/widgets.ts)

- `BarOptions` (interface): How `createBar` makes a bar.
- `createBar` (function): A filled bar in `parent` (see the file comment); `set(value)` moves its fill.
- `createBox` (function): A window frame in `parent` (see the file comment); `set(text)` changes its body.
- `createHearts` (function): A row of hearts in `parent` (see the file comment); `set([hp, max])` changes them.
- `createPadCursor` (function): The pad's cursor over `root` (see the file comment), from `input`.
- `createRepeat` (function): A held direction's repeat: `(input, action, dt)` is true on the press and on each repeat while held.
- `HeartsOptions` (interface): How `createHearts` makes a row of hearts.
- `PadCursor` (interface): A gamepad's cursor over a page (see the file comment).
- `REPEAT` (const): How long a held direction waits before it repeats, then between repeats (s).
- `setText` (function): Sets `el`'s text when it differs.
- `UiBoxOptions` (interface): How `createBox` makes a window frame.
- `UiCue` (type): A cue a widget asks the page to play.
- `uiElement` (function): An element `tag` of `className` in `parent`'s document, marked `data-ui=kind` (and `data-id`) when given.
- `UiInput` (interface): What a widget reads of a page's input (engine/input/input.ts's `Input` is one): the system layer's actions.
- `UiSound` (type): Plays a cue (the page's audio); widgets without one stay silent.
- `Widget` (interface): A widget made by this module: its element, an update and its removal.
- `widgetStyle` (function): Adds the widgets' stylesheet to `doc` once.

### [`engine/world/ai.ts`](../engine/world/ai.ts)

- `ATTACK_TOKENS` (const): Attack tokens with every field at its default: 3 tokens, none held.
- `ATTACK_TOKENS_FIELDS` (const): The attack tokens' fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('tokens', { description, fields: … })`.
- `AttackTokens` (interface): Attack tokens: who holds one and when the next may be granted (`ATTACK_TOKENS_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `canSee` (function): Whether an agent with its feet at `from` is aware of a target with its feet at `to`: within `range` metres on the ground, and either within `near` metres or in a clear sight line from its eye to the target's `aim`.
- `clearSight` (function): Whether the straight line from (ax, ay, az) to (bx, by, bz) metres passes over every tile it crosses (walked in order, as Amanatides and Woo's grid traversal does): no tile's top (`level.top`) stands above the line's lowest point over that tile, and no point of it lies off the map.
- `holdsToken` (function): Whether `id` holds a token: one of the oldest `cap` grants.
- `keepTokens` (function): Keeps the tokens of the holders `keep` approves (alive, still attacking), freeing the rest: how many are held.
- `releaseToken` (function): Gives `id`'s token back (its attack ended, or was broken off): true when it held one.
- `SIGHT` (const): `canSee`'s defaults: emberdeep's 150 units of sight and 60 of sense, an eye at 1.5 m on a chest at 1 m.
- `SightOptions` (interface): How `canSee` looks.
- `takeToken` (function): Asks for a token for `id` at sim time `time` (s): true when it holds one now.

### [`engine/world/aiRoutes.ts`](../engine/world/aiRoutes.ts)

- `ASIDE` (const): How far ahead (m) someone stands in an agent's way, and how near its line (m), for `stepAside`.
- `followRoute` (function): Where an agent at `at` heads on `stops` at sim time `time` (s), and whether it stays there now: it arrives within `near` metres on the ground, stays the stop's `stay`, then heads for the next, the last leading back to the first.
- `ROUTE_FIELDS` (const): An agent's place on its route, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('route', { description, fields: … })`.
- `RouteLeg` (interface): Where `followRoute` has an agent head: the stop, and whether it stays there now.
- `RouteState` (interface): An agent's place on its route (`ROUTE_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `RouteStop` (interface): A stop of a route: where (world metres), how long to stay (s), what to do there and the way to face (rad, 0 +Z).
- `stepAside` (function): The way (a unit `[x, z]`) for an agent at `self` heading `heading` (rad, 0 along +Z) to step aside for `other` standing in its way, else null (see the file comment): to its right, or to its left when `other` is on its right.

### [`engine/world/awareness.ts`](../engine/world/awareness.ts)

- `Awareness` (interface): An agent's awareness (`AWARENESS_FIELDS` says what each field means).
- `AWARENESS` (const): An agent with every field at its default: unaware, remembering 10 s, hearing noises as loud as they are.
- `AWARENESS_FIELDS` (const): An agent's awareness fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('aware', { description, fields: … })`.
- `AWARENESS_STATES` (const): What an agent knows (see the file comment).
- `AwarenessState` (type): One of `AWARENESS_STATES`.
- `earshot` (function): How far `noise` carries to `ears` for an agent of `hearing` (m): its loudness, half through a wall.
- `hears` (function): Whether an agent at `ears` of `hearing` hears `noise` (see `earshot`).
- `Noise` (interface): A noise a step made: where, how far it carries (m), who made it (−1: nobody) and what it was (a shot, a kick).
- `sense` (function): Moves `aware` on by a step (see the file comment): sight first (it knows where he is), then the step's noises (the nearest for its earshot wins), then its memory; returns what it knows now and whether this step woke it.
- `Sensed` (interface): What `sense` found: what the agent knows now, and whether this step woke it (it knew nothing a step ago).
- `SenseInput` (interface): What `sense` reads in a step: the time, the agent's ears, whether it sees its target and where, the noises.

### [`engine/world/footsteps.ts`](../engine/world/footsteps.ts)

- `footstepSound` (function): The step a foot on `surface` plays at `gait`: its effect, gain and pitch ratio; null when the gait has none.
- `STEP_GAITS` (const): Gait → a step's gain and pitch ratio, or null: no step (see the file comment).
- `stepGait` (function): The gait a walker moving at `speed` m/s has when nothing tells it (see the file comment).
- `StepGait` (type): A walker's gait, as a step hears it: the movement model's (engine/physics/movement/model.ts `GAITS`) on its feet.
- `SURFACE_STEPS` (const): Surface tag → the step it plays (see the file comment); `'*'` for any other tag.

### [`engine/world/level/colliders.ts`](../engine/world/level/colliders.ts)

- `groundSlab` (function): The slab under the whole level, one tile wider than the map all round, from 1 m down to y 0.
- `levelColliders` (function): The colliders of every glyph with a collider recipe, by glyph id: merged boxes, hulls under `slopes`, cylinders.
- `Slopes` (interface): The level's ramps and daises (engine/world/level/shapes.ts), which the hull colliders stand under.

### [`engine/world/level/compile.ts`](../engine/world/level/compile.ts)

- `compileLevel` (function): Compiles a level's text against the legend of `options.registry` (the shared one by default) into plain data; see the file comment.
- `CompileOptions` (interface): What `compileLevel` takes beside the text.
- `levelName` (function): The name of a level file: `fixtures/levels/room.txt` → `room`.

### [`engine/world/level/glyph.ts`](../engine/world/level/glyph.ts)

- `defineGlyph` (function): Defines a glyph on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `Glyph` (type): A `glyph` entry: what one map character means.
- `GLYPH_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `glyph` entry.
- `glyphKind` (function): Declares the kind `glyph` on `registry`, with the engine's v1 to v4 glyphs, unless it has it.
- `GlyphSpec` (type): What `defineGlyph` takes: `char`, and any other field (`nav` may give one flag, the other keeping its default).
- `legendOf` (function): Every glyph of `registry` (the shared one by default), keyed by its character, in id order.
- `STOREY_FIELDS` (const): The fields only format 2 reads: a format-1 level's legend leaves them out (engine/world/level/compile.ts).

### [`engine/world/level/grid.ts`](../engine/world/level/grid.ts)

- `byText` (const): Code-unit order, so sorting never depends on the locale.
- `glyphsOf` (function): The distinct glyphs of `grid`, by id.
- `holds` (function): A predicate: whether tile (col, row) of `grid` holds one of `glyphs`.
- `TileGrid` (interface): A level's grid: its size, its tile size (m) and each tile's glyph, row-major.

### [`engine/world/level/heights.ts`](../engine/world/level/heights.ts)

- `floorBelow` (function): The height (m) of the highest surface at or under (x, y, z): a storey's floor (flat, a ramp, a flight, a dais, under a solid too), the top of a solid standing there (a low wall, a railing, a wall, the head over a door, a window or a low ceiling, even with no floor above it), a roof's top, or the ground slab under the level; null where nothing is (outside the ground slab).
- `floorHeight` (function): The walkable surface's height (m) at (x, z): the highest flat floor, ramp or dais there; 0 outside the map.
- `HeightSource` (type): What the height queries read: a compiled level, or validate.ts's view of one before it compiles; a storey's view adds its `base` (where its flat floors stand), `fullTop` (where its full glyphs rise to) and its `roofs` (a pitched one clips them).
- `roomAt` (function): The room at (x, y, z): the room of the tile under it on `storeyBelow`'s storey (a hall's stairs are the hall's to their top), or null (outside every room, on a roof, or a level without rooms).
- `solidAt` (function): Whether (x, z) is in a solid tile (a wall, a pillar, a low wall, a brazier), or outside the map.
- `storeyAt` (function): The storey a height is in (an index into `level.storeys`): the highest whose floor slab's underside is at or below `y`; 0 below them all, and in a format-1 level, which is one storey.
- `storeyBelow` (function): The storey of the surface `floorBelow` finds at (x, y, z), an index into `level.storeys` (0 in a format-1 level): a flight's tiles are the storey they rise from, all the way to their top, where `storeyAt` already reads the next; −1 on a roof, on the ground slab, or over nothing.
- `surfaceAt` (function): The surface tag underfoot at (x, z): a dais's where it stands highest, else its tile's glyph's; '' outside the map.
- `surfaceBelow` (function): The surface tag of `floorBelow`'s surface at (x, y, z): '' on the ground slab or where nothing is.
- `tileAt` (function): The tile under (x, z) metres, or null outside the map.
- `topHeight` (function): The top (m) of whatever stands at (x, z): a wall's top over its tiles, a brazier's within its radius, the floor elsewhere; 0 outside the map.

### [`engine/world/level/legend.ts`](../engine/world/level/legend.ts)

- `V1_GLYPHS` (const): The v1 glyphs by id, as `defineGlyph` specs (the kind's defaults fill the rest).
- `V2_GLYPHS` (const): The v2 glyphs by id (WP 4.2): the hall's gallery, stairs, dais and brazier.
- `V3_GLYPHS` (const): The v3 glyphs by id (WP 13.7): the ladder, which engine/world/traverse.ts's `levelLadders` stands.
- `V4_GLYPHS` (const): The v4 glyphs by id (WP 13.13): what levels written as storeys (format 2) add.

### [`engine/world/level/level.ts`](../engine/world/level/level.ts)

- `defineLevel` (function): Registers a level on `registry` (the shared one by default) after checking its text compiles against that registry's legend; returns the entry.
- `getLevel` (function): The level `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default), compiled: its name is the id without `level:`.
- `LEVEL_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `level` entry.
- `LevelEntry` (type): A `level` entry: a level's text and where it came from.

### [`engine/world/level/meshes.ts`](../engine/world/level/meshes.ts)

- `levelMeshes` (function): The mesh descriptors: one per recipe, bottom, top, surface and footprint, for every glyph whose mesh is not 'none'; with `storey` (a format-2 storey's grid), full glyphs apart from the rest, since they rise to the storey above.

### [`engine/world/level/openings.ts`](../engine/world/level/openings.ts)

- `findOpenings` (function): The openings of a storey's grid and the opening blocks that make none; `storey` gives its index and floor (m).
- `OpeningProblem` (interface): A block of an opening glyph that makes no opening, and why, for storeys.ts's problems.
- `sidesOf` (function): The tiles either side of an opening across its wall, the lower x or z first: `[col, row]` each, or null off the map.

### [`engine/world/level/parse.ts`](../engine/world/level/parse.ts)

- `LevelHeader` (interface): The front matter's values, defaults filled.
- `ParsedLevel` (interface): A level's text, read: header, map rows (each an array of characters) or storeys, positions and problems.
- `ParsedStorey` (interface): One storey of a format-2 level, read: its name, keys, map rows and their positions.
- `parseLevel` (function): Reads a level's text: its front matter, its map rows (or its storeys) and their positions, and the problems of the text itself.
- `StoreyKeys` (interface): A storey's keys as its block writes them, absent when not given (engine/world/level/storeys.ts reads them).

### [`engine/world/level/problems.ts`](../engine/world/level/problems.ts)

- `LEVEL_CODES` (const): The level codes, with their fixes (collected into docs/ERRORS.md by `x docs`).
- `LEVEL_CONTENT_CODES` (const): The content codes: `validateLevel` and `node x qa level` report them; `compileLevel` compiles a level that has them.
- `LevelCode` (type): A level code.
- `levelProblem` (function): A problem with `code` at `line`:`column`, its message filled from `values` (which name `at`).
- `LevelProblem` (interface): One problem with a level: its code, where it is (from 1, in the whole file) and the sentence naming its fix.
- `where` (const): `<file>:<line>:<column>`, the `at` of a problem's message.

### [`engine/world/level/rects.ts`](../engine/world/level/rects.ts)

- `findBlocks` (function): The 4-connected blocks of the tiles `inside` accepts, and the block index of every tile (−1 outside any).
- `mergeRects` (function): Rectangles `[col0, row0, col1, row1]` (inclusive) covering every tile of a cols × rows grid that `inside` accepts.
- `TileBlock` (interface): A 4-connected block of tiles: its first tile in reading order, its bounding rectangle and its tile count.

### [`engine/world/level/roofs.ts`](../engine/world/level/roofs.ts)

- `makeRoof` (function): A storey block's roof keys (`roof`, `pitch`, `ridge`, `eaves`) made into a roof over `site`.
- `onRoof` (function): Whether (x, z) is under the roof: in its footprint or over its eaves.
- `ROOF_SURFACE` (const): The default roof surface tag.
- `ROOF_THICKNESS` (const): A roof slab's depth, measured straight down (m).
- `roofColliders` (function): The roof's slab as convex hulls' corners (m): each plane's top and the same corners `thickness` lower.
- `roofHeight` (function): The roof's top (m) at (x, z), the surface bodies stand on; −Infinity off it.
- `RoofSite` (interface): Where a storey stands, for its roof: its index, floor, ceiling, floored tiles' bounds (m) and surface tag.
- `roofUnder` (function): The roof's underside (m) at (x, z): its top less its thickness; −Infinity off it.
- `wallUnder` (function): The corners of the convex hull of a wall under the roof (m): the rectangle `[x0, z0, x1, z1]` from `bottom` up to the roof's underside (see the file comment), over only the part of it where the underside clears `bottom`, so near the eaves, where the underside falls below the floor, no wall stands into the slab (WP 13.18: it had, up to 0.18 m).

### [`engine/world/level/rooms.ts`](../engine/world/level/rooms.ts)

- `findRooms` (function): The rooms of `storeys` (bottom first), each storey's room index per tile, and the problems; see the file comment.
- `RoomProblem` (interface): A room problem: where (the storey and tile, in reading order) and why.
- `roomSides` (function): Each opening with the rooms either side of it filled in from `roomOf` (each storey's room per tile).
- `RoomSource` (interface): One storey as `findRooms` reads it: its grid, which tiles have a floor, and its floor's height (m).

### [`engine/world/level/shapes.ts`](../engine/world/level/shapes.ts)

- `daisHeight` (function): A dais's surface height (m) at (x, z), or −Infinity off its base.
- `findDaises` (function): The daises of `grid` and the dais blocks that make none.
- `findRamps` (function): The ramps of `grid` and the ramp blocks that make none.
- `frustumPoints` (function): The corners of a dais's hull (m): its base octagon on the ground (and at its bottom, when above 0) and its top.
- `octagonRadius` (function): An octagon's "radius" at an offset from its centre: the distance to its nearest face (faces toward the axes and the diagonals).
- `outside` (function): The tiles just outside side `side` of `rect`, inside a `cols` × `rows` map.
- `rampHeight` (function): A ramp's surface height (m) at (x, z), on tiles `tile` metres wide; held to its edges' heights past them.
- `ShapeProblem` (interface): A block of a ramp or dais glyph that makes no ramp or dais, and why, for validate.ts.
- `SIDES` (const): The four sides, in the order messages list them.
- `wedgePoints` (function): The corners of a ramp's hull (m): its rectangle on the ground, and over each corner its height there when above 0.

### [`engine/world/level/storeys.ts`](../engine/world/level/storeys.ts)

- `CheckedStorey` (interface): One storey, checked: its numbers, its grid and what stands in it, ramps and daises measured from its floor.
- `CheckedStoreys` (interface): A format-2 level, checked: its storeys and rooms, or the structural problems that stop it.
- `checkStoreys` (function): The structural problems of a level written as storeys, and its checked storeys and rooms when it has none.
- `LOWEST_SLAB` (const): The floor slab under the lowest storey (m).
- `storeyView` (function): Storey `index` of `level` read as a format-1 level: its grids, ramps, daises, meshes, colliders, spawns and lights, with `base`, `fullTop` and its roof for the height queries (heights.ts), so navigation, drawing and ladders read any storey as they read a level.

### [`engine/world/level/types.ts`](../engine/world/level/types.ts)

- `BoxCollider` (interface): An axis-aligned box collider (Rapier's cuboid: half extents `(max − min)/2`, centred at `(min + max)/2`).
- `ColliderDescriptor` (type): A collider descriptor: a merged box, a hull or a cylinder, by `shape`.
- `ColliderPart` (type): What a format-2 collider holds up beyond its glyph (absent on a glyph's own): `'slab'` a storey's floor (its glyph `''`), `'head'` the wall over an opening or a low ceiling, `'roof'` a roof's slab (its glyph `''`).
- `CompiledLevel` (interface): A compiled level: the map, its legend, per-tile grids and descriptors; see the file comment.
- `CylinderCollider` (interface): An upright cylinder collider (Rapier's cylinder, three.js's CylinderGeometry): one per tile, at its centre.
- `DaisDescriptor` (interface): A dais: an octagonal frustum (faces toward the axes and the diagonals) standing on a block of a dais glyph's tiles.
- `GroundDescriptor` (interface): The slab under the whole level: the ground's collider, one tile wider than the map all round, 1 m deep.
- `HullCollider` (interface): A convex hull collider (Rapier's convex hull of its points): a ramp's wedge or a dais's frustum, from the ground.
- `LEVEL_FORMAT` (const): The format tag of a compiled level.
- `LEVEL_FORMAT_2` (const): The format tag of a compiled level written as storeys (WP 13.13).
- `LevelGlyph` (interface): One glyph as the level used it: the `glyph` entry's fields (engine/world/level/glyph.ts) and its id.
- `LightSpot` (interface): A light spot: a tile's centre, `lightHeight` above its top.
- `MeshDescriptor` (interface): What the level meshes (WP 2.4) build for one recipe at one height: the tiles, merged and as pieces.
- `OpeningDescriptor` (interface): A door or a window: a filled rectangle of an opening glyph's tiles in a wall.
- `Point3` (type): A point in metres: `[x, y, z]`.
- `RampDescriptor` (interface): A ramp: a filled rectangle of a ramp glyph's tiles (stairs) whose floor rises in a straight slope from `bottom` along the side opposite `rises` to `top` along `rises`, the side whose neighbours stand at its top (a gallery).
- `RoofDescriptor` (interface): A roof over a storey (its block's `roof` key): its shape, footprint and heights.
- `RoomDescriptor` (interface): A room: the floor a room marker's tile reaches inside walls and doors (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §6.2).
- `Side` (type): A compass side of a block: north is −Z (row 0's edge), south +Z, west −X, east +X.
- `SpawnPoint` (interface): A spawn point: a tile's centre, on its floor.
- `StoreyDescriptor` (interface): One storey of a format-2 level (WP 13.13): its heights and its own grids and descriptors, heights absolute.
- `TileRect` (type): A rectangle of tiles, inclusive: `[col0, row0, col1, row1]`.

### [`engine/world/level/validate.ts`](../engine/world/level/validate.ts)

- `CheckedLevel` (interface): A level read against its legend: the parsed text, the glyph of every tile, its slopes, and the structural problems.
- `checkLevel` (function): The structural problems of a level's text: the text's own, unknown characters and bad footprint blocks.
- `FLIGHT_LIMIT` (const): The steepest flight of stairs bodies walk (°): the shooter model's walkable slope, 45.57°, rounded down.
- `LEVEL_BODY` (const): The body format 2's content checks measure against (m): the shooter model's hull (`movement:apex`, 16 Source units in radius: 0.8128 m across; 1.8288 m tall standing, 1.19 crouched), the largest the engine ships.
- `LevelSource` (interface): Where a level comes from, for messages, and the legend to read it with.
- `NAV_CLIMB` (const): The default climb limit between neighbouring tiles' floors (m): the prototype's `CLIMB`, 3.5 units.
- `validateLevel` (function): Every problem of a level's text, structural and content (see the file comment), in a fixed order; `[]` when it is fine.

### [`engine/world/level/walk.ts`](../engine/world/level/walk.ts)

- `canStep` (function): Whether a body walks from the centre of tile (col, row) to the centre of tile (col + dc, row + dr), climbing at most `climb` metres between samples.
- `STEP_SAMPLES` (const): How many points along a step `canStep` samples the floor at.
- `StoreyArea` (interface): An area over a level's storeys: its first tile (`[storey, col, row]`, storey by storey, in reading order) and size.
- `WalkArea` (interface): An area of tiles that reach each other both ways: its first tile in reading order and its tile count.
- `walkAreas` (function): The areas of `level`'s walkable tiles under the climb limit, and the area index of every tile (−1 if unwalkable).
- `walkStoreys` (function): The areas of the walkable tiles of `storeys` (each storey's height source, one grid size), walking the 4 neighbours within a storey under the climb limit and each of `links` (pairs of tiles, each `storey · cols · rows + index`) both ways; and the area of every tile, so indexed (−1 if unwalkable).

### [`engine/world/nav.ts`](../engine/world/nav.ts)

- `FlowField` (class): Every tile's walking distance to a goal set: walk downhill to get there.
- `FlowOptions` (interface): What `flowField` takes.
- `GroundPoint` (type): A point on the ground (m): x east, z south.
- `LOOK_AHEAD` (const): How many tiles downhill `FlowField.direction` looks ahead (shardfall's 3).
- `NAV_DIRECTIONS` (const): The 8 neighbours, as [columns east, rows south]: east, west, south, north, then the diagonals (bit k of a step).
- `NAV_GRID_FIELDS` (const): The options of `new NavGrid(level, options)`.
- `NavGrid` (class): The walkable grid of a compiled level, and the searches over it (see the file comment).
- `NavGridOptions` (type): What `new NavGrid` takes: each field of `NAV_GRID_FIELDS`, optional.
- `NavSource` (type): What a grid is built from: a compiled level, or a surface.
- `NavSurface` (interface): What a grid walks besides a compiled level: `cols` × `rows` tiles `tile` metres wide from `origin` ([x, z], [0, 0] by default), which are `walkable`, each one's `floor` (m), and whether a body on tile (col, row) steps to (col + dc, row + dr) climbing at most `climb` metres on the way.
- `NEAREST_RINGS` (const): How many rings of tiles `nearestOpen` searches round a blocked point (shardfall's 5).

### [`engine/world/patterns.ts`](../engine/world/patterns.ts)

- `direction` (function): The unit direction of a heading (rad, 0 along +Z) and a rise above the ground (rad).
- `headingTo` (function): The heading and rise (rad) from `from` to `to`; straight up or down, or onto itself, heads along +Z.
- `loose` (function): The shots of one volley from `from` (m), the emitter facing `facing` (rad): `PROJECTILE`s `muzzle` out along each direction at `speed`, with the emitter's radius, life, gravity, pierce, kind and team.
- `LooseOptions` (interface): Who looses a volley: its entity, which its shots keep as their `source` (−1: none).
- `MOST_VOLLEYS` (const): The most volleys an emitter looses in one step, however short its interval: a runaway one never floods a step.
- `Pattern` (type): One of `PATTERNS`.
- `PATTERNS` (const): The ways a volley flies (see the file comment).
- `SHOT_EMITTER` (const): An emitter with every field at its default: one shot forward at 20 m/s every half second, from the first step.
- `SHOT_EMITTER_FIELDS` (const): A shot emitter's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('turret', { fields: SHOT_EMITTER_FIELDS })`.
- `ShotEmitter` (interface): An emitter: its pattern, its shots' numbers and its timing (`SHOT_EMITTER_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `stepVolleys` (function): Moves an emitter's clock on by `dt` seconds, its target within range or not (`near`), and returns how many volleys it looses now (see the file comment): 0 or more, at most `MOST_VOLLEYS`.
- `volley` (function): A volley's directions, unit vectors in firing order (see the file comment), the emitter facing `facing` (rad).
- `VolleyAim` (interface): What a volley aims by besides the emitter's facing: where it stands, its target, the stream `random` draws from.

### [`engine/world/projectiles.ts`](../engine/world/projectiles.ts)

- `capsuleCast` (function): Where a ball of `radius` moving from `from` by `delta` (m) first touches `target`: the share of the move, 0 to 1 (0 when it touches already), or −1 when it never does.
- `HurtCapsule` (interface): A target's hurt volume: an upright capsule standing on its feet at `x`, `y`, `z` (m), `radius` wide, its straight middle `height` long (CapsuleGeometry's sizes; 2 × radius + height tall), or a ball (`shape: 'ball'`, or height 0).
- `hurtLength` (const): The length of a hurt capsule's straight middle: 0 for a ball.
- `hurtNear` (function): The ids within `reach` (plus the set's margin) of (x, z) on the ground, in the hash's fixed order.
- `HurtSet` (interface): Targets for hit tests: a spatial hash of their feet by id (filled this step, engine/world/spatial.ts) and their hurt capsules.
- `Projectile` (interface): A shot: what it is, where it flies and what it hit (`PROJECTILE_FIELDS` says what each means).
- `PROJECTILE` (const): A shot with every field at its default: a 5 cm ball at the origin, at rest, flying for 3 s.
- `PROJECTILE_FIELDS` (const): A shot's fields, for a scene's component: `defineComponent('bolt', { description, fields: PROJECTILE_FIELDS })`.
- `ProjectileHit` (interface): A shot's hit this step: a target or a wall, where along the move and where the shot's centre was then.
- `ProjectileState` (type): Where a shot is in its flight: see `PROJECTILE_FIELDS.state`.
- `ProjectileStep` (interface): How `stepProjectiles` steps.
- `stepProjectiles` (function): Steps every flying shot once (`step.dt`): gravity, then its move swept against its targets and the walls.
- `WallContact` (interface): A wall a shot struck: the share of its move where it touched, the body (−1: none) and the surface's normal.
- `WallTest` (type): A wall test: the first wall a ball of `radius` meets moving from `from` by `delta` (m), or null.

### [`engine/world/props/catalog.ts`](../engine/world/props/catalog.ts)

- `BUILT_IN_PROPS` (const): The engine's props, by id.

### [`engine/world/props/fittings.ts`](../engine/world/props/fittings.ts)

- `FITTING_PROPS` (const): The house's fittings, by id.

### [`engine/world/props/library.ts`](../engine/world/props/library.ts)

- `LIBRARY_PROPS` (const): The props library's props, by id.

### [`engine/world/props/place.ts`](../engine/world/props/place.ts)

- `levelProps` (function): The placements `level` makes for the props of `registry` (the shared one by default); see the file comment.
- `propBody` (function): The body `physics.addBody` takes for `placement`, or `null` when its prop has none; see the file comment.
- `PropBody` (interface): A prop's body, as `physics.addBody` takes it (engine/physics/world.ts's `BodySpec`).
- `PropCollider` (type): A prop's collider, as `physics.addBody` takes it.
- `PropPlacement` (interface): A prop placed: `{ prop: 'prop:<id>', at: [x, y, z], yaw }`, its base at `at` (m) and its turn `yaw` about +Y (rad), as `spawnProp` takes it and `levelProps` gives it.
- `propPose` (function): Where `placement` is drawn while no body moves it: the prop's centre and turn.
- `PropPose` (interface): Where a prop is drawn: its centre (m) and its turn, `[x, y, z, w]`.

### [`engine/world/props/prop.ts`](../engine/world/props/prop.ts)

- `defineProp` (function): Defines a prop on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getProp` (function): The prop `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `prop:crate`, with a warning.
- `Prop` (type): A `prop` entry: see the file comment.
- `PROP_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `prop` entry.
- `PROP_PART_FIELDS` (const): The fields of one part: a mesh of the prop.
- `PROP_SHAPES` (const): The physics shapes a prop's body may have, sized as three.js sizes its geometries.
- `propCentre` (function): The height of a prop's centre above its base (m): its body's origin, half its shape's height; 0 without a body.
- `PropDefinition` (type): What `defineProp` takes: any field, and of its objects (body, light, place, each part and its flame) any key.
- `propKind` (function): Declares the kind `prop` on `registry`, with the engine's props, unless it has it.
- `PropKnock` (interface): How hard a knock is, as engine/physics/bodies.ts's `knock` takes it.
- `PropPart` (type): One part of a `prop` entry, filled: see `PROP_PART_FIELDS`.
- `PropTouch` (interface): What a hook is given: the prop, its body, where the touch comes from, and the means to answer it.

### [`engine/world/site.ts`](../engine/world/site.ts)

- `defineSite` (function): Registers a site on `registry` (the shared one by default); throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming its problems.
- `getSite` (function): The site `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default), made afresh: its name is the id without `site:`.
- `makeSite` (function): Makes `spec`'s site, named `name`, from the levels and the terrain `registry` holds (see the file comment).
- `quarterTurn` (function): The rotation of `turn` quarter turns about +Y, as [x, y, z, w].
- `QuarterTurns` (type): A quarter turn's count, 0 to 3.
- `Site` (interface): A made site (see the file comment).
- `SITE_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `site` entry (see the file comment).
- `SiteEntry` (type): A `site` entry.
- `siteProblems` (function): The problems with a site spec's shape; none when it makes a site.
- `SiteSpec` (interface): What `defineSite` takes.
- `SiteStructure` (interface): A structure placed: its level, in its own frame, and where it stands (see the file comment).
- `StructureSpec` (interface): A structure as a site's spec places it.
- `toLocal` (function): A structure's own (x, z) from world (wx, wz): `toWorld` undone.
- `toWorld` (function): World (x, z) from a structure's own (lx, lz): turned `turn` quarter turns, then moved to `at`.
- `turnVector` (function): A direction (x, z) turned `turn` quarter turns about +Y, as `toWorld` turns a structure's; never −0 (state holds it).
- `worldRect` (function): A local rectangle [x0, z0, x1, z1] (m) of structure `s` as a world rectangle.

### [`engine/world/siteNav.ts`](../engine/world/siteNav.ts)

- `createSiteNav` (function): Builds `site`'s navigation (see the file comment).
- `CROUCH_COST` (const): How many times its length a step costs where a body must crouch to take it (a crouch-walk's pace against a run).
- `NavBlock` (interface from [`engine/world/siteNavGrids.ts`](../engine/world/siteNavGrids.ts)): A box of the world (m) a body cannot walk through: a prop's body, a door's leaf where it opens to.
- `SiteNav` (interface): A site's navigation (see the file comment).
- `SiteNavGrid` (interface): One of a site's grids: the terrain's or a structure's storey's, and its first node's number.
- `SiteNavOptions` (interface): How `createSiteNav` builds: the climb limit (m), the steepest ground (m a metre), and the body it walks (m; the shooter's hull, `LEVEL_BODY`, by default, the largest the engine ships): its radius, the clear height a step needs (crouched, with a margin) and the height it stands (a step lower costs `CROUCH_COST` times its length, crouched).

### [`engine/world/siteNavClear.ts`](../engine/world/siteNavClear.ts)

- `CLEAR_SAMPLES` (const): How finely `clearOffset` samples a tile for its clear point: samples a metre (every 5 cm).
- `ClearGraph` (interface): What `clearPoints` reads of a site's graph: its grids, each one's tiles open in its own surface, its links.
- `clearOffset` (function): `tile`'s clear point on `grid` as an offset from its centre (m; see the file comment); `own` is each tile's openness in its own grid, before the blocks closed any.
- `ClearOptions` (interface): What `clearOffset` keeps clear of (see the file comment).
- `clearPoints` (function): Every node's clear point on a site's graph (engine/world/siteNav.ts), each found once: a function giving a node's on its floor (m).

### [`engine/world/siteNavGrids.ts`](../engine/world/siteNavGrids.ts)

- `blockedSurface` (function): `surface` with every tile closed that a block stands on: one whose middle is within a body's `radius` of its footprint (so a gap between two blocks narrower than the body closes) and in sight of it, no closed tile between (a bookshelf by a wall closes none of the tiles behind it), rising more than 5 cm over the tile's floor and lower than a standing body's top over it (a rug or a roof over a sidewalk closes none).
- `CURB` (const): The most a step across a ramp's side climbs or drops (m): a flight is walked along its rise, from its foot and top.
- `NavBlock` (interface): A box of the world (m) a body cannot walk through: a prop's body, a door's leaf where it opens to.
- `siteTerrainSurface` (function): The terrain's cells as a surface, closed where the terrain is cut and over every structure's footprint (see the file comment).
- `storeyCeilings` (function): What is above each tile of storey `k` (m, in the structure's frame; see the file comment); Infinity under the sky.
- `storeyLinks` (function): The pairs of a structure's local tiles a body passes between storeys k and k + 1: flights' tops and ladders.
- `storeySurface` (function): Storey `k` of structure `s` as a surface in the world's orientation (see the file comment), with each tile's ceiling at the structure's height: a step needs `height` metres clear over the higher of its two floors under the ceiling it goes to (storeyCeilings's), and a diagonal under its corners' too.
- `tileHighs` (function): Each tile's highest floor (m): a ramp's or a flight's at its high edge, where a body crossing it may stand.

### [`engine/world/siteQueries.ts`](../engine/world/siteQueries.ts)

- `siteClearSight` (function): Whether the straight line from `from` to `to` (m) meets nothing solid, sampled every `step` metres and at both ends.
- `siteFloorBelow` (function): The height (m) of the highest surface at or under (x, y, z) on the site; null where nothing is.
- `siteRescueGrid` (function): The site's rescue grid, `tile` metres a tile, over its terrain and its structures (see the file comment).
- `SiteRescueGrid` (interface): The lost-body rescue's grid (engine/physics/rescue.ts's `RescueLevel`): see the file comment.
- `siteSolidAt` (function): Whether (x, y, z) is in something solid on the site (see the file comment).
- `siteStructureAt` (function): Where (x, y, z) is in a structure: the first whose box holds it, its storey there and its room; null outside them.
- `siteSurfaceBelow` (function): The surface tag of `siteFloorBelow`'s surface at (x, y, z): '' where nothing is.

### [`engine/world/spatial.ts`](../engine/world/spatial.ts)

- `SPATIAL_HASH_FIELDS` (const): The options of `new SpatialHash(options)`.
- `SpatialHash` (class): Points on the ground, hashed by cell (see the file comment).
- `SpatialHashOptions` (type): What `new SpatialHash` takes: each field of `SPATIAL_HASH_FIELDS`, optional.

### [`engine/world/steer.ts`](../engine/world/steer.ts)

- `airTime` (function): How long (s) a body thrown up at `up` m/s flies under `gravity` (m/s², above 0) until it comes down to `rise` metres above where it left (below for a drop): the later root of `rise = up·t − gravity·t²/2`.
- `APPROACH_RING` (const): `approachRing`'s defaults: the prototype's walker (3 units either side, back at half speed, round at 0.4).
- `approachRing` (function): The way to wait round `to` on a ring of `ring.radius` metres: beyond `radius + band`, in by `followFlow` (straight when `field` is null); inside `radius − band`, straight out at `backoff` of full speed; on the ring, round it at `circle × sway` of full speed (`sway` in [−1, 1]; positive turns about +Y, anticlockwise seen from above).
- `ApproachRingOptions` (interface): What `approachRing` takes: the ring's radius, and how an agent moves in, out and round.
- `FOLLOW` (const): `followFlow`'s defaults: straight within 4 m in a clear line (emberdeep's 64 units), full speed to the target.
- `followFlow` (function): The way to walk from `from` to `to` along `field` (a flow field toward the target's tile): straight at `to` within `near` metres when the grid has a clear line for a body (`NavGrid.lineOfSight`), else the field's look-ahead direction (`FlowField.direction`), else, where the field has no way (beyond its reach, or arrived at the goal tile's centre), straight at `to`, as the prototype does.
- `FollowOptions` (interface): How `followFlow` steers.
- `hop` (function): The launch velocity (m/s) that carries a body thrown up at `up` m/s from `from` to land on `to` under `gravity` (m/s²): `up` vertically and the ground distance over `airTime` across, so a jumper hops onto a crate as well as across the floor.
- `HOP` (const): The prototype slime's jumps: `up` (m/s) for a hop of at most `reach` metres, `pounce` (m/s) for its lower, flatter leap at a target.
- `hover` (function): A flyer's vertical speed (m/s) that holds its feet at `y` metres `height` over `floor`, bobbing `bob` metres at `bobRate` radians per second of `time` (s; its own clock, or the sim's plus a phase): the gap times `climb`.
- `HOVER` (const): `hover`'s defaults: the prototype's wisp, 20 units over the floor bobbing ±3 at 2 rad/s, climbing at 6 × the gap.
- `HoverOptions` (interface): How `hover` holds a flyer up.
- `seek` (function): The way from `from` to `to` on the ground: a unit vector, zero within a millimetre.
- `SteerPoint` (type): A point in the world (m): x east, y up, z south.

### [`engine/world/telegraphs.ts`](../engine/world/telegraphs.ts)

- `coneOf` (function): A cone's fields from a measured hit shape (engine/anim/moves.ts `measureMove`): its range, angle and heights.
- `defineTelegraph` (function): Defines a telegraph on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `floorGap` (function): The signed distance on the floor from (`f`, `s`) to `t`'s shape scaled by `size`: below 0 inside.
- `getTelegraph` (function): The telegraph `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `telegraph:arc`, with a warning.
- `inTelegraph` (function): Whether a body at `point` with `radius` overlaps telegraph `t` placed at `place`: what it hits as it goes off.
- `nearMiss` (function): Whether a body at `point` with `radius` stands outside telegraph `t` but within its `near` metres (scaled).
- `PointLike` (type): A point: three.js's `Vector3`, `{ x, y, z }` or `[x, y, z]`, metres.
- `pointOf` (function): The coordinates of a `PointLike`.
- `Telegraph` (type): A `telegraph` entry: see the file comment.
- `TELEGRAPH_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `telegraph` entry.
- `TELEGRAPH_SHAPES` (const): The shapes a telegraph has.
- `telegraphFill` (function): How far `t`'s drawn fill reaches at wind-up share `u` (clamped 0 to 1), metres before scaling (file comment).
- `telegraphGap` (function): How far a body at `point` (its feet, metres) with `radius` stands outside telegraph `t` placed at `place`, minus the radius: between its heights, the signed distance to its shape on the floor (below 0 inside); above or below them, the distance to the extruded shape.
- `telegraphKind` (function): Declares the kind `telegraph` on `registry`, with its four shapes, unless it has it.
- `TelegraphPlace` (interface): A telegraph where it stands: plain data, as a component or a frame's list holds it.
- `TelegraphSpec` (type): What `defineTelegraph` takes: any field.

### [`engine/world/terrain.ts`](../engine/world/terrain.ts)

- `defineTerrain` (function): Registers a terrain on `registry` (the shared one by default); throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming its problems.
- `getTerrain` (function): The terrain `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default), made afresh: its name is the id without `terrain:`.
- `makeTerrain` (function): Makes `spec`'s terrain, named `name` (see the file comment); throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming its problems.
- `ScatterRule` (interface): How `scatterTerrain` places (see its comment).
- `scatterTerrain` (function): Stateless placement (shardfall's decor): each cell holds one place with the chance `density`, jittered inside it, turned and sized, by hashes of the terrain's seed, the rule's `salt` and the cell, never a stream; so a cell's place never depends on another's, and the same rule gives the same places.
- `Terrain` (interface): A made terrain: its grid, its heights and what the queries and the drawing read (see the file comment).
- `TERRAIN_FIELDS` (const): The fields of a `terrain` entry (see the file comment).
- `TerrainEntry` (type): A `terrain` entry: its spec.
- `TerrainFlat` (interface): A footprint a terrain flattens.
- `terrainGrade` (function): How steep the ground is at (x, z): metres risen a metre along its slope (1 is 45°); null outside the grid.
- `terrainGradient` (function): How the ground rises at (x, z), as metres a metre east and south: its triangle's; null outside the grid.
- `terrainHeight` (function): The ground's height (m) at (x, z): the collider's surface (see the file comment); null outside the grid.
- `TerrainHill` (interface): A dome added to a terrain.
- `terrainNormal` (function): The ground's upward unit normal at (x, z): its triangle's; null outside the grid.
- `TerrainPlace` (interface): A place `scatterTerrain` picks: on the ground, a turn about +Y (rad) and a size factor.
- `terrainProblems` (function): The problems with a terrain spec's shape (beyond its fields' types); none when it makes a terrain.
- `TerrainSpec` (type): What `defineTerrain` and `makeTerrain` take: each field of `TERRAIN_FIELDS` (`size` required).
- `terrainSurface` (function): The surface tag underfoot at (x, z): `steepSurface` where it is steep, else `surface`; '' outside the grid.

### [`engine/world/terrainNav.ts`](../engine/world/terrainNav.ts)

- `terrainNavGrid` (function): A navigation grid over `terrain`'s cells (see the file comment).
- `TerrainNavOptions` (interface): What `terrainNavGrid` takes: a grid's options, and the steepest ground it walks (m a metre; 1 by default).
- `terrainNavSurface` (function): The walkable surface of `terrain`'s cells (see the file comment).

### [`engine/world/things.ts`](../engine/world/things.ts)

- `defineThing` (function): Defines a kind of thing on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getThing` (function): The kind of thing `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `thing:target`, with a warning.
- `hitThing` (function): Hits `thing` for `amount` points at `time` (s): counts it and takes the points; at 0 it goes down (`down`), or breaks (`broken`) when its kind never rises.
- `stepThing` (function): Moves `thing` on to `time` (s), a step of `dt` seconds: one down for its kind's `rise` stands back up, its hit points whole (returns true then); one standing slides along its track at its kind's speed, turning back at each end.
- `Thing` (interface): A thing's state (`THING_FIELDS` says what each field means).
- `THING_FIELDS` (const): The component a thing's state lives in, for a scene: `defineComponent('thing', { description, fields: … })`.
- `THING_KIND_FIELDS` (const): A `thing` kind's fields (see the file comment).
- `thingAt` (function): Where `thing` stands now (m): its track's start, `along` of the way to its far end.
- `ThingHit` (interface): What `hitThing` did: the outcome and the hit points left.
- `thingKind` (function): Declares the kind `thing` on `registry`, with its default `thing:target`, unless it has it.
- `ThingKind` (type): A `thing` entry: see the file comment.
- `ThingOutcome` (type): What a hit did: struck it, put it down, or broke it.
- `ThingSpec` (type): What `defineThing` takes: any of the kind's fields, the rest at their defaults.
- `ThingStanding` (type): Where a thing is: standing, down for a while, or broken for good.
- `thingState` (function): A new thing of `kind` standing at `at` (m), its hit points whole, at its track's start.
- `ThingTouch` (interface): What a hook is told (see the file comment): the thing, its kind, and what touched it.

### [`engine/world/tileHeap.ts`](../engine/world/tileHeap.ts)

- `TileHeap` (class): An indexed binary min-heap of tiles keyed by `keys[tile]`, ties to the lower tile; pushing a held tile re-sorts it.

### [`engine/world/traverse.ts`](../engine/world/traverse.ts)

- `LADDER_DEPTH` (const): How far a ladder's rungs stand off the wall it leans on (m).
- `LADDER_FIELDS` (const): A ladder's fields (see the file comment).
- `LadderSpec` (type): A ladder, parsed: every field of `LADDER_FIELDS`, its defaults filled.
- `LAUNCHER_FIELDS` (const): A launcher's fields (see the file comment).
- `LauncherSpec` (type): A jump pad or a trampoline, parsed: every field of `LAUNCHER_FIELDS`, its defaults filled.
- `launcherVolume` (function): A launcher's volume: from its top's corner a little below it to `reach` above, `[min, max]` (m).
- `levelLadders` (function): The ladders `level`'s ladder glyphs stand (see the file comment), in reading order; in a level written as storeys, each storey's (bottom first), from its floor up to the top of the wall it leans on, the floor of the storey above.
- `parseTraverse` (function): `spec` parsed and checked as a `kind` (see `traverseProblems`); throws `CORE_BAD_SPEC` naming each problem.
- `TRAVERSE_FIELDS` (const): The kinds of traversal, by their fields.
- `traverseProblems` (function): The problems of a spec of `kind` beyond its fields (its fields' own are `parse`'s): sizes, lengths, directions.
- `ZIPLINE_FIELDS` (const): A zipline's fields (see the file comment).
- `ZiplineSpec` (type): A zipline, parsed: every field of `ZIPLINE_FIELDS`, its defaults filled.

### [`engine/world/weapons.ts`](../engine/world/weapons.ts)

- `defineWeapon` (function): Defines a weapon on `registry` (the shared one by default) and returns it.
- `getWeapon` (function): The weapon `id` of `registry` (the shared one by default); a missing id gives `weapon:gun`, with a warning.
- `recoilStep` (function): The kick of shot `n` of a burst (0: the first), [up, right] degrees: its recoil step, the last repeating.
- `spreadOf` (function): The cone a shot strays in now (half-angle, deg): the hip's (and the move's, `moving`) toward the sights' by `aim`, 0 to 1.
- `WEAPON_FIELDS` (const): A `weapon` kind's fields (see the file comment).
- `weaponKind` (function): Declares the kind `weapon` on `registry`, with its default `weapon:gun`, unless it has it.
- `WeaponKind` (type): A `weapon` entry (see the file comment).
- `WeaponSpec` (type): What `defineWeapon` takes: any of the kind's fields (`spread` and `reload` field by field), the rest at their defaults.

### [`eslint.config.js`](../eslint.config.js)

- `configure` (function): Builds the whole config; `switches` defaults to `SWITCHES` (tests turn every switch on).
- `default` (default): ESLint's settings for T0 (PLAN.md §6.10; `npm run lint`, inside `npm run check`): typescript-eslint's recommended rules without type information (so T0 stays fast), the file-comment and size rules, then the doctrine's rule families from tools/eslint/, one block per family, each message naming the fix.
- `SWITCHES` (const): Rules written ahead of the code they guard.

### [`labs/anim/overlay.ts`](../labs/anim/overlay.ts)

- `BONES` (const): Each joint and its parent in the humanoid skeleton (engine/anim/skeleton.ts): the bones the overlay draws.
- `drawBones` (function): Draws each skeleton of `skeletons` (joint name → world position) on `canvas` through `camera`; clears it first.
- `project` (function): Where world point `p` (m) falls on a `width` × `height` picture seen through `camera`; null behind it.

### [`labs/anim/scenes/lineup.ts`](../labs/anim/scenes/lineup.ts)

- `LAB_FIGURE` (const): The component `labFigure` (see `FigureData`).
- `lineup` (const): The Animation Lab's lineup (see the file comment).
- `LINEUP_AT` (const): Where the row stands: the middle of the stage's ground, as the gallery stands its subject (m).
- `LINEUP_BUILDS` (const): The builds in the row, left to right; the mannequin's only with `lab.anim.mannequin`.
- `LINEUP_GAP` (const): How far apart the figures stand (m).
- `LINEUP_SETTINGS` (const): The scene's settings (see the file comment).
- `LINEUP_STATES` (const): Every name `lab.anim.play` takes besides a move's id: walk and run, the sample states, the poses and the stances.
- `REST` (const): How long a figure rests between two swings of a move (s).

### [`labs/box/cast/hero.ts`](../labs/box/cast/hero.ts)

- `HERO` (const): The hero's character, untuned.
- `HERO_BODY` (const): The hero's animator: the default build, empty-handed.
- `HERO_FIGHT` (const): The hero's fight (Box 5, WP 6.7), with a sword.
- `heroCharacter` (function): The hero's character with `tuning` over his own numbers.
- `HeroHit` (interface): What one of the hero's hits does: its cone, hit points, push (m/s), lunge (m/s) and whether it is a big one.
- `HeroTuning` (interface): What a scene may tune of the hero: his walk, take-off and dash speeds, m/s.
- `PROTOTYPE` (const): The hero's numbers as the prototype wrote them, in its units and seconds (see the file comment).
- `spawnHero` (function): Spawns the hero, the player, with his feet at `at` facing `yaw` (rad), and any further `components` (the fight's reactions and cape); returns his id.

### [`labs/box/cast/slime.ts`](../labs/box/cast/slime.ts)

- `CROWD_SLIME` (const): The slime's component: where it is in its hop, and the time left in that part (or spent in the air).
- `makeSlime` (function): A new slime's own state: resting, its first rest drawn from `rng`, up to 1 s.
- `SLIME` (const): The slime's numbers (see the file comment).
- `SLIME_ATTACK` (const): The slime's pounce (see the file comment): seconds, metres, m/s and hit points.
- `SLIME_POUNCE` (const): The slime's pounce on the floor: a line its own width, from it to just past the hero on its ring.
- `SlimeData` (interface): The slime's own state, beside its crowd agent.
- `SlimeHop` (type): Where a slime is in its hop.
- `steerSlime` (function): Moves a living slime one step (see the file comment): in the air until it lands, else braking on the floor while it rests and crouches, then a leap by `knockback` and `launch` (engine/physics/crowd.ts).

### [`labs/box/cast/walker.ts`](../labs/box/cast/walker.ts)

- `Chase` (interface): What every member of the cast steers by, each step.
- `CROWD_WALKER` (const): The walker's component: its speed, heading and sway phase.
- `levelWith` (const): Whether a point at height `y` (m) is level with the hero.
- `makeWalker` (function): A new walker's own state, its speed and sway's phase drawn from `rng`, facing `yaw`.
- `steerWalker` (function): The velocity (m/s) the walker wants this step, into `out`, turning it toward where it goes (see the file comment).
- `WALKER` (const): The walker's numbers (see the file comment).
- `WALKER_ATTACK` (const): The walker's attack (see the file comment): seconds, metres, m/s and hit points.
- `WALKER_SWING` (const): The walker's swing on the floor: an arc ±0.8 rad, from 0.6 of its radius to 1.35 m, its colour the prototype's.
- `WalkerData` (interface): The walker's own state, beside its crowd agent.

### [`labs/box/cast/wisp.ts`](../labs/box/cast/wisp.ts)

- `CROWD_WISP` (const): The wisp's component: which way it circles, and its hover's clock.

- `steerWisp` (function): The velocity (m/s) the wisp wants this step, into `out`, its clock advanced (see the file comment).

- `WISP_ATTACK` (const): The wisp's shot (see the file comment): seconds, metres, m/s and hit points.
- `WISP_SHOT` (const): The wisp's shot on the floor: a narrow line from under it, as far as it shoots.
- `WispData` (interface): The wisp's own state, beside its crowd agent.

### [`labs/box/menu.ts`](../labs/box/menu.ts)

- `BOX_ACTION_MAP` (const): The action map the page's input binds: createEngine's default (engine/input/input.ts).
- `BoxMenuOptions` (interface): What the menu lists.
- `ControlRow` (interface): One row of the controls: what it does, then the keys and mouse buttons, then the pad's buttons.
- `controlRows` (function): The rows of the controls for `map`: moving first, then each other action in the map's order.
- `createBoxMenu` (function): Builds the menu in `document` when `box.menu` shows it (see the file comment) and returns its panel; null when it stays out (automation, or `box.menu=off`).
- `linkQuery` (function): A link's query: `changes` (null removes a key) over `search`, or over only its `keep` keys; `:` and `,` readable.
- `MENU_KEY` (const): The key that shows and hides the menu: M, which no action map binds.
- `MENU_SETTINGS` (const): The menu's view setting (see the file comment).
- `MENU_STORAGE_KEY` (const): The `localStorage` key that remembers whether the reader left the menu `open` or `closed`.
- `MenuEntry` (interface): A listed entry: a scene or a look, as its module exports it.
- `menuShown` (function): Whether `setting` (the query's `box.menu`) shows the menu in a browser that automation does or does not drive.
- `menuStartsOpen` (function): Whether the menu starts open: unless `storage` remembers the reader closing it; storage that throws forgets.
- `MenuStorage` (type): Where the menu remembers being open or closed: the `localStorage` shape.
- `rememberMenu` (function): Remembers in `storage` that the reader left the menu open or closed; storage that throws (blocked, full) forgets.

### [`labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts)

- `CROWD_GRID` (const): The crowd's walkable grid: the hall under a climb of 6 cm, what a crowd body manages (Rapier 0.21 steps a capsule up 7 cm and a ball 8.5 cm, measured in WP 5.2), so the stairs' gentle rise is walkable and their sides are not.
- `CROWD_MEMBER` (const): A member's crowd agent (engine/physics/crowd.ts): its body, its make and what the last readback saw.
- `CROWD_SETTINGS` (const): The crowd's settings: how many, and the mix.
- `CROWD_TILES` (const): The tiles a member may start on: the hall's open floor, at height 0 (no dais, stairs or gallery).
- `crowd1000` (const): The crowd at 1,000.
- `CrowdComponents` (type): The scene's components.
- `default` (default): The crowd, Box 4 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 5.7): the hall with a hero (labs/box/scenes/hall.ts) filling with `box.crowd.count` walkers, slimes and wisps (labs/box/cast/{walker,slime,wisp}.ts) that chase him, round the walls and pillars and up the stairs after him.
- `MIXES` (const): A crowd mix: the share of walkers, and of walkers and slimes together; the rest are wisps.
- `setupCrowd` (function): The crowd's setup: the hall and its hero (with any further `components`), `box.crowd.count` members queued, the crowd's systems; returns the hero's id.
- `SPAWN` (const): Where members start: at least `away` m from the hero (the prototype's 80 units), `tries` draws, `jitter` in a tile.

### [`labs/box/scenes/fight-rules.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/fight-rules.ts)

- `breakAttack` (function): Ends a foe's attack: its token back, its telegraph gone.
- `FIGHT_FOE` (const): The component `fightFoe`: where a foe is in its attack, and its timers.
- `FIGHT_HEALTH` (const): The component `fightHealth`: a fighter's hit points (see the file comment).
- `FIGHT_HERO` (const): The component `fightHero`: the hero's combo, thrust and counters.
- `FIGHT_SHOT` (const): The component `fightShot`: a bolt in flight.
- `FIGHT_TELEGRAPH` (const): The component `fightTelegraph`: a foe's telegraph where it stands.
- `FIGHT_TOKENS` (const): The component `fightTokens`: the hero's attack tokens.
- `FightBurst` (interface): A burst for the page's effects: where, and how big.
- `FightComponents` (type): The fight's components: the crowd's, the hero's actor, the bodies' reactions and his cape, and its own.
- `FightEvents` (type): The fight's events.
- `FightFoe` (interface): A foe's fight: where it is in its attack, its move and swing, and its timers (s).
- `FightHero` (interface): The hero's fight: his combo's and thrust's saved states, and his counters (ticks).
- `FightShot` (type): A bolt in flight: a projectile, and the hit points it takes.
- `FightTelegraph` (interface): A foe's telegraph where it stands: a `TelegraphPlace` as plain data (none while `telegraph` is empty).
- `FightWorld` (type): The fight's world.
- `FoePhase` (type): Where a foe is in its attack.
- `foeSet` (function): The living foes as hurt capsules, through a spatial hash of their feet, built now.
- `heroCombo` (const): The hero's combo, as `HERO_FIGHT` says (an idle one; its state is `fightHero.combo`).
- `heroOf` (function): The hero: his id and components; undefined before setup.
- `heroSet` (function): The hero as a hurt capsule (his controller's), built now.
- `heroThrust` (const): The hero's thrust out of a dash (an idle one; its state is `fightHero.thrust`).
- `hurtHero` (function): A foe's blow (`amount` hit points, from `from`) on the hero: unless he is safe, he flinches (his body state `hurt`, and his reactions along the push) and is pushed away, the hit lands through `damage` (no hit points in god mode), his combo is broken off when it takes any, and the event `hit` fires.
- `knockedDown` (const): Whether a body's reactions play a knockdown or its get-up (or a death): while they do, it acts on nothing.
- `strikeFoe` (function): The hero's blow (`hit`, from his feet `from`) on the foe `id`: its hit points, push, throw and hit-stop through `damage`, a walker's reactions (a flinch; a big blow's knockdown, a killing one's death), its attack broken off, a stun, and the events `hit` (and `slain`).
- `STUN` (const): How long a blow stuns a foe (s): it steers and attacks again after.

### [`labs/box/scenes/fight.ts`](../labs/box/scenes/fight.ts)

- `default` (default): The fight, Box 5 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 6.7): the hall with its hero and a crowd (labs/box/scenes/crowd-1000.ts), fighting.
- `fight` (const): The fight, 36 mixed.
- `FIGHT_SETTINGS` (const): The fight's settings: whether the hero's hit points hold, and whether his sword's trail is sim data.
- `fightStep` (function): The fight's step: joined at the first, then the hero's fight (labs/box/scenes/fight-hero.ts).
- `joinFight` (function): The fight joined, once, at the first step (spawns made in the setup join at its end): the hero's sword and his components, each member's (see the file comment).
- `setupFight` (function): The fight's setup: the crowd's, and the fight's systems (see the file comment); returns the hero's id.

- `default` (default): The hall with its props, Box 3 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 4.6): the hall with a hero (labs/box/scenes/hall.ts) and its props, standing in the scene through `spawnProp` (their bodies in the physics world, the page drawing them through the instanced prop meshes): the level's own, a brazier's fire on each of its 30 stands (`levelProps`), and `box.hallProps.count` crates and barrels, 10 to 300, on the first of `HALL_SPOTS`.
- `HALL_PROPS_SETTINGS` (const): The scene's settings: how many crates and barrels.
- `HALL_SPOTS` (const): The 300 spots of the hall's crates and barrels (see the file comment), as placements on the floor or a stack.
- `HALL_SWING` (const): The scene's own component: the hero's shove, whose it is and its ticks left.
- `hallProps` (const): The hall with its props.
- `inShove` (function): Whether a shove from `hero` (his feet and heading) reaches the prop centred at `p` (see `SHOVE`).
- `shove` (function): The hero shoves: every prop his shove reaches is hit, from his feet (see the file comment); returns the ids hit.
- `SHOVE` (const): The hero's shove: how far it reaches (m), how wide (rad either side), how high (m from his middle), how long (s).

- `default` (default): The hall with a hero, Box 3 (PLAN.md §9.0, WP 4.6): the hall (labs/box/levels/hall.txt: 64 × 44 m inside walls 3 m high, a grid of pillars 3.5 m high, low walls to jump onto, 30 brazier stands, two galleries 1 m up along the north wall with stairs rising to each, and the octagonal rune dais at the centre, 0.5 m up) as a physics level, and the hero (labs/box/cast/hero.ts) at its spawn `@` on the dais, facing south.

### [`labs/box/sounds/effects.ts`](../labs/box/sounds/effects.ts)

- `boxDeath` (const): A body falling for good: a sinking groan, then the thud.
- `boxHit` (const): A blow landing: a bright crack over a low knock.
- `boxLaunch` (const): A bolt leaving: a rising saw with a hiss.
- `boxStep` (const): A footstep on stone: a heel's low thump under a gritty scuff.
- `boxStepIron` (const): A footstep on iron: a tick and a short metal ring.
- `boxThud` (const): A body coming down (a landing, a slime's pounce): a falling sine with a dull burst.
- `boxTorch` (const): A torch's crackle, looped on the ambience bus: pops over a soft roar that rises from and falls to silence.

### [`labs/box/sounds/events.ts`](../labs/box/sounds/events.ts)

- `BOX_FOOTSTEPS` (const): Footsteps by surface tag (the level legend's `surface`): the effect a step on it plays; `'*'` any other.
- `BoxSoundEvent` (interface): One sound the box plays for a sim event.
- `boxSounds` (function): A scene's `sounds` hook for the box's scenes on `level`: each event's effect and gain, as the page plays them.
- `createSoundReader` (function): A reader that reads each event of a world once (see the file comment).
- `footstepSfx` (function): The effect a footstep plays at `at` on `level`: its surface's (`BOX_FOOTSTEPS`), the `'*'` one off any level.
- `Point` (type): A point in the world, metres.
- `SOUND_EVENTS` (const): The event types that play a sound, in the order the file comment gives them.
- `soundOf` (function): The sound one traced event plays in `world` on `level` (read at `world.tick`), or null when it plays none.
- `SoundReader` (interface): Reads a world's new events as sounds (see the file comment).
- `SoundWorld` (interface): What the reader reads of a world: its step, its event trace and its entities.
- `timelineHash` (function): A timeline's hash: FNV-1a, 64 bits, over its JSON's UTF-16 code units, as 16 hex digits.

### [`labs/box/sounds/page.ts`](../labs/box/sounds/page.ts)

- `BOX_ROOMS` (const): The reverb by level id; any other level, or none, is dry.
- `BoxSound` (interface): The box's sound in a page (see the file comment).
- `BoxSoundInfo` (interface): What `info()` reports: plain data.
- `createBoxSound` (function): Makes the box's sound: `audio` to play into (a page's `createAudio()` by default), published unless `publish` is false.
- `LOG_SIZE` (const): How many sound events `info().log` keeps.
- `MUSIC` (const): The song, and the seconds without a blow before it calms.
- `nearestTorches` (function): The torches that sound: those of `playing` within `keep` m of the `voices`-th nearest, then the nearest others, up to `voices`; nearest first, ties by index.
- `SoundFrame` (interface): What `frame` reads each rendered frame (the engine's `onFrame` gives it): never a way to change play.
- `TORCH` (const): The torch ambience: voices at once, the margin before a nearer torch takes a voice (m), and its gain.

### [`labs/box/touch.ts`](../labs/box/touch.ts)

- `BOX_TOUCH` (const): The box page's touch layout's id.

### [`labs/game/best.ts`](../labs/game/best.ts)

- `BEST_KEY` (const): The key the best round is kept under.
- `bestOf` (function): The fastest won round kept (s), or null: none yet, or a value that is no time.
- `recordBest` (function): Keeps `seconds` when it beats the best kept; returns the best after.

### [`labs/game/bot.ts`](../labs/game/bot.ts)

- `botIntents` (function): The intents for one step: run toward the nearest gem by walking distance; none when no gem is left.
- `BotView` (interface): What the bot sees each step: the player's feet and the gems left.
- `GroundSpot` (interface): A point on the ground, m: x east, z south.
- `HEADINGS` (const): How many headings the bot steers by: few, so its intents change seldom and its replays stay short.
- `playBot` (function): Plays the bot until the round ends or `limit` steps pass; returns how the round stands and the steps it took.
- `roundOf` (function): The round as it stands, read through the inspector.
- `viewOf` (function): What the bot sees in a running engine: the player's feet and the gems left, read through the inspector.

### [`labs/game/cast/player.ts`](../labs/game/cast/player.ts)

- `JUMP_SPEED` (const): The player's take-off speed, m/s: about 1.27 m up under the controller's gravity, over a 0.75 m low wall.
- `PLAYER_BODY` (const): The body the player is drawn as: the humanoid in the chibi build, empty-handed.
- `playerCharacter` (function): The player's character at `speed` m/s; createCharacter's defaults for the rest (its dash among them).
- `spawnPlayer` (function): Stands the player in `w` (a scene with physics) at `at`, facing `yaw`: an actor the step's intents move.

### [`labs/game/scenes/play.ts`](../labs/game/scenes/play.ts)

- `ARENA` (const): The arena, compiled: its colliders for physics, its tiles for the gems and the bot's paths.
- `ARENA_TEXT` (const): The arena: 18 × 14 m inside walls 3 m high, two 2 × 2 m pillars, two low walls (0.75 m) to jump, the spawn `@`.
- `default` (default): The starter game's scene `game:play`: every new game begins as this one (tools/game/new-game.mjs copies labs/game/ into it), so it is small, plays, and shows the parts a game is made of.
- `GAME_SETTINGS` (const): The game's settings: each is reachable through `x set`, URL parameters (`?game.gems=3`) and `__engine.set`.
- `GameComponents` (type): The scene's components, typed.
- `GEM` (const): A gem: where it floats and how it looks (the page draws a component that declares x and z in metres).
- `play` (const): The starter game: collect every gem before the clock runs out.
- `REACH` (const): How close the player's feet come to a gem to collect it, m (on the ground plane).
- `Round` (type): The round, as the component holds it.
- `ROUND` (const): The round: the score, the clock and how it ended.

### [`labs/hello/hello.ts`](../labs/hello/hello.ts)

- `HelloView` (interface): A started hello scene.
- `startHello` (function): Starts the renderer on `canvas` (rejecting with `GfxError` `GFX_NO_WEBGPU` without WebGPU), builds the scene, and draws the first frame, directly or through the post pass; resolves once the GPU has finished it.

### [`labs/index/gallery.ts`](../labs/index/gallery.ts)

- `galleryBoot` (function): Starts the engine in `doc`'s `#view` on the gallery entry `hash` names, everything registered (see the file comment).
- `GalleryInspector` (interface): What a lab reads through the engine's inspector (`__engine`): the gallery's lists and `describe`.
- `galleryLab` (function): Starts a gallery lab for `spec.kinds` in `doc` (see the file comment); resolves once its panel is filled.
- `hashEntry` (function): The kind and entry a gallery hash names: `#gallery/prop/prop:crate` → ['prop', 'prop:crate'].

### [`labs/index/lab.ts`](../labs/index/lab.ts)

- `button` (function): A button in `parent` labelled `label` that runs `act` when pressed; returns it.
- `el` (function): An element `tag` with `attributes` and `children`.
- `entryList` (function): Lists `entries` as links in `parent`, the current one marked (`aria-current`); returns the list.
- `labPanel` (function): The lab's panel in `#lab` (made when the page lacks one): its header, then the sections the lab adds.
- `LabPanel` (interface): A lab's panel: its sections and a status line.
- `LabSpec` (interface): What a lab says about itself: its title, what it is for, and the `x` command that does the same job.
- `ListItem` (interface): One entry of a list: what it says and where it leads.
- `reloadOnHash` (function): Reloads the page when its hash changes, so a deep link (`#gallery/<kind>/<id>`) opens what it names.

### [`labs/index/labs.ts`](../labs/index/labs.ts)

- `checkLabs` (function): Every problem with `index` (see the file comment), each naming its fix; none when it is sound.
- `expiredLabs` (function): The temporary labs whose `expires` date is before `today` (`YYYY-MM-DD`).
- `labLinks` (function): Every link of the index, from the index page's own directory: its address, its label and its page.
- `LabRecord` (interface): One lab or page: where it lives, its links, what it is for, its `x` command; a temporary one's question and dates.
- `LabsIndex` (interface): labs/labs.json.
- `LabsSection` (interface): A section of the index: the engine's pages, the labs kept, the temporary ones.
- `SECTIONS` (const): The sections the index has, in order.

### [`labs/playground/bodies/neighbours.ts`](../labs/playground/bodies/neighbours.ts)

- `NEIGHBOUR_BODIES` (const): The four neighbours' bodies, by their index.
- `NEIGHBOUR_SEED` (const): The first neighbour's seed; the k-th's is this plus k.
- `neighbourBody` (function): Neighbour `k`'s body: the player's, its slots drawn by its seed (see the file comment).

### [`labs/playground/bodies/player.ts`](../labs/playground/bodies/player.ts)

- `PLAYER` (const): `body:player`, registered with the shared registry once this module loads.
- `PLAYER_BODY` (const): The player's body (see the file comment).

### [`labs/playground/cast/dog.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/dog.ts)

- `DOG` (const): How the dog goes about (see the file comment): speeds, distances (m) and times (s).
- `DOG_FIELDS` (const): The dog's own state (the component `dog`).
- `DOG_MODES` (const): What the dog does (see the file comment).
- `standDog` (function): Stands the dog beside the player's spawn `at` (where he faces `yaw`), facing him, its ball before its paws, and adds its systems.

### [`labs/playground/cast/dummies.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/dummies.ts)

- `DUMMY_KIND` (const): The ring's dummies' kind (see the file comment).
- `RING_DUMMIES` (const): Where the ring's dummies stand (m, on its canvas 1 m up) and face: three across its north half, toward its steps.
- `Sparring` (interface): A dummy's lean and swing (`SPARRING_FIELDS`).
- `SPARRING_FIELDS` (const): The component `sparring`'s fields: the lean (rad: its head toward +X and +Z), its swing (rad/s) and its turn.
- `SPRING` (const): A sparring dummy's spring: its frequency (Hz) and damping ratio, a hit's swing (rad/s) and the most it leans (rad).
- `standDummies` (function): Stands the ring's dummies (`RING_DUMMIES`): their entities, in order.
- `standDummy` (function): Stands a sparring dummy on its base at `at` (m), facing `yaw` (rad): its entity.

### [`labs/playground/cast/health.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/health.ts)

- `CAST_HP` (const): As many hit points as one of the cast ever needs: given back at every blow.
- `castHealth` (const): A cast member's `health`: full, never hit.

### [`labs/playground/cast/neighbours.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/neighbours.ts)

- `Neighbour` (interface): A neighbour: its name, its body's index (`body:neighbour<k>`) and its route.
- `NEIGHBOUR` (const): How they go about: a stroll (m/s), how far they see and look (m), how near a shove comes (m) and how fast (m/s), how long a step aside, a flinch's rest and a look at a noise last (s), and the noises' carry (m).
- `NEIGHBOUR_FIELDS` (const): A neighbour's own state: its index, its step aside (until when, which way), its last flinch, whether it looks.
- `NEIGHBOURS` (const): The neighbours and their rounds (see the file comment): stops in world metres, stays in seconds.
- `standNeighbours` (function): Stands the neighbours at their routes' first stops and adds their systems (see the file comment); their ids.

### [`labs/playground/cast/partners.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/partners.ts)

- `PARTNER_BLOWS` (const): What each hard blow does, by its move: its push along the blow and up (m/s).
- `RING_PARTNERS` (const): Where the partners stand (m, on the canvas 1 m up) and face: the canvas's south corners, toward the steps.
- `standPartners` (function): Stands the ring's partners (`RING_PARTNERS`) and adds the systems that spar with them (see the file comment).

### [`labs/playground/cast/player.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/player.ts)

- `APEX_GRAVITY` (const): Apex's gravity (m/s²): 750 units/s², an inch a unit (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §3.2).
- `APEX_JUMP` (const): Apex's jump (m): 56 units.
- `APEX_RUN` (const): Apex's run with a weapon out (m/s): 173.5 units/s; holstered, the player runs 1.15 times as fast.
- `PLAYER_LOOK` (const): How the player is drawn: `body:player` on the adult build, empty-handed.
- `playerCharacter` (function): The player's character: `movement:apex`, its run and its jump's height (a take-off of √(2 g h)) as tuned.
- `PlayerTuning` (interface): What a scene may tune: the run with a weapon out (m/s) and the jump's height (m).
- `spawnPlayer` (function): Stands the player in `w` (a scene with physics) at `at`, facing `yaw`: an actor the step's intents move, carrying `weapons` (ids, in slot order; none by default), holstered.

### [`labs/playground/cast/ways.ts`](../labs/playground/cast/ways.ts)

- `plainWays` (function): The site's navigation without a scene's props, made once (a pure function of the site): for placing in a setup.
- `replanWays` (function): Makes `w`'s ways again round its props as they stand now (a walker held by what its way does not know).
- `waysOf` (function): `w`'s navigation of the block round its props (see the file comment).
- `wayTo` (function): The flow field to `goal` kept under `key` (see the file comment), and the navigation it runs over.

### [`labs/playground/controls.ts`](../labs/playground/controls.ts)

- `keysLine` (function): The HUD's keys: the map in use's, as its prompts label them (rebound, or on a pad), then the page's own.
- `PLAYGROUND_ACTIONS` (const): The actions the player answers, with what each does, in the menu's order; the rest are bound for later WPs.
- `PLAYGROUND_MAPS` (const): The action maps, by camera mode (labs/playground/views.ts `PLAYGROUND_CAMERAS`' names).
- `playgroundMap` (function): The action map for the camera `code` (`cam3=first,…`): its mode's, the shooter's for a camera no mode opens.

### [`labs/playground/levels/gym.ts`](../labs/playground/levels/gym.ts)

- `GYM_BALLOON` (const): The redeploy balloon: a vertical line from the floor up to the balloon (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.2's stands 60 m up on the hill; the gym's 90 m, so a course glides, then dives to 35 m/s, before the landing pose takes over at 30 m).
- `GYM_CRAWL` (const): The crawl (m): a tunnel `clear` high inside, `long` and `wide`, its walls `wall` high with the roof slab (`slab` thick) laid on them, and a bar whose underside is `bar` up, on two posts `post` high.
- `GYM_FEATURES` (const): The features, north to south (see the file comment and docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.3).
- `GYM_GATES` (const): The gym's gates on the site (labs/playground/levels/site.ts), each a gap in its perimeter wall in level metres: north to the range, east to the backyard and to the street; each clear of every course's runs.
- `GYM_LAUNCHERS` (const): The launchers and the heights they throw to (m): a jump pad flush with the floor, and a trampoline whose mat stands 0.5 m up against the tower's west face, so a walk off the tower's top drops onto it from 5.5 m.
- `GYM_PROPS` (const): The crawl's slab and bar: fixed boxes the gym stands on its walls and posts (the level's blocks start at the floor).
- `GYM_SITE_TEXT` (const): The same with its gates open (`GYM_GATES`): the gym as it stands on the site.
- `GYM_SIZE` (const): The gym's floor (m): west to east and north to south, inside its perimeter wall.
- `GYM_SPAWN` (const): The spawn: the tile `@` marks, at the north end of the gym, its centre (m).
- `GYM_TEXT` (const): The gym's level text (format 1), drawn from `GYM_FEATURES`.
- `GYM_TILE` (const): The gym's tile (m): half a metre, so a fence is half a metre thick.
- `GYM_ZIPLINE` (const): The tower's zipline, from its top's pulley to the south one (engine/world/traverse.ts's spec).
- `GymFeature` (interface): A calibrated feature of the gym.
- `GymKind` (type): What a feature measures (docs/PLAYGROUND.md §2.3).
- `GymRect` (interface): A rectangle of a feature in level metres (0, 0 is the perimeter's north-west corner), on whole tiles, of `char`.

- `sigh` (const): A neighbour sitting down: a long breath out, falling, through a relaxed mouth.
- `tags` (const): The dog's collar tags jingling as it trots off.
- `whine` (const): The dog held and waiting: a thin whine rising and falling.

- `ADVICE_CODE` (const): An engine advice line: `[AREA_WORDS] message`; group 1 is the code.

- `listing` (function): The entry that lists `warning`: its code exactly for an advice line, a contained text for any other warning.
