- `THREE_TSL_ERROR` (const): A shader three.js could not build (r182's `Nodes.getForRender` prints it as an error, then draws a default).
- `trap` (function): The trap's verdict on one message: a `Warning` when it is advice, a deprecation, a TSL error or a `console.warn`.
- `Warning` (interface): A console message the trap caught.
- `watchConsole` (function): Wraps `target`'s methods so each trapped message reaches `sink` before it prints; returns the unwrap function.

- `SampleAt` (type): Where a parity samples a clip: `grid`, 30 a second and the 60 Hz midpoints; `keys`, at the clip's own keys.
- `SET_DIRS` (const): Every set's directory under data/anim/sets/, sorted.
- `setOf` (function): The set in `dir`, joined once.
- `writeBaseline` (function): Writes `section` of the baseline (call it only when `WRITING`).
- `WRITING` (const): Whether this run rewrites the baseline (`ANIM_CLIPS_BASELINE=write`).

### [`tests/unit/data/anim/catalogs/catalogs.ts`](../tests/unit/data/anim/catalogs/catalogs.ts)

- `canonicalSha256` (function): SHA-256 of `value` as `JSON.stringify` writes it (no spaces, keys in their order).
- `COVERAGE_HEADING` (const): The coverage map's heading in the research document, without its `## `.
- `CoverageRow` (interface): One row of the coverage map.
- `differences` (function): The pointers at which `a` and `b` differ, in `a`'s order: a value that differs, a key or index that only one has, or an object whose keys are in another order (reported at the object).
- `readCoverage` (function): Reads the coverage map out of `text` (the research document).
- `RESEARCH_FILE` (const): The research document that carries the coverage map.
- `sourceOrigin` (function): A `my-3d2dge:<path>` or `shardfall:<path>` origin, split; undefined for a URL.
- `valueAt` (function): The value at `pointer` inside `doc`, or undefined.
- `Verdict` (type): What a coverage row says of its item.
- `withValueAt` (function): A copy of `doc` with `value` at `pointer` (whose parent must exist).

### [`tests/unit/data/anim/ledger/ledger.ts`](../tests/unit/data/anim/ledger/ledger.ts)

- `ANIM_DIR` (const): The library's data directory, `data/anim/`.
- `Category` (interface): One category of `categories.tsv`.
- `categoryOf` (function): The ledger's rule: a take's category from its own description only (`data/anim/cmu/README.md`).
- `compareIds` (function): Numeric order of take ids (`2_10` after `2_9`, `10_01` after `9_99`).
- `fallbackCategoryOf` (function): my-3d2dge's rule (`my-3d2dge:tools/cmu.mjs:122`): the take's description first, then its subject's.
- `joinBack` (function): The original ledger's header and rows, rebuilt from the split: every take in id order, its subject's description restored and its category given by my-3d2dge's rule.
- `Ledger` (interface): The whole split ledger, as read.
- `LEDGER_DIR` (const): The split ledger's directory, `data/anim/cmu/`.
- `ledgerFiles` (function): The `.tsv` files in `dir`, sorted.
- `ORIGINAL_COLUMNS` (const): The columns of my-3d2dge's single-file ledger (`my-3d2dge:src/mocap/catalogs/cmu-takes.tsv`), in order.
- `originalRows` (function): The header and rows of the original ledger's text: its comment and empty lines left out.
- `parseTsv` (function): Parses tab-separated `text`: `#` lines are comments, the first other line is the header, empty lines are skipped.
- `readLedger` (function): Reads `categories.tsv`, `subjects.tsv` and every category file under `dir`.
- `readLedgerFile` (function): Reads a file of the split ledger.
- `Subject` (interface): One row of `subjects.tsv`.
- `Take` (type): One take: a row of a category file, with the category its file names.
- `TAKE_COLUMNS` (const): The columns of each category file, in order.
- `Tsv` (interface): A tab-separated file: its comment lines, its header and its rows, each padded to the header's length.

### [`tests/unit/data/anim/sources/sources.ts`](../tests/unit/data/anim/sources/sources.ts)

- `Catalog` (interface): A catalog: clip entries `[tags, description, orig?]` by name, plus its `$sources`, `$skip` and `$pick`.

- `CatalogSource` (interface): A catalog's `"$sources"` record for one library.

- `entries` (function): A catalog's clip entries (its keys not starting `$`), by name.
- `FileRow` (interface): A row of the Where-each-file-came-from table.
- `readCatalogs` (function): Each catalog in `data/anim/catalogs/`, by file name (`cmu.json`).
- `readSources` (function): Reads SOURCES.md's two tables.
- `SourceRow` (interface): A row of the Sources table.
- `Sources` (interface): Both tables of SOURCES.md, and its text.
- `SOURCES_FILE` (const): `data/anim/SOURCES.md`.
- `squash` (function): `text` with every run of white space as one space, for comparing verbatim quotes across line breaks.
- `tableUnder` (function): The rows of the first table under the `## <heading>` of `text`, as raw cells (the header and rule left out).

### [`tests/unit/hooks/harness.ts`](../tests/unit/hooks/harness.ts)

- `HookRun` (interface): What a hook run printed and returned.
- `HOOKS` (const): The hook scripts' directory.
- `runHook` (function): Runs `.claude/hooks/<script>` (`.ts` with this Node, `.sh` with bash), `input` as JSON on stdin.
- `RunOptions` (interface): How to run a hook.

### [`tests/unit/readmeClaims.ts`](../tests/unit/readmeClaims.ts)

- `missingProblems` (function): What the README leaves out of `scenes` (`<lab>:<name>` ids) and `settings` (paths), one sentence each: a scene needs a row in the demo index naming its file or id, a setting a row in the settings table.
- `ReadmeLab` (interface): A lab whose README is checked: its name (`box`, the scenes' prefix) and a scene that lists the members.
- `readmeProblems` (function): Every problem with the claims in `text`'s code spans, one sentence each ([] when all hold).
- `section` (function): The text under the heading `heading` in `markdown` (up to the next `##` heading); '' without it.

### [`tests/unit/ui/fakeDom.ts`](../tests/unit/ui/fakeDom.ts)

- `asDom` (function): The fake's objects as the DOM types the modules take.
- `CanvasRect` (interface): A canvas's client rect, CSS px.
- `FakeDocument` (class): A fake document: a `<html>` with `<head>` and `<body>`, and an optional window.
- `FakeElement` (class): A fake element (see the file comment).
- `FakeEvent` (interface): An event as the fake fires it: its type and the element it was fired at.
- `fakePage` (function): A fake page and a canvas (not yet in it) whose client rect is `rect`, which a test may change.

### [`tests/unit/ui/uiKit.ts`](../tests/unit/ui/uiKit.ts)

- `fakeInput` (function): A page input on `device` (see the file comment).
- `FakeInput` (interface): A test's page input (see the file comment).

### [`tools/anim/asf-amc-fixture.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc-fixture.ts)

- `testAmc` (function): A take of `n` frames at 120 a second: a walk forward at `travel` units a second (0: in place), as `.amc` text.
- `testAsf` (function): The skeleton, as an `.asf` file's text.

### [`tools/anim/asf-amc.ts`](../tools/anim/asf-amc.ts)

- `AmcFrame` (type): One frame of a take: each bone's channel values.
- `AsfBone` (interface): A bone: its rest direction (unit, world), length (file units), axis frame C and its inverse, and channels.
- `mm` (const): The product `a · b` of two 3 × 3 matrices.
- `mv` (const): Vector `v` turned by matrix `m`.
- `pose` (function): Every bone's world rotation and end (metres) in one frame (none: the rest pose, the root at the origin).
- `readAmc` (function): Reads an `.amc` take: one `{ bone: values }` per frame.
- `readAsf` (function): Reads an `.asf` skeleton.
- `Skeleton` (interface): A skeleton: metres per file unit, its bones, their order (parents first) and each one's parent.
- `tr` (const): The transpose of `m` (its inverse, for a rotation).
- `V` (type): A vector, or a 3 × 3 matrix (row major).

### [`tools/anim/cmu-capture.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu-capture.ts)

- `CmuCapture` (type): A capture read from a take, with each bone's rotation from rest per frame (`bones` order), quaternions.
- `CmuOptions` (interface): How `readCmu` samples: the output rate, nearest frames (legacy) or in-betweened ones, and where notes go.
- `Pick` (interface): A picked stretch of a take: seconds `from`–`to` (to the end when absent), its rate, and whether it loops.
- `readCmu` (function): One subject's picked stretches as captures, plus `_rest` (see the file comment); `asfFile` is the skeleton.

### [`tools/anim/cmu-cli.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu-cli.ts)

- `CMU_SUBCOMMANDS` (const): The `cmu` subcommands.
- `CmuRequest` (interface): What `runCmu` needs: the words after `cmu`, the flags, and the repository root (for paths it prints).
- `cmuTargets` (const): The report target of `x anim cmu …`.
- `runCmu` (function): Runs `x anim cmu <sub> …`; throws plain errors for bad arguments (the caller makes them usage errors).

### [`tools/anim/cmu.ts`](../tools/anim/cmu.ts)

- `ANIM_CACHE` (const): The cache's root, `.cache/anim/`.
- `ARCHIVE` (const): Every subject's skeleton and takes, 1.08 GB, read by ranges.
- `asfOf` (const): The skeleton file of subject `s` in `dir`: `02.asf`.
- `CMU_CACHE` (const): Where takes go: `.cache/anim/cmu/`.
- `cmuAll` (function): Every take: the archive's, read in a few dozen ranged requests, and the motion list's that it lacks.
- `cmuArchive` (const): The archive, its directory read (two small requests); entries are read only when asked for.
- `cmuGet` (function): The cached paths of takes `ids` (`02_01`), each with its subject's skeleton, fetching what is missing.
- `cmuIndex` (function): The site's motion list, from `index.tsv` in `dir` (fetched and written there once).
- `IndexedTake` (interface): A take on the site's motion list.
- `parseMotionList` (function): The takes on the site's full motion list (`search.php?subjectnumber=%&motion=%`), from its HTML.
- `SITE` (const): The site; it serves plain HTTP.

### [`tools/anim/contacts.ts`](../tools/anim/contacts.ts)

- `AIRBORNE` (const): How long (s) nothing may be held before a foot's contact is a landing: a jump's, not a run's flight.
- `CARRY` (const): How far (mm) the pelvis must move past a held hand or raised foot over its hold.
- `detectContacts` (function): A capture's contacts and events (see the file comment), on its rest body `R`; `clip` is the capture fitted (its strike is timed on what plays) and `tags` its catalog words.
- `FOOT_CLEAR` (const): How far above the floor (mm) a foot's sole may be and still stand on it.
- `HAND_FLOOR` (const): How far above the floor (mm) a hand's knuckle may be and still lie on it.
- `HANG` (const): How far (mm) under a hand held above the head the pelvis hangs when the body hangs from it.
- `HOLD` (const): How long (s) a hand or a raised foot must hold still to count.
- `HOLD_REACH` (const): How far (mm) a held point may stray from where its hold began.
- `STILL` (const): How slowly (mm/s) a held point moves in the ground's frame.
- `treadmill` (function): The ground's velocity under an in-place loop (mm/s; zero for any other clip): of the planted balls' median velocity along the floor and the velocity most hand and foot frames share (a ladder's, a wall's), whichever more of the hand and foot frames move with.

### [`tools/anim/cut.ts`](../tools/anim/cut.ts)

- `cutSet` (function): Cuts the clips `picks` out of `sets` into a new set named `name` (see the file comment).

### [`tools/anim/cycle.ts`](../tools/anim/cycle.ts)

- `bestCycle` (function): The best cycle in seconds `from`–`to` of a take of `count` frames at `src` a second: `[start, end, seam]`, in seconds, `seam` the cost that remained.

### [`tools/anim/fetch.ts`](../tools/anim/fetch.ts)

- `fetchMesh2Motion` (function): Mesh2Motion's three files in `dir` (from the repository root `root`), fetched when missing or changed; each is checked against its sha256, and a file that does not match is an error naming it and the fix.
- `MESH2MOTION` (const): Mesh2Motion's commit and its three files' sha256.
- `MESH2MOTION_CACHE` (const): Where `x anim fetch` keeps Mesh2Motion's files.
- `SET_SOURCES` (const): Every set's originals (a set not named here has none to re-import).
- `SetSource` (interface): Whether a set's originals can be re-imported here, and why not when they cannot.

### [`tools/anim/find.ts`](../tools/anim/find.ts)

- `catalogRows` (function): Every set's catalog rows, in set and clip order.
- `ClipHit` (interface): One clip a search found: its `set/clip`, its catalog row and its score.
- `findClips` (function): Searches the sets, then the ledger, for `words` (see the file comment).
- `Found` (interface): What a search found: every hit, a count, and the lines that show the best.
- `TakeHit` (interface): One CMU take a search found, not yet in a set.

### [`tools/anim/glb-fixture.ts`](../tools/anim/glb-fixture.ts)

- `FixtureTrack` (interface): One animation track: a bone, a path, key times and flat values, optionally quantized or splined.
- `FixtureVertex` (interface): A vertex of `riggedGlb`'s skinned mesh: where it sits in the bind pose (metres) and its bones' weights.
- `GlbBuilder` (class): Packs elements into one binary buffer, one buffer view and accessor each.
- `riggedGlb` (function): A T-posed Unreal-named humanoid with `clips` (by name, each a list of tracks) as a `.glb`; with `mesh`, a skinned mesh of those vertices too, each bone's inverse bind matrix taking the bind pose to the bone's own frame.
- `turn` (function): A rotation of `deg` degrees about `axis` as `[x, y, z, w]`.

### [`tools/anim/glb-library.ts`](../tools/anim/glb-library.ts)

- `GlbCapture` (type): A captured clip and the rate its keys were exported at.
- `GlbLibrary` (interface): A library read from a `.glb`: its rig, its clips as body points, its mannequin's look, and what is worth noting.
- `listGlb` (function): What a `.glb` holds, for `x anim import --list`: its rig (or none), its clips and its bones.
- `MannequinBody` (interface): The mannequin's look, measured from a Rigify mesh: height (mm), segment radii and joint-ring bands.
- `readGlbLibrary` (function): Reads a library from a `.glb`'s bytes (`file` names it), sampling every clip at `fps` (see the file comment).

### [`tools/anim/glb.ts`](../tools/anim/glb.ts)

- `Glb` (interface): A parsed `.glb`: its JSON, the whole file and where the binary chunk's data starts.
- `glbBytes` (function): A `.glb` file's bytes from a document and its binary data (for tests and tools that write one).
- `GltfAccessor` (interface): An accessor: how to read typed elements out of a buffer view.
- `GltfAnimation` (interface): An animation: channels targeting node paths, through samplers.
- `GltfJson` (interface): The parts of a glTF document the importer reads (anything else is ignored).
- `GltfNode` (interface): A node: its name, children, and rest transform.
- `mat` (function): A transform matrix from a translation, a rotation and a scale.
- `mul` (function): The product `a · b`.
- `nodeTree` (function): The document's node tree.
- `NodeTree` (interface): A node tree: each node's parent (−1 for a root), the order that visits parents first, and names by any case.
- `parseGlb` (function): Splits a `.glb` into its JSON and the binary chunk's start; `file` names it in errors.
- `readAccessor` (function): An accessor's elements: numbers for SCALAR, else arrays of its components, normalized when it says so.
- `sampleTrack` (function): A track's value at `time`: held before its first key and after its last, in-betweened as it says between.
- `slerp` (function): The shortest rotation from `a` toward `b`, a share `t` of the way (normalized-linear when they nearly agree).
- `Track` (interface): One animation channel: the node and path it moves, its key times and values, and how it in-betweens.
- `tracksOf` (function): An animation's tracks (channels with no node, or moving weights, are left out).
- `xf` (const): Point `p` transformed by `m`.

### [`tools/anim/import.ts`](../tools/anim/import.ts)

- `Catalog` (type): A catalog: each clip's `[tags, desc, orig?]`, plus `$sources`, `$skip` and (CMU) `$pick`.
- `fitFormat2` (function): A capture fitted in format 2: hands, grips and foot roll on every key, and the spine override where the shares miss the capture by more than `SPINE_MISS` and it brings the worst frame closer (it can bare a long neck's own miss: CMU's).
- `ImportOptions` (interface): What to import and how (see the file comment).
- `importSet` (function): Imports a set (see the file comment); `notes` says what was left out, warned of or measured.

### [`tools/anim/ledger.ts`](../tools/anim/ledger.ts)

- `Category` (interface): One category: its name, its file, its number of takes and its pattern (none for `other` and `undescribed`).
- `categoryOf` (function): A take's category: the first whose pattern matches its description, lower-cased; `undescribed` or `other` else.
- `compareIds` (function): Numeric order of take ids (`2_10` after `2_9`).
- `Ledger` (interface): The whole ledger, and each file's comment lines (kept on writing).
- `LEDGER_DIR` (const): The split ledger's directory, `data/anim/cmu/`.
- `ledgerFiles` (function): The ledger's files as text, by name: each category's rows, the index with their counts, and the subjects.
- `queryLedger` (function): The takes matching every word (a category's name, or text in the id, description, flags, note or clips used).
- `readLedger` (function): Reads the ledger in `dir`.
- `Subject` (interface): One subject: its number, its number of takes and its description on the site's motion list.
- `Take` (type): One take's row, with the category its file names.
- `TAKE_COLUMNS` (const): The columns of each category file, in order.
- `writeLedger` (function): Writes the ledger into `dir`; returns the files whose text changed.

### [`tools/anim/legacy-readable.ts`](../tools/anim/legacy-readable.ts)

- `CLIP_FPS` (const): The rate the clips are decoded at, frames per second.
- `clipVectorFiles` (function): The files `x port refs --clips` writes, from the checkout at `sourcePath`: `clips/` (the README, and each set's samples and checksums), returned in `files`, which tools/cmd/port.ts writes and checksums; and every frame of each set, written here to `out/port/clips/<set>.json` under `root` and listed in `artifacts`.
- `clipVectorsReadme` (function): The README written beside the clip vectors, naming the source commit and the files decoded.
- `CURATED_SETS` (const): The curated sets, 325 clips (HERO, Emberdeep's subset, is dropped: PLAN.md §10.1).
- `decodeLegacyClip` (function): Every frame of a clip decoded by the oracle at 30 fps on its own source's rest body: frames × 108 float32s.
- `float32Number` (function): A float32 as the double of its shortest decimal that reads back to it through `Math.fround`, `-0` kept.
- `frameCount` (const): How many frames a clip of `dur` seconds has at 30 fps (`my-3d2dge:src/mocap/mocap.js`'s count).
- `framesSha256` (const): The sha256 of decoded frames: their float32 bytes, little-endian, frame after frame.
- `LEGACY_CODEC` (const): The codec's file in the source checkout.
- `legacyClipVectors` (function): One set's clip vectors, `file` naming it: each clip's `sha256` of every frame and its sampled frames, as committed; with `every`, each clip's every frame instead (the full set, for out/port/clips/).
- `LegacyReadable` (interface): The parts of the source's `MocapReadable` the tests and `x port` call (its own names; see the source).
- `LegacySet` (interface): A source set file's object (`window.MOCAP[name]`), as the tests read it.
- `loadLegacyReadable` (function): The source's `MocapReadable`, loaded from the checkout at `sourcePath`.
- `readLegacySet` (function): The source's set `name` (`quaternius`, `mesh2motion`, `cmu`, `hero`), read from `src/mocap/sets/<name>.js`.
- `sampledFrames` (const): The frames committed for a clip of `n` frames: the first, and those a third and two thirds of the way in.

### [`tools/anim/library.ts`](../tools/anim/library.ts)

- `ACTIONS_DIR` (const): The engine's actions, one file each (`{ "action": "<name>", …spec }`).
- `defineActions` (function): Defines every action of `ACTIONS_DIR`, in file order, into `registry` (the shared one) and returns them: a file defined before with the same spec is kept (`loadActions`), so a second call changes nothing.
- `defineLibrary` (function): Registers every set of the library, then the mannequin, into `registry` (once); returns the sets' ids.
- `libraryDirs` (function): The library's set directories (`cmu`, `quaternius`…): each directory of `root` with a set header, sorted.

### [`tools/anim/rates.ts`](../tools/anim/rates.ts)

- `amcFrames` (const): How many frames an `.amc` take has.
- `applyRates` (function): Writes the evidence into the ledger's rows: the rate, and the evidence in place of `fps?`.
- `c3dEvidence` (function): The rate in a take's C3D file on the site, when it has one there and its frames agree with the `.amc`'s.
- `c3dHeader` (function): A C3D header's point frame rate and number of frames (an Intel-format file; another is refused).
- `RateEvidence` (interface): What settles a take's rate.
- `twinCandidates` (function): Listed takes the ledger measured the same as `id` (length, stretch, fit, travel, hips): its possible twins.
- `verifyRates` (function): Verifies the rate of each take in `ids` (default: every `fps?` take), downloading what it compares into `dir`; `readC3d` reads the first kilobyte of a C3D file's URL (by default, by an HTTP range).

### [`tools/anim/repack.ts`](../tools/anim/repack.ts)

- `ALT_TAG` (const): The tag of a clip that is another set's clip again (it has an `orig`): finders rank it after the original.
- `CATALOG_COLUMNS` (const): The columns of `catalog.tsv`: a clip's name, length, loop, speed, tags, description, origins and fit.
- `CATALOG_FILE` (const): The generated index of a set's clips.
- `catalogTsv` (function): The set's `catalog.tsv`: three `#` comment lines, the columns, then one row per clip in the set's order, each stopping at its last field (`.editorconfig` trims trailing tabs).
- `clipSlug` (function): The file name of a clip, without `.json`: its name with each run of characters other than letters, digits, `_` and `-` made one `_`, and `_` and `-` trimmed from the ends.
- `CMU_CREDIT` (const): The credit every CMU set carries: CMU's terms in short (data/anim/SOURCES.md has them verbatim) and the acknowledgment the database asks for, verbatim.
- `joinSet` (function): Reads a set's directory files back into the set it was split from (`where` names it in errors): the clips in the order `_set.json`'s `fit` lists them, then any others by file name.
- `keepUpgrades` (function): `set` with the clips its committed version in `root` re-imported from their source (WP 8.8: `via: "source"`, tools/anim/upgrade.ts) taken from it, with their fits and its format, so a curated set repacks as committed and never undoes the upgrade; every other clip stays the source's.
- `legacySetFiles` (function): The files of my-3d2dge's three curated sets (HERO dropped), from the checkout at `sourcePath`, by directory.
- `main` (function): The command line (see the file comment).
- `readPlainSet` (function): A plain JSON set, as shardfall writes it (text, or an object), read through the codec's parser.
- `readSet` (function): The set stored in `data/anim/sets/<dir>/` (or under `root`, or at `dir` when absolute), rejoined.
- `readSetDir` (function): Reads a set's directory: every file in it, by name.
- `repackSets` (function): Repacks sets into `root` (see the file comment): plain JSON sets from `paths`, else the curated sets the my-3d2dge checkout still provides (mesh2motion and cmu; WP 8.10 replaced quaternius), their clips re-imported from the source kept (`keepUpgrades`); with `check` it only compares.
- `SET_FILE` (const): The file that holds a set's header: everything but its clips.
- `setDirName` (const): A set's directory name: its name, slugged, in lower case (`STYLE100_BACK` → `style100_back`).
- `SetFiles` (type): A set's directory as text: file name → contents.
- `SETS_DIR` (const): The sets' directory, `data/anim/sets/`: one directory per set, named by `setDirName`.
- `splitSet` (function): Writes a set as its directory's files: one `text()` per clip, `_set.json` and `catalog.tsv` (the file comment).
- `tagAlternates` (function): The set with `alt` added last to the tags of each clip made from another set's clip (one with an `orig`).
- `withCmuTerms` (function): The CMU set with CMU's terms in each of its source records, as the CMU catalog states them, and `CMU_CREDIT` as its credit: my-3d2dge's set said "free for all uses" in both; WP 8.1 corrected the catalog, and the importer (`x anim import --cmu`) writes what it says.
- `writeSetDir` (function): Writes a set's files into `dir`, made if missing, and removes the files it no longer has; lists what changed.

### [`tools/anim/rigs.ts`](../tools/anim/rigs.ts)

- `bonesFor` (function): Each of the 36 body points with the bone (and the spot on it) that gives it, in `POSE_POINTS` order.
- `BoneSpot` (type): Where on a bone a point sits: its head (absent), its far end, or 12 cm in front of it.
- `PointBone` (type): One body point's bone: `[point, bone, where]`.
- `recogniseRig` (const): The rig whose `test` bone the file has (`has` matches names whatever their case), or undefined.
- `Rig` (interface): A rig: the bone that identifies it, its root, its limb and core bones, and its measured segments.
- `RIGS` (const): The rigs the importer knows, by name.
- `Segment` (type): A segment whose thickness the mesh gives: `[from point, to point, bone that owns its vertices]`.

### [`tools/anim/shardfall.ts`](../tools/anim/shardfall.ts)

- `adoptSet` (function): A set of shardfall's as this library keeps it (the file comment): each clip marked `via: "shardfall"`, a `body` after its `sources` (v1's, or `null` without `v1`), and the clips named in `keep` taken from `v1`, marked `via: "v1"`, each after the clip it followed in v1, with its `fit` entry.
- `CATALOGS_DIR` (const): The catalogs' directory, `data/anim/catalogs/`.
- `main` (function): The command line (see the file comment), writing under `sets` and `catalogs`.
- `markVia` (function): The clip, marked as having come `via` that route (`shardfall`, `v1`): `via` last in its header, before its keys.
- `readShardfallSet` (function): The set of shardfall's in `dir` (a key of `SHARDFALL_SETS`), read from the checkout at `shardfallPath`, as is.
- `readV1Set` (const): my-3d2dge's set `name` from the checkout at `my3d2dgePath`, read through the codec's parser.
- `SHARDFALL_CATALOGS` (const): The catalogs that come from shardfall (its `anim/catalogs/`), by file name: 100STYLE's seven and Quaternius v2's.
- `SHARDFALL_SETS` (const): The sets that come from shardfall, by directory: each one's file in shardfall at `fa2dab6`.
- `shardfallCatalogFiles` (function): The catalogs in `SHARDFALL_CATALOGS`, by file name: shardfall's, formatted by Prettier as the repository is.
- `shardfallSet` (function): The set in `dir` as this library keeps it, from the shardfall checkout and, for a set in `V1_SETS`, the my-3d2dge checkout (throws without it, naming the fix).
- `shardfallSetFiles` (function): The files of every set in `SHARDFALL_SETS`, by directory, as the repacker writes them.
- `V1_KEPT` (const): The clips a set keeps from my-3d2dge's v1 of it, by directory: those shardfall's version dropped.
- `V1_SETS` (const): The set of my-3d2dge whose `body` and `V1_KEPT` clips a shardfall set takes, by directory.

### [`tools/anim/survey.ts`](../tools/anim/survey.ts)

- `CMU_CATALOG` (const): The CMU catalog, whose `$pick` names the take each clip of the CMU set was cut from.
- `flagsOf` (function): The flags a take's measurements earn: upside down (over 2 frames), feet off the floor (60%), short, loose.
- `LIBRARY_DIR` (const): The converted library's directory, `.cache/anim/cmu-lib/`.
- `surveyCmu` (function): Surveys the downloaded takes (see the file comment); returns how many it converted and the seconds of motion.
- `SurveyOptions` (interface): What the survey does: which subjects, legacy reading, the ledger and library tolerances, and where things go.
- `usedBy` (function): Which clips of the CMU set each take feeds: `{ '13_17': ['Boxing_Guard_Loop', 'Boxing_Jab'] }`.

### [`tools/anim/upgrade.ts`](../tools/anim/upgrade.ts)

- `apartOf` (function): How far apart (mm) two clips decode, mean and worst, at 30 fps over the shorter.
- `judge` (function): The verdict on swapping `fresh` in for `held` (see the file comment).
- `readUpgraded` (function): `UPGRADE_FILE` as committed (empty when there is none).
- `reimport` (function): Set directory `dir`'s originals imported again in format 2, from the repository root `root` (see fetch.ts).
- `UPGRADE_FILE` (const): The clips each re-imported set kept, and why: `{ set: { swapped, of, kept: { clip: why } } }`.
- `Upgraded` (interface): One set's line in `UPGRADE_FILE`.
- `upgradedOf` (function): Set `dir`'s line for `UPGRADE_FILE` from its verdicts.
- `upgradeSet` (function): `held` with `fresh`'s clips swapped in where they keep parity (see the file comment): the set, now format 2, and a verdict per clip in the set's order.
- `Verdict` (interface): What happened to one clip: swapped or kept, why, and the numbers (mm) that decided it.
- `writeUpgraded` (function): Writes set `dir`'s line into `UPGRADE_FILE`, the others kept, sets in name order.

### [`tools/anim/view.ts`](../tools/anim/view.ts)

- `bakedPoints` (function): The 36 decode points of `baked` at `t`, by FK on its rest body's own skeleton (mm, rig frame).
- `bakeReport` (function): A baked clip, its tracks' size in bytes and its FK parity with the decode (mean and worst, mm).
- `ClipRef` (interface): A clip found in the library: its set's directory and header, its name, the clip and its rest body.
- `clipSheet` (function): The clip as a contact sheet: `frames` poses spread over it, each from `views`, on its rest body's skeleton.
- `resolveClip` (function): Finds `<set>/<clip>` in `setsDir`, or a clip name only one set has; errors name the closest choices.
- `shownDir` (function): A directory as an error names it: from the repository root when it is inside it, else as given.

### [`tools/anim/zip.ts`](../tools/anim/zip.ts)

- `ByteSource` (interface): Where bytes come from: `bytes(from, to)` gives bytes `from`–`to` inclusive, or with `from` < 0 the last `-from`.
- `fetchBytes` (const): A whole file on the web (`curl` follows redirects and the proxy settings).
- `fileSource` (function): A file on disk, read by ranges.
- `MAX_GAP` (const): The most unwanted bytes `readMany` fetches between two wanted entries rather than start a new request.
- `MAX_RANGE` (const): The most bytes `readMany` asks for at once.
- `openZip` (function): Opens an archive: reads its end record and central directory (two reads), not its entries.
- `urlSource` (function): A file on the web, read by ranges.
- `Zip` (interface): An archive's entries, and a reader for them.
- `zipBytes` (function): A zip archive of `files` (name → text), deflated, for tests and tools that write one.
- `ZipEntry` (interface): One file in an archive: its name, compression, packed and unpacked sizes, and where its local header is.

### [`tools/checkAll.ts`](../tools/checkAll.ts)

- `CACHE_DIRS` (const): The cache directories ESLint and Prettier create on a cold run.
- `CHECK_TOOLS` (const): The T0 tools, in the order their output is printed; `tsc` runs package.json's `typecheck` command.
- `checkAll` (function): Runs every tool in parallel, prints their output in order, and returns the exit code (0 only if all pass).
- `CheckTool` (interface): One T0 tool: its name and its command line, run from the repository root.

### [`tools/cmd/anim.ts`](../tools/cmd/anim.ts)

- `default` (default): The animation library's tools (PLAN.md §10, WP 8.5): find a clip, show it, bake it, draw it, cut a smaller set, import libraries, fetch their sources and re-import them, all from the command line, with no browser.
- `subcommandOf` (function): The subcommand named first, or a usage error naming the closest.
- `targetOf` (const): The report's target: the subcommand and its first arguments.

### [`tools/cmd/audio.ts`](../tools/cmd/audio.ts)

- `default` (default): Renders a sound in Node and prints its numbers, or mixes a replay's sound events (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 9.4, I-23).
- `encodeWav` (function): Encodes samples as a 16-bit mono PCM WAV file, clamped to ±1.
- `mixSoundEvents` (function): The events' effects rendered (each once per variant, seed 0, at 44,100 Hz) and summed into one mono mix at least `seconds` long, with each event's span in it, `[start, end)` in samples.
- `Picture` (type): A picture as RGBA bytes, row by row from the top.
- `replaySoundEvents` (function): Plays `replay` (its scene defined on `registry`) step by step through `createPlayback` (engine/app/playback.ts, the page's real-time playback), hashing its checkpoints, and reads the sound events from the sim's event trace after setup and after each step, as the box's page does (labs/box/sounds/events.ts).
- `SoundEvent` (interface): One sound event of a replay: when, from which sim event, which effect at which gain and variant.
- `SoundTimeline` (interface): A replay's sound events, the problems of those that name no sound, its length and the hashes of its checkpoints.
- `spectrogram` (function): A spectrogram of `samples` as RGBA bytes (see the file comment for its axes and colours).
- `SPECTROGRAM` (const): The spectrogram's size, FFT length, floor (dBFS) and lowest frequency (Hz).

### [`tools/cmd/check.ts`](../tools/cmd/check.ts)

- `assetRules` (function): The engine repository's rules; in a game, its approvals stand without their records, which stayed behind.
- `assetScan` (const): The asset scan (doctrine: Assets).
- `binaryKind` (function): What binary format `bytes` (a file named `path`) is, or undefined for text.
- `CheckContext` (interface): What a plugin is given: the repository root, and whether this checkout is an ultracode lane.
- `CheckOutcome` (interface): What a plugin found.
- `CheckPlugin` (interface): One repository check.
- `default` (default): Runs the repository checks no standard tool covers, last in `npm run check` (PLAN.md §8.1).
- `discoverPlugins` (function): The plugins: the asset scan, then each `check` exported by a module in `tools/cmd/` (a text scan finds them).
- `isLane` (function): Whether `root` is an ultracode lane: `X_LANE` when set (0 or 1), else whether it is a linked git worktree.
- `repositoryFiles` (function): The files git tracks or would track under `root`: tracked plus untracked, ignored ones left out.
- `runChecks` (function): Runs `plugins` side by side and merges what they found; in a lane, `warnInLane` plugins only warn.
- `scanAssets` (function): The asset scan of `files`, paths under `root` as `repositoryFiles` lists them.

### [`tools/cmd/ci.ts`](../tools/cmd/ci.ts)

- `CI_STEPS` (const): The steps of `x ci --local`, in order (PLAN.md §8.9); the quick gate leaves out the `full` ones.
- `CiDeps` (interface): What `x ci` reaches outside itself; the tests replace each part.
- `CiRun` (interface): A whole run of the gate.
- `CiStep` (interface): One step of the gate.
- `createCiCommand` (function): Builds the `x ci` command; the tests pass fakes for the step runner, git, the selections and the clock.
- `default` (default): The merge gate and the full run (PLAN.md §8.9, WP 0.9; ADR-0023).
- `FULL_ONLY` (const): Why the quick gate leaves a step out.
- `Head` (interface): HEAD's commit and branch, and the uncommitted changes (`git status --porcelain` lines).
- `KEPT_CACHES` (const): What `npm ci` must not wipe, relative to the root: the tools' caches, and Vitest's record of each file's duration, from which it starts the longest files first (without it, T1 took 39 s instead of 36 s).
- `parseShard` (function): `--shard`'s `<i>/<n>`, 1 ≤ i ≤ n; a usage error otherwise.
- `readHead` (function): Reads `Head` with git.
- `readOrigin` (function): The repository's `origin` URL, or undefined (no git, no remote).
- `runCi` (function): Runs the gate in `root`: the quick steps, or every step with `full` (a share of them with `shard`); then the long runs with `long`, the budget, the summary and, when green and whole, `out/ci/last-green`.
- `Shard` (interface): One machine's share of a sharded full run: the `index`th of `total`, from 1.
- `spawnStep` (const): Runs `command` as a child process, stdout and stderr captured together, colours off.
- `StepOutcome` (interface): What running one command gave: its exit code (1 when it could not start), its wall time and its output.
- `StepResult` (interface): One step's result.
- `StepRunner` (type): Runs one command from `cwd`; the tests inject a fake.

### [`tools/cmd/deps.ts`](../tools/cmd/deps.ts)

- `check` (const): The `deps` plugin of `x check` (T0): the offline check.
- `createDepsCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the day, the active node, a fixture registry and a recording runner.
- `default` (default): Checks the dependency pins against `tools/deps.json` (offline), and asks the registry for compatible releases to adopt and for lines that have qualified (PLAN.md §6.10; doctrine: Mastery, Common ground).

### [`tools/cmd/describe.ts`](../tools/cmd/describe.ts)

- `afterMs` (const): A watch that stops the child `ms` after it started.
- `createDescribeCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests give the child process's watch (`hang`) and the time limit its message names.
- `default` (default): Lists the registries from their schemas (PLAN.md §8.1, §6.6): `x describe` names every kind with its entry count, `x describe <kind>` gives its fields (type, default, range, unit, docs) and ids, and `x describe <kind> <id>` one entry's values, `*` marking those that differ from the default.
- `describeFile` (function): Where `x describe [kind [id]]` writes the whole description: `describe.json` beside its report.
- `describeInWorker` (function): Runs the listing in a child Node process over `root`'s registrations; resolves to what it sent, or to the failure when it hung (stopped by `hang`, after `timeoutMs` by default) or ended without a listing, naming the module it was loading.
- `fieldLine` (function): One line for a field: name, type, default, range, unit, values, flags, then its description.
- `HangWatch` (type): When the child process counts as hung: `watch(stop)` arms the watch, hears each module the child starts loading (`loading`), and is `done` when the child ends.
- `idsLine` (function): A kind's ids as one line of at most `IDS_LINE` characters; a cut list says how many there are and where.
- `listing` (function): What one listing prints, from the shared registry, ending with where the whole description is when a line was cut; throws the registry's error for an unknown kind or id.
- `Listing` (interface): What one listing prints, besides the verdict, and the data `describe.json` holds.
- `loadRegistrations` (function): Imports each module that registers content, telling `loading` first; a module that fails becomes a warning.
- `registersContent` (function): Whether a parsed module calls something that registers content (comments, strings and declarations aside).
- `REGISTRATION_ROOTS` (const): Where modules that register content live.
- `registrationModules` (function): The modules under `root` that register content, repository-relative and sorted.
- `resolveTarget` (function): The kind and id `x describe` was asked for, as the registry names them (see the file comment): a lone `kind:name` that is no kind is that kind's entry; a `name` that is no id of `kind` is `kind:name` when that one is.
- `WORKER_TIMEOUT_MS` (const): How long the child process may take before it is stopped and the module it was loading named (ms).
- `WorkerDone` (interface): What the child process reports when it is done: what loaded, and the listing or the usage problem.
- `WorkerMessage` (type): One message from the child process: the module it starts loading, or the end.

### [`tools/cmd/docs.ts`](../tools/cmd/docs.ts)

- `check` (const): The `x check` plugin: the drift checks without the examples (they run in T1 and in `x docs --check`).
- `checkComments` (function): What the code says about its own documentation: missing or long file comments, undocumented exports, bad codes.
- `createDocsCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the source checkouts and the planned paths.
- `default` (default): Generates and checks the docs that come from the code (PLAN.md §6.8, §8.12): `docs/INDEX.md`, `docs/API.md` and `docs/ERRORS.md`, the `@example` blocks, the paths the docs mention, and `docs/PROGRESS.md`'s length.
- `DocsOptions` (type): Options for the checks; tests inject the source checkouts and the planned paths.
- `driftChecks` (function): Every drift check except the examples: comments, codes, paths, generated docs and PROGRESS.md.
- `MAX_COMMENT_LINES` (const): The longest a file comment (PLAN.md §6.8) or `docs/PROGRESS.md` (one screen) may run, in lines.
- `PROGRESS` (const): The one screen every session reads first: where things stand, what is next, the open issues.

### [`tools/cmd/dump.ts`](../tools/cmd/dump.ts)

- `default` (default): Dumps the scene and the state of the page `x inspect` keeps open, as text (PLAN.md §8.1, §8.3, WP 2.7): `__engine.scene.dump()`, one object a line (name, type, position, size, material, triangles, entity), then the run's tick, hash and entities.

### [`tools/cmd/engine.ts`](../tools/cmd/engine.ts)

- `check` (const): `x check`'s plugin `engine`: in a game, its engine files as shipped or declared; in the engine, nothing to do.
- `default` (default): A game's engine (PLAN.md WP 10.7, ADR-0024): in a game made by tools/game/new-game.mjs, which engine it is on and whether its engine files are as shipped; in the engine's own repository, the proof that a new game works.
- `engineFindings` (function): A game's engine check: each engine file changed or missing that ENGINE-FEEDBACK.md does not declare.
- `engineOnlyListed` (function): The engine's own commands that a game's `x help` listed: none, when game mode works.

### [`tools/cmd/esc.ts`](../tools/cmd/esc.ts)

- `check` (const): The `esc` plugin of `x check` (T0): well-formed records, none overdue, a current README.
- `checkEscalations` (function): The `x check` rules: well-formed records with unique ids, no open record overdue, a current README.
- `createEscCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the clock and the environment.
- `default` (default): Escalations and the calls made without an answer (DOCTRINE.md, Escalation; PLAN.md §8.14, ADR-0017): writes and lists the records in docs/escalations/ (tools/lib/escalations.ts), and checks them as `x check`'s `esc` plugin.
- `EscOptions` (interface): What the command reads from outside; tests pass a virtual clock and a fixed environment.
- `messageFor` (function): The short message `open` prints for the owner: the question, the options and what happens without an answer.
- `runId` (function): The run a record belongs to: `--run`, else `$X_RUN`, else the Claude Code session, else `local`.

### [`tools/cmd/eval.ts`](../tools/cmd/eval.ts)

- `default` (default): Evaluates JavaScript in the page `x inspect` keeps open, and prints its value as JSON (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 2.7): `node x eval "__engine.hash()"`.

### [`tools/cmd/eye.ts`](../tools/cmd/eye.ts)

- `default` (default): `node x eye <scene>` (PLAN.md WP 12.3, §5.8): the agent eye in Node, no GPU.
- `EYE_FRAMES` (const): The frames the camera is moved on by before the eye looks: a second of a page's, so a follow camera has swung out.
- `EYE_PRINT` (const): The printed picture's size at most: 56 × 16 characters, the page's 16:9 in a terminal's tall characters.
- `printOf` (function): `map` (the eye's picture, a character a cell) shrunk to at most `size` for a terminal: each printed character stands for the cells under it, the player's `@` if any, else the thing most of them show, else a wall over a floor.
- `seenText` (function): What the summary says it sees: the first `SUMMARY_THINGS` things (`thingText`), then how many more.
- `SUMMARY_THINGS` (const): How many things the summary names, most cells first; `eye.json` lists them all.
- `thingText` (function): One thing seen, as the summary names it: the player, the level, or its kind and entity; its share, or its cells.

### [`tools/cmd/feel.ts`](../tools/cmd/feel.ts)

- `courseName` (const): A course's name in its lab: its id without `course:<lab>-`.
- `default` (default): `node x feel <lab> [--course <name,…|all>]` (PLAN.md WP 13.4, docs/PLAYGROUND.md §9.1): runs a lab's feel courses headless and judges every number against its reference and tolerance (engine/dev/feel/run.ts).
- `labOf` (function): The lab a target names (`labs/playground`, `labs/playground/` or `playground`), and its directory.
- `missText` (const): A miss as a sentence: the number, its reference and its tolerance.
- `toleranceText` (function): A measure's tolerance for reading: `±2%`, `±0.3`, `±1 tick`; several are "or".

### [`tools/cmd/film.ts`](../tools/cmd/film.ts)

- `addWorktree` (function): Checks commit `sha` out in a temporary worktree under out/film/, with this tree's node_modules linked into it.
- `default` (default): Films a page (PLAN.md WP 3.11, I-28): plays a script of steps over `__engine.input` and `step`, shoots a frame wherever the script says, lays the frames out on a labelled contact sheet, and with `--compare <ref>` films the same steps at that commit and attributes every pixel that differs to an object, through the ID pass.
- `FilmStep` (interface): One step of a film: the `__engine` member it calls and the arguments; the verb `shot` films a frame.
- `hasFile` (const): Whether commit `sha` has the file `path`.
- `parseSteps` (function): Reads a script of steps (see the file comment); throws `UsageError` naming the step it cannot read.
- `PARTS` (const): How many parts, each followed by a frame, a `step` is filmed in when the script never shoots.
- `removeWorktree` (function): Removes a worktree `addWorktree` made: the node_modules link first (never what it points at), then the checkout.
- `resolveRef` (function): The commit `ref` names, in full; throws `UsageError` when it names none.
- `sameSources` (const): Whether the working tree's sources are commit `sha`'s: no tracked change, no untracked file git does not ignore.
- `SHOT` (const): The shot a film takes: the pixels, the ID pass and the thumbnail, without the look metrics.
- `simSteps` (const): `n` sim steps with what the virtual device holds.

### [`tools/cmd/gallery.ts`](../tools/cmd/gallery.ts)

- `BURST_SHOWN` (const): The least share an emitter covers in its fullest frame, about 8 pixels of 240 × 135: a burst thins to its last specks, and a sky effect run from the floor (snow, which no floor stops) falls out of sight at once.
- `default` (default): Contact sheets from the gallery (PLAN.md WP 7.7, §8.5): `node x gallery <kind> [id]` films every entry of a kind with a `gallery` field (engine/core/gallery.ts), or the one named, in a page's gallery: it opens `<page>#gallery/<kind>/<id>` as `x shot` opens a page (Vite, Chromium on WebGPU, the virtual clock, seed 1), calls `__engine.gallery.shoot` for each entry (engine/dev/galleryShoot.ts: each frame staged, its camera fitted, shot), and lays the frames out on x film's contact sheet (tools/lib/filmSheet.ts), each labelled: an entry a row, or eight entries a row when each has one frame.
- `emptyFrames` (function): The frames of `entry` that show too little: each of a still subject's below `SHOWN`; a burst's all of them when its fullest is below `BURST_SHOWN`.
- `Filmed` (interface): An entry's filmed frames, as `gallery.shoot` returns them; `burst` for an emitter's.
- `PAGE` (const): The page the gallery films unless `--page` says: every lab's entries registered.
- `readSize` (function): Reads `--size WxH`; throws `UsageError`.
- `seenShare` (function): What a shot's ID pass sees of its subject: the share of the frame besides the stage's ground (stage.ts).
- `sheetFrames` (function): The sheet's frames: every entry's in order, labelled, with its pixels.
- `SHOWN` (const): The least share of a frame a still subject covers in each of its frames: about 65 pixels of 240 × 135.
- `shows` (const): Whether a shot shows its subject: its ID pass sees at least `SHOWN` of it.
- `SIZE` (const): The shots' size unless `--size` says: 16:9, wide enough for a 30-letter label.

### [`tools/cmd/help.ts`](../tools/cmd/help.ts)

- `default` (default): Prints the generated help: every command, or one command's file comment and flags.

### [`tools/cmd/inspect.ts`](../tools/cmd/inspect.ts)

- `callSession` (function): Sends `op` with `body` to the session; resolves with its JSON reply, or rejects with its error's message.
- `default` (default): Keeps one headless page open over the Vite dev server, for `x eval`, `x dump` and `x set`, which `x shot` reuses while it runs (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 2.7; doctrine: Agent-operable).
- `findSession` (function): The running session's info, or null; a session whose process is gone is cleared.
- `Opened` (interface): A shot taken (for `x shot`), with what the page said: its signal, its failures so far and its console.
- `pageErrorFinding` (const): A page error as a failure.
- `pageFailures` (function): The failures of a page that should be ready: its thrown errors, its error signals, no signal, another backend.
- `reloadLines` (const): The line every reply starts with when Vite reloaded the page since the last one, else nothing.
- `SESSION_FILE` (const): Where a running session says where it listens.
- `SessionInfo` (interface): What `session.json` holds.
- `sessionShot` (function): The session's `shot` op: the open tab when it shows `path`, else a new tab of the browser opened on `path`.
- `SessionTab` (interface): What the session's `shot` op works with: its tab, the page open in it, its browser, Vite's URL and the root.
- `shootInSession` (function): Shoots `path` through the running inspect session (tools/cmd/inspect.ts): its page when it shows `path`, else a new tab of its browser; null when the page has no `__engine.shot` (then `x shot` screenshots it itself).

### [`tools/cmd/lab.ts`](../tools/cmd/lab.ts)

- `createLabCommand` (function): Builds the command; tests inject the day.
- `default` (default): `node x lab` (PLAN.md WP 10.8): keeps the labs index, labs/labs.json, which the index page (labs/index/) and the labs suite (tests/e2e/labs.spec.ts) read through labs/index/labs.ts.
- `LAB_DAYS` (const): How long a temporary lab lasts by default, in days.
- `LABS_FILE` (const): The index's file, from the repository root.

### [`tools/cmd/mcp.ts`](../tools/cmd/mcp.ts)

- `default` (default): Serves the engine to MCP clients (PLAN.md §8.11, WP 7.6): `node x mcp` speaks the Model Context Protocol on stdin and stdout, so an agent that cannot run `node x` drives the engine as `x inspect`, `x eval` and `x shot` do.
- `openArgs` (function): What the flags name to open first, or undefined when they name nothing.

### [`tools/cmd/new.ts`](../tools/cmd/new.ts)

- `CheckName` (type): One check's name.
- `CHECKS` (const): The checks a kind may ask for.
- `default` (default): Scaffolds a new entry of a kind from its template (PLAN.md §8.13): `x new <kind> <id>` writes the files of `tools/templates/<kind>/`, filled in for the id, then runs the kind's checks and prints the summary.
- `fill` (function): Fills `{{id}}`, `{{name}}`, `{{NAME}}` and `{{dir}}` in `text`; throws on any other placeholder.
- `Kind` (interface): A kind, as its manifest declares it.
- `listKinds` (function): Reads and validates every kind under `tools/templates/`; throws naming the first problem.
- `NEXT` (const): What to do after writing an entry of a kind whose manifest has no `next`.
- `nextIn` (function): A `next` as a game reads it: there `x docs` is the engine's own command, and its checks take its place.
- `render` (function): The files an entry of `kind` with `id` consists of: repository path → formatted text.
- `runCheck` (function): Runs one check on the new files; returns one sentence per problem.
- `runChecks` (function): Runs a kind's checks on `files`: one line per check, and a finding per problem.
- `testKind` (function): Writes `kind`'s sample, checks it and removes it again.
- `writeFiles` (function): Writes rendered files; refuses (throws) when any exists.

### [`tools/cmd/perf.ts`](../tools/cmd/perf.ts)

- `agentsSetting` (function): The setting `asked` (`--agents`, else the budget's): an integer setting that allows the top rung's agents.
- `default` (default): Performance as counters against budgets, never frames per second (PLAN.md §8.1, §8.7, WPs 1.5 and 5.5).
- `measure` (function): One run's timings: ms per step, then per hash and per capture of the state it reached (10 of each).

### [`tools/cmd/port.ts`](../tools/cmd/port.ts)

- `buildFiles` (function): Every file of `PORT_DIR` but the checksums and `clips/`, by name, generated from the checkout at `sourcePath`.
- `check` (const): The `port` plugin of `x check`: the committed vectors still match their checksums.
- `CHECKSUMS` (const): The file in `PORT_DIR` that records every other file's sha256.
- `checkVectors` (function): Compares the vectors under `root` with their checksums, offline: a changed, missing or unlisted file fails.
- `default` (default): Records the reference vectors the ports from my-3d2dge are tested against (PLAN.md WP 0.11, §9.0): the old engine's own outputs as text JSON in `tests/baselines/port/`, with a generated README that says what each file holds, the source commit, the sampling and the conversion to my-3dge's frame (Appendix C).
- `layout` (function): Writes JSON in a stable layout: a container that fits in 120 columns stays on one line, and so does any array of scalars (one sample per line); the others open one item per line, indented by two spaces.
- `PORT_DIR` (const): Where the vectors live, relative to the repository root.
- `writeVectors` (function): Writes `files` (names may hold `/`) and their checksums into `dir`, and removes the files an earlier run wrote that are gone now; of the files this run does not `own`, it keeps the recorded checksums.

### [`tools/cmd/qa.ts`](../tools/cmd/qa.ts)

- `closestIds` (function): The ids among `ids` closest to `prefix`: the longest start they share with it first, then in id order; at most `n`.
- `compareWithBaselines` (function): Compares a family's violations with its baselines: failures for new or worse ones, warnings for slack entries.
- `default` (default): Runs content QA for the families named, against their baselines (PLAN.md §8.6).
- `kept` (const): Whether `id` passes the `only` prefixes.
- `loadFamily` (function): Loads `tools/qa/<family>.ts`'s default export.
- `QaBaseline` (interface): An accepted exception in `tests/baselines/qa-<family>[-<area>].json`.
- `QaContext` (interface): What a family is given: the repository root and the id prefixes to keep (empty: every id).
- `qaFamilies` (function): The families in `tools/qa/`, by file name.
- `QaFamily` (interface): A QA family: the default export of `tools/qa/<family>.ts`.
- `QaViolation` (interface): One violation a family found; a larger `value` is worse.
- `readBaselines` (function): Reads every baseline file of `family`, with a failure per malformed file or entry.
- `runQa` (function): Runs one family against its baselines; T1 tests call this (`expect((await runQa(ROOT, 'level')).failures)…`).

### [`tools/cmd/replay.ts`](../tools/cmd/replay.ts)

- `Checked` (interface): What `checkFiles` came to: the outcomes' lines, findings and metrics, and each file's verdict.
- `checkFile` (function): Plays one replay file in every runtime and judges it (see the file comment); writes nothing.
- `checkFiles` (function): Checks every file, then reads `pageErrors` (Chromium's), and only when nothing failed writes the goldens `--update` recorded.
- `default` (default): Replays against their golden hashes (PLAN.md §8.4, §6.5 items 8–9, WPs 1.5 and 2.7).
- `findParting` (function): The first step where any run parts from the first, compared there (`table` reads the components' registry).
- `Outcome` (interface): What one replay came to: its verdict, lines, bisect details, findings, metrics, and goldens to write.
- `parseSwap` (function): Parses `--swap`: `none`, or names from the swap (`sin,pow`).
- `partingLines` (function): The lines that tell a parting: the step, parts, entities and first field, then every field and the inputs.
- `PLATFORM` (const): This platform's golden key: `linux-x64`.
- `replayFiles` (function): The replay files a target names: the file, or every `*.replay.json` under the directory.
- `ReplayOptions` (interface): How replays are checked.
- `Run` (interface): A run of a replay: which runtime, and the hashes it took.
- `RunParting` (interface): Where two runs part: the step, the runs, and what differs there (engine/sim/replay.ts `partingOf`).

### [`tools/cmd/set.ts`](../tools/cmd/set.ts)

- `checkSetting` (function): Types `text` for the setting `path` on a fresh store; throws `UsageError` naming the closest path or the rule.
- `default` (default): Checks a setting against the settings schema, prints it as a URL parameter, and applies it to the page `x inspect` keeps open (PLAN.md §8.1, §3's Agent-operable, I-37, WP 2.7): `node x set box.room.speed 3`.
- `loadSettings` (function): Imports the modules that declare settings, so the shared registry knows them; returns them.
- `sceneModuleOf` (function): The module of `scene`: a module path, a scene id, or the name after an id's colon (`room` for `box:room`).
- `settingModules` (function): The modules that declare settings (`defineSettings(` in their text), tests aside; with `scene`, only its own.
- `settingParam` (function): A setting as a URL parameter: `path=value`, a string as it is, anything else as JSON.

### [`tools/cmd/sheet.ts`](../tools/cmd/sheet.ts)

- `default` (default): Draws a body's state matrix as a contact sheet, plus its numeric checks (PLAN.md WP 6.6, §8.5): `node x sheet <subject>` runs the humanoid through the states a QA id or prefix names, as the `anim` QA family does (tools/qa/anim.ts `humanoidStates`), draws them with `anim.sheet()` (engine/anim/sheet.ts) from the cameras of a `SHEET_CAMERAS` preset (engine/anim/stateMatrix.ts), and turns the SVG into a PNG in the platform's Chromium.
- `MAX_WIDTH` (const): The widest sheet, pixels (§8.5: contact sheets are capped at 1,600 px).
- `qaPrefixes` (function): The `only` prefixes of `subject`'s `anim` QA: itself, or for `humanoid` its kinds (never the library's clips).
- `sheetFor` (function): The sheet of `subject`: its frames (`sheetFrames`) drawn by `animSheet` from the cameras `cams` names (`move` for moves, else `body`) on the skeleton of `build`, so a build's own proportions are what the sheet shows.
- `sheetFrames` (function): The frames a sheet of `subject` draws, and whether they are moves (for the cameras).
- `SheetFramesOptions` (interface): What `sheetFrames` draws.
- `subjectIds` (function): The QA ids `subject` names on `build`: itself, or every id it prefixes (`humanoid`: all of them).

### [`tools/cmd/shot.ts`](../tools/cmd/shot.ts)

- `default` (default): Renders a page on WebGPU in the platform's Chromium and reports what it drew as numbers and text: the look metrics, the ID pass (which object covers which pixels) and a 48 × 27 text thumbnail; images only on demand.
- `encodePng` (function): Encodes RGBA bytes as an 8-bit RGBA PNG (Node's zlib; no image dependency).
- `frameMetrics` (const): The look metrics of a frame of RGBA bytes (engine/gfx/lookMetrics.ts), as the e2e suites import them from here.
- `judgeFrame` (function): The verdict on a frame's look notes: notes that fail are failures, the others warnings.
- `pageUrl` (function): The page's URL path with `scene`, `cam` and each `key=value` of `set` added as URL parameters.
- `READY_TIMEOUT_MS` (const): How long a page may take to signal ready or an error, in milliseconds.
- `resolvePage` (function): Turns a page argument into the URL path to open (relative to the server) and the file that must exist for it.
- `shotMetrics` (function): A shot's numbers for report.json: the look metrics, the ID-pass list and the marks' legend, flat.

### [`tools/cmd/sim.ts`](../tools/cmd/sim.ts)

- `default` (default): Runs a scene headless in Node and prints its hash and events (PLAN.md §8.1, WP 1.5).
- `feelLines` (function): The feel report as two lines of text, a third on the shooter model, rounded for reading (the metrics keep every digit).
- `feelMetrics` (function): The feel report as metrics, `feel.<name>`, the shooter model's as `feel.motion.<name>`.
- `feelOf` (function): The feel meter's report for a run's first player actor (the inspector member `feel`); a usage error without one.
- `HashedView` (interface): One run's view of a step, with the hash its runtime gave.
- `levelOf` (function): The level a scene loads, for `--map`: registered by its module, else read from its lab's or the fixtures' levels.
- `navMap` (function): The text map of `level`'s nav grid under `climb` (the crowd's by default), as `--map` writes it: a key, then one row per map row, and an A* route from the hero's spawn (else the first spawn) to the tile it reaches in the most steps.
- `nodeRuntime` (function): Replays in Node, in this process, on `registry` (the shared one by default): `x replay`'s first runtime.
- `parseSets` (function): `key=value` pairs as path → text; throws `UsageError` for a pair without `=`.
- `replayText` (function): A replay as readable text: its keys in file order, one change-point per line, each platform's hashes one step per line, numbers exact (`-0` kept, engine/core/hash.ts `serialize`).
- `Runtime` (interface): Where replays play: Node in this process, or Chromium in tests/pages/replay.html.
- `typedSets` (function): `--set` values typed and checked against the settings schema (after the scene module declared its settings).
- `writeReplay` (function): Writes a replay through Prettier with the repository's settings (wherever the file is); true when it changed.

### [`tools/cmd/src.ts`](../tools/cmd/src.ts)

- `default` (default): Prints and checks the read-only source checkouts, `$MY3D2DGE_SRC` and `$SHARDFALL_SRC`, at their pins.

### [`tools/eslint/askTheEntry.ts`](../tools/eslint/askTheEntry.ts)

- `default` (default): The local rule "ask the entry, never the id" (PLAN.md §6.6, ADR-0012): shared code reads an entry's hooks and fields, each with a default on the kind's schema, and never compares a registered id, so new content works without editing the code that uses it.
- `ID_SHAPE` (const): A registered id: a kind, a colon, a name (`move:slash`, `prop:crate`; PLAN.md §6.3).

### [`tools/eslint/banned.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.ts)

- `BANNED_FILES` (const): Where the bans apply.
- `BANNED_IMPORT_FILES` (const): The import bans also cover tests/: a bare `three` in a test page gets its own pre-bundled copy in Vite (WP 0.8).
- `bannedBlocks` (function): The banned-API blocks: imports and names over every file in scope, then syntax and properties by zone.
- `bannedPlugin` (const): The plugin the banned-API blocks use: core's restriction rules as `banned/<rule>`, and `no-namespace-names`.

### [`tools/eslint/family.ts`](../tools/eslint/family.ts)

- `Ban` (type): One entry of a restriction rule's options (`{ selector, message }`, `{ property, message }`…), plus its scope.
- `family` (function): Returns a plugin named `name` whose rules are the named core rules, unchanged.
- `messagesOf` (function): Every `message` in a list of blocks' rule options, `no-restricted-imports`'s paths and patterns included.
- `resolvingImports` (function): `plugin` with its `no-restricted-imports` matching each relative source as resolved from the importing file.
- `shortest` (function): A relative source's shortest spelling from `dir`: `./a/../b` is `./b`, and `../../engine/sim` from `engine/core` is `../sim`.
- `zoned` (function): Blocks that apply one aliased rule over `files` so each file gets exactly the bans that apply to it: one block for all `files`, then one per path an `only` or `except` names, the most specific last (flat config's last block wins).

### [`tools/eslint/index.ts`](../tools/eslint/index.ts)

- `askTheEntryBlocks` (function): The "ask the entry, never the id" block over shared code; `on` is `SWITCHES.askTheEntry` (WP 1.2 turns it on).
- `bannedBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/banned.ts`](../tools/eslint/banned.ts)): The banned-API blocks: imports and names over every file in scope, then syntax and properties by zone.
- `family` (function from [`tools/eslint/family.ts`](../tools/eslint/family.ts)): Returns a plugin named `name` whose rules are the named core rules, unchanged.
- `layerBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/layers.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.ts)): The layer rules' blocks, in order.
- `local` (const): The local plugin: rules no stock rule expresses, as `local/<rule>`.
- `publicApiBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/publicApi.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.ts)): The public-API blocks; `on` is `SWITCHES.publicApi` (on since WP 1.6).
- `simSideBlocks` (function from [`tools/eslint/simSide.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.ts)): The sim-side blocks: globals, properties and syntax over all sim-side files, then imports (core/math.ts last).

### [`tools/eslint/layers.ts`](../tools/eslint/layers.ts)

- `layerBlocks` (function): The layer rules' blocks, in order.
- `layerPlugin` (const): The plugin the layer blocks use: core's `no-restricted-imports`, resolving, as `layer/no-restricted-imports`.
- `THREE_MATH` (const): three.js's math classes, the only names `core/math.ts` takes from `three/webgpu` (§6.1); `Color` (from three.js's `src/math/`) since WP 1.1, for engine/core/color.ts (ADR-0020 amendment 1).

### [`tools/eslint/namespaceNames.ts`](../tools/eslint/namespaceNames.ts)

- `EntryName` (interface): One banned name of an entry point: its source, the namespace name the docs use, the name, and the fix.
- `namespaceNames` (const): The rule: options are the banned names (`EntryName`), each reported with its message wherever it is read.

### [`tools/eslint/publicApi.ts`](../tools/eslint/publicApi.ts)

- `publicApiBlocks` (function): The public-API blocks; `on` is `SWITCHES.publicApi` (on since WP 1.6).
- `publicApiPlugin` (const): The plugin the public-API blocks use: core's `no-restricted-imports` (resolving) and `no-unnamed-imports`.
- `SIM_SIDE_GAME_CODE` (const): Sim-side game code: the sim barrel only.
- `unnamedImports` (const): `public-api/no-unnamed-imports`: side-effect imports, dynamic imports with a literal source and TS import types, matched like `no-restricted-imports` matches named ones (options `{ patterns: [{ regex, message }] }`).

### [`tools/eslint/simSide.ts`](../tools/eslint/simSide.ts)

- `SIM_SIDE` (const): Sim-side code: reproducible and renderer-free (PLAN.md §3, "Terms used throughout").
- `simPlugin` (const): The plugin the sim-side blocks use: core's restriction rules as `sim/<rule>`.
- `simSideBlocks` (function): The sim-side blocks: globals, properties and syntax over all sim-side files, then imports (core/math.ts last).

### [`tools/eslint/testing.ts`](../tools/eslint/testing.ts)

- `ALL_ON` (const): Every switch on: the rules written ahead of their code are tested now.
- `Case` (interface): One rule proved both ways.
- `caseProblems` (function): What is wrong with a case's result: its failing source must trip its rule, its passing source lint clean.
- `CaseResult` (interface): A case and the messages ESLint gave its two sources.
- `ConfigModule` (interface): What eslint.config.js exports.
- `describeMessages` (const): One line per message, for readable assertion failures.
- `lintCases` (function): Lints every case's failing and passing source and pairs the results, in the order given.
- `lintFixtures` (function): Lints `files` (repository path → source, each given a file comment) and returns each path's messages.
- `loadConfigModule` (function): Imports the repository's eslint.config.js.
- `Switches` (interface): eslint.config.js's switches.
- `uncovered` (function): The configured messages (from `messages`) that no failing fixture produced.

### [`tools/game/files.mjs`](../tools/game/files.mjs)

- `declaredPatches` (function): The engine files ENGINE-FEEDBACK.md lists under "Local engine patches", outside comments.
- `ENGINE_DIRS` (const): The engine's folders in a game: a file there that the lock does not name was added by the game.
- `ENGINE_REPOSITORY` (const): Where the engine lives on GitHub: what a game's lock names and `x engine --update` clones.
- `engineIdentity` (function): The engine's identity: its repository, commit and commit date, and whether the checkout had changes.
- `engineNpm` (function): The entries of each of `NPM_FIELDS` a game gets from the engine's package.json: all its scripts but `e2e`, since no browser specs ship, and all its dependencies, devDependencies and allowScripts.
- `FEEDBACK_FILE` (const): Where a game writes what it needed from the engine, and declares the engine files it patched.
- `gameLockfile` (function): The engine's package-lock.json for a game named `name`: the same tree, the root renamed.
- `gamePackage` (function): A game's package.json: the engine's pins and scripts.
- `hashFile` (function): A file's SHA-256, as the lock writes it.
- `hashText` (function): A text's or a buffer's SHA-256, as the lock writes it.
- `LOCK_FILE` (const): The lock a game keeps at its root: the engine's commit and every engine file's hash.
- `LOCK_FORMAT` (const): The lock's format.
- `lockFor` (function): The lock for the engine files of `items` (hashed from the source), with the engine's identity, the package.json entries the game got from it, and the root files written from its templates (`templates`: path → hash or null).
- `NPM_FIELDS` (const): The package.json fields a game shares with the engine: the engine's entries in each, the game's own beside them.
- `npmClashes` (function): The game's own package.json entries (in `previous`, not named by `before`, its lock's `npm`) that the engine's package.json sets otherwise, as `field.key`: what an update would replace.
- `npmLost` (function): The entries of `previous` (a game's package.json) that `next` (what an update writes) drops, or sets back to the engine's where the game had edited one the engine gave (`before`, its lock's `npm`), as `field.key`: what an update names, since the engine's entries win.
- `ownerOf` (function): Whose a source path is: 'engine', 'game' (the starter) or 'skip'; null when no rule names it.
- `plan` (function): What a game gets from `source`: each file to copy, from its source path to its path in the game, and whose it is.
- `RENAMED` (const): Engine files a game gets under another path: the engine's license travels with its code.
- `RULES` (const): Which source files a game gets, and as whose: the first rule whose `test` matches a path decides (`ownerOf`).
- `sameDependencies` (function): Whether a game's dependencies are exactly the engine's, so the engine's lockfile fits it.
- `SOURCE` (const): This checkout's root: two levels above this file.
- `sourceFiles` (function): The source's files, as git tracks or would track them (or, in an archive, every file), sorted, with `/`.
- `STARTER` (const): The starter game: copied into a new game, then the game's own.
- `verifyGame` (function): Compares a game's engine files with its lock: those changed, those missing, files the game added in the engine's folders, and the patches it declares; `undeclared` is every one of the first three that the game does not declare.

### [`tools/game/new-game.mjs`](../tools/game/new-game.mjs)

- `createGame` (function): Makes a game in `target` from the engine at `source`; on a clash it throws, having written nothing.
- `gameLockfile` (re-export): (undocumented)
- `gameName` (function): A game's name: an npm package name, from the folder's name by default (`Dragon Run!` → `dragon-run`).
- `gamePackage` (re-export): (undocumented)
- `main` (function): The command line; returns the exit code.
- `npmClashes` (re-export): (undocumented)
- `render` (function): Fills a template's `{{name}}` and `{{engine.*}}`; any other placeholder is an error.
- `TEMPLATES` (const): The game's root files: template (in tools/game/template/) → where it goes.
- `updateGame` (function): Moves the game in `target` to the engine at `source`; returns what changed.

### [`tools/lib/browser.ts`](../tools/lib/browser.ts)

- `AdapterRecord` (interface): One adapter WebGPU returned: its identity and features.
- `browserRuntime` (function): The browser part of a report's runtime: `153.0.8010.12` → `chromium153`.
- `cachedChromium` (function): Where scripts/setup.sh keeps Chrome for Testing `CHROMIUM_VERSION` on a machine without `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM`.
- `CHROMIUM_VERSION` (const): The platform's Chromium release (tools/deps.json), which scripts/setup.sh fetches where the container's is absent.
- `chromiumPath` (function): The Chromium executable: `$CHROMIUM_PATH`; else `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM` when it exists; else `cachedChromium()` when it exists (a machine outside the container, after scripts/setup.sh); else `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM`, so the launch error names the platform's path.
- `ConsoleRecord` (interface): One console message the page printed.
- `DEFAULT_CHROMIUM` (const): The container's Chromium (153 since 2026-10-22); `$CHROMIUM_PATH` overrides it.
- `describePageError` (function): One line for a page error: its message and where it was thrown (`tests/pages/harness.ts:12:9`).
- `GpuLog` (interface): What WebGPU really did in the page, counted by the probe: `window.__gpu`.
- `initScript` (function): The init script for `page.addInitScript`: the virtual clock seeded with `seed`, then the WebGPU probe.
- `launchBrowser` (function): Launches the platform's Chromium with WebGPU, for `x` commands that open pages.
- `launchOptions` (function): Playwright's launch options for WebGPU on this platform, shared by `playwright.config.ts` and the `x` commands.
- `mapPageError` (function): Maps one uncaught page error to its source frames.
- `mapStack` (function): Maps every frame of a browser stack to its source through the served modules' inline source maps.
- `PageError` (interface): A page error with its stack mapped to sources; `file`, `line` and `column` are its first repository frame.
- `PageWatch` (interface): What `preparePage` collects while the page runs.
- `parseStack` (function): Splits a V8 stack into its frames' function names, URLs and 1-based positions.
- `preparePage` (function): Prepares a page before it loads anything: installs the init script (virtual clock seeded with `seed`, seeded `Math.random` and named streams, the WebGPU probe) and starts collecting console messages and mapped page errors.
- `servedPath` (function): The repository-relative path of a URL the dev server serves (`/@fs/…` included), or the URL itself.
- `SourceFrame` (interface): One frame of a stack, at its source position when a source map gave one.
- `VIEWPORT` (const): The viewport every harness page gets.
- `VirtualClock` (interface): The page's virtual clock and seeded streams, installed as `window.__clock`.
- `WEBGPU_FLAGS` (const): Shardfall's WebGPU flags (PLAN.md §8.8): SwiftShader through Vulkan, presenting to the page's own canvas.

### [`tools/lib/ciShards.ts`](../tools/lib/ciShards.ts)

- `E2eReport` (interface): The parts of Playwright's JSON report it reads: each suite's file and its tests' results' durations (ms).
- `E2eSuite` (interface): A suite of a Playwright JSON report, as far as `minutesFromReports` reads it.
- `minutesFromReports` (function): Each spec file's minutes over `reports` (the shards'), to a tenth, by name.
- `minutesOf` (const): What `spec` weighs in `table`.
- `planShards` (function): Deals `specs` out to `total` machines by their minutes (see the file comment); each machine's files by name.
- `readT2Minutes` (function): The table under `root`; empty when there is none.
- `SPEC_DIR` (const): Where the spec files are (playwright.config.ts's `testDir`).
- `specFiles` (function): The spec files under `root`, by name.
- `T2_MINUTES` (const): The table of T2's minutes a spec file on the workflow's runner, under the root (a baseline: tests/baselines/).
- `T2Minutes` (interface): The table: which run measured it, the first machine's other steps, and each spec file's minutes.
- `UNMEASURED_MINUTES` (const): What a spec file the table does not list weighs, until a full run measures it.
- `writeMinutes` (function): Rewrites the T2 minutes table under `root` from full-run reports (`paths`, Playwright's JSON), keeping its steps.

### [`tools/lib/ciStatus.ts`](../tools/lib/ciStatus.ts)

- `mainStatus` (function): How main's last full run went, for `x ci --status`: fails only when the last finished run did not pass.
- `readRuns` (const): The real reader: GitHub's API through curl, 15 s at most.
- `repoSlug` (function): `owner/repo` from a GitHub remote URL (https, ssh, or a git proxy's `…/git/owner/repo`), else undefined.
- `RunsReader` (type): Reads the workflow's runs on main for `slug` (`owner/repo`), newest first; rejects when GitHub cannot be asked.
- `WORKFLOW` (const): The workflow whose runs are read.
- `WorkflowRun` (interface): One run of the workflow, as GitHub's API gives it: the fields read here.

### [`tools/lib/ciSummary.ts`](../tools/lib/ciSummary.ts)

- `CI_OUT` (const): Where `x ci --local` writes, relative to the root.
- `renderSummary` (function): The run as Markdown, for `out/ci/summary.md` (and the GitHub workflow's step summary).
- `toResult` (function): The run as the dispatcher's result: the timing table, the T2 note and one finding per problem.

### [`tools/lib/deps.ts`](../tools/lib/deps.ts)

- `compareVersions` (function): Orders two versions: negative when `a` is older.
- `DepsRecord` (interface): `tools/deps.json`.
- `evenLines` (const): Node's releases on even lines only: odd lines never get LTS and are skipped (§6.10, rule 6).
- `firstOfNextLine` (const): The first release of a later line than `version`'s.
- `gitBlob` (const): The git blob id of `bytes`, as `git hash-object` prints it.
- `isDay` (const): Whether `value` is a `YYYY-MM-DD` day.
- `isRelease` (const): Whether `value` is a `{ version, date }` release.
- `Knowledge` (interface): A pinned document that follows a pin's line; `blob` is the git blob of its text after the header comment.
- `lineName` (function): A line's name, for messages and `knowledge`: `3.x`, `0.182.x`, `0.0.4`.
- `lineOf` (function): A version's line, as its lowest version: 3.2.7 → 3.0.0, 0.182.1 → 0.182.0, 0.0.4 → 0.0.4.
- `LockEntry` (interface): One lockfile entry: a package's version and what it depends on (the root entry also lists dev dependencies).
- `Lockfile` (interface): The parts of package-lock.json (v3) the tools read.
- `lookup` (const): Finds a record by name in any section; `node` and `chromium` are the platform's.
- `newestInLine` (const): The newest release of `version`'s line.
- `newestQualified` (const): The newest release that is 12 months old on `day`.
- `NextLine` (interface): The next line's first release, and the day it qualifies.
- `parseVersion` (function): Parses a stable release `x.y.z` (no prerelease), else undefined.
- `PinRecord` (interface): One package's record in `tools/deps.json`.
- `qualifiesOn` (function): The day a release published on `date` turns 12 months old (a 29 February release: 1 March).
